News.title: Jude Bellingham hails Harry Kane as ‘best England player to have worn the shirt’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Jude Bellingham has described England captain Harry Kane as “the best player to have worn the shirt” after he produced another sterling performance on a historic night.

Kane equalled Peter Shilton’s record for the most appearances for the Three Lions when he was named in the starting line-up for the Nations League game against the Czech Republic on Tuesday night.

As he so often is Kane was the lynchpin of the England team at Wembley, scoring a brace and registering an assist, the latter as Vladimir Coufal poked his cross into his own net, on his 125th cap.

Afterwards his teammate Bellingham and manager were quick to lavish praise on the striker.

Bellingham told ITV: “I can only talk from my perspective and first and foremost he is an unbelievable human being. As a captain, as a man, he looks after every single person. He's the one to take responsibility off the pitch.

“And on the pitch he's the best England player to have worn the shirt. It's an honour to play with him.

“He's playing at a level that is unmatched. He's scoring goals for fun, he's dropping deep and playing passes in behind and contributing, making tackles and everything. He's only getting better.”

Manager Thomas Tuchel, when asked to comment on Kane’s performance, replied with a smile: “It's what he does. I don’t take it for granted.

“He is just exceptional every single match. It’s difficult to find words for him.”

Kane was substituted late on to a standing ovation from the Wembley crowd and replaced by Leeds forward Dominic Calvert-Lewin as England saw out a routine 3-0 win.

The result follows a 2-0 win in the reverse fixture in Prague as well as a 7-0 demolition job of Croatia away to leave Tuchel’s side second in Group A3, behind World Cup winners Spain, who inflicted a 3-2 defeat on England in the opening game of this international window.

Tuesday night’s win leaves England only needing to avoid an 8-0 defeat to Croatia at home in the November international break in order to seal their spot in the Nations League quarter-finals in March, with Spain having already secured their berth.

News.title: CNN now has a new owner. What will the future of the network be under Skydance?
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

CNN has a new owner: Skydance.

After a tumultuous, roughly yearlong process, Skydance-owned Paramount closed its $81 billion buyout of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday. And beyond Hollywood, the mega merger brings two titans of the American TV news landscape — CBS and CNN — under the same roof.

On the eve of the deal's completion, Skydance confirmed that CNN's Mark Thompson will stay on as editor-in-chief of the network — separate from CBS, where Bari Weiss remains at the helm. But how the combined company's news operations will look farther down the road is yet to be seen.

Politics are also top of mind. The billionaire family of Skydance CEO David Ellison has a cozy relationship with President Donald Trump — who has been far from shy about targeting coverage he deems unfavorable from both CNN and CBS. Last month, his administration moved to bar CNN from the White House. And the network's new ownership arrives as coverage ramps up less than a month ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

Ellison has pledged to maintain editorial independence. Under a recent settlement with states that challenged the merger, the company agreed to establish new monitoring of CBS and CNN by forming a “News Editorial Independence Board” within 180 days of completing its Warner acquisition.

Still, Skydance's corporate leaders are to choose who sits on this board. Critics are bracing for potentially deepening editorial turmoil — and warn of consequences of industry consolidation overall.

CNN's editor-in-chief remains in top spot

Skydance announced on Monday that Thompson — who has been CNN's chair and CEO since 2023 — would continue to lead the network. In a memo to staff published by Business Insider and other outlets, Thompson said he had “real confidence” Ellison and other Skydance leaders “will fully support the principle and practice of the kind of independent news that CNN has always stood for.”

Thompson, a former chief executive of the BBC and The New York Times, acknowledged that some details of how CNN will operate have yet to be finalized — but said he planned to lead the network “as an independent Editor-in-Chief with the same responsibilities and prerogatives that I have now.”

Paramount-owned CBS News and its hallmark “60 Minutes” program have already seen editorial turmoil since coming under Skydance ownership last year. For critics of those changes, news of Thompson staying at CNN marked a meaningful safeguard — but some experts cautioned that time will tell.

“Both CNN and CBS News will ultimately sit under the same corporate ownership, and ownership can exert influence in ways that are much more subtle than directly telling an editor what stories to cover," said J. Christopher Hamilton, an associate professor at Syracuse University. Decisions about everything from budgets to personnel "can gradually affect the editorial character of a news organization.”

The long-term question “is whether that independence remains intact when it becomes costly or uncomfortable for the parent company,” he added.

Charles Schreger, an adjunct professor at NYU's Leonard N. Stern School of Business, expects Thompson not to be influenced by politics — and said that he doesn't think Skydance would keep the executive on if the company didn't "have the intention of letting him operate (CNN) in a neutral way.”

New editorial monitoring

According to court documents, the new editorial independence body will include five “active or retired” journalists with at least 10 years of experience.

Still, those members will be appointed by and report to the combined company's board of directors. Ellison is remaining chairman of what is now the combined Skydance.

“While it is termed independent, it is going to be filled with members appointed by Paramount,” said Megan Duncan, an associate professor of journalism at Virginia Tech's School of Communication. She predicts that will “lessen the teeth of this board."

The settlement outlines some additional criteria for board members, including that no more than two members be affiliated with the same political party, and that no government employees be appointed to the board or have oversight over who is on it.

According to court documents, the board's responsibilities include establishing a set of “guiding editorial principles” based on CBS and CNN's standards and practices, resolving “any disputes” between both employees at the two networks and corporate management and “monitoring adherence to ethical journalism.”

Members are to serve for terms of three years, although the board of the combined Paramount-Warner can still remove them for cause.

‘Disappointed that we could not do more’

Top state prosecutors like California Attorney General Rob Bonta — who led the coalition of 12 states that initially sought to block the Paramount-Warner merger — said when announcing the deal on Sept. 21 that the board will help “ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting at CBS News and CNN."

Still, others wished the settlement could've gone further, including Connecticut Attorney General William Tong, who wanted a full divestiture of CNN and CBS and said he was “deeply disappointed that we could not do more.”

Meanwhile, while joining the rest of the states in the wider settlement, Colorado and Washington notably declined to sign off on the proposed editorial board terms.

As part of a separate settlement with Hollywood writers, the Writers Guild of America said that Paramount had also agreed to prohibit writer layoffs at CBS News Broadcast for the next five years.

Ellison, meanwhile, previously promised that editorial independence “will absolutely be maintained” under Paramount ownership.

“It’s maintained at CBS. It’ll be maintained at CNN,” Ellison told CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” in March, while noting that his company wants to speak to “the 70%” of viewers who he said identify as center-left or center-right. And in an August op-ed published by the New York Times amid the height of Paramount's antitrust battle with 12 states, he reiterated that “our journalists will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve — not to any party or cause.”

Trump and CNN

Last month, Trump barred CNN — as well as Politico and MS NOW — from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage and “fake news.” All three outlets have since filed a joint lawsuit, and are continuing to fight their case in court.

CNN has long attracted ire from the Republican president, and members of his administration have also made their opinions clear about the network's future ownership. Shortly after Trump joined Israel to launch the war against Iran earlier this year, for example, the White House attacked CNN for its coverage — and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told reporters that “the sooner David Ellison takes over that network, the better.”

CBS has faced its own attacks from Trump. Skydance’s 2025 acquisition of Paramount was approved by the Federal Communications Commission just weeks after the company agreed to pay Trump $16 million to settle a lawsuit over editing at the network's “60 Minutes” program.

____

AP Reporter Laurie Kellman in London contributed.

News.title: Trump reveals why tariff is only his ‘fifth favorite word’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump went on a largely aimless rant to a group of Navy midshipmen and a handful of members of the armed forces’ top brass on Tuesday as he announced the construction of a new submarine shipyard in Baltimore, Maryland.

The president spoke Tuesday afternoon in front of a combat vessel at Sparrows Point, Maryland, where he announced that defense contractor Anduril would build the facility to support the construction of the Navy’s new autonomous submarine craft. But the point of his visit was once again obscured by an unfocused diatribe about the war in Iran, the U.S. strike on Venezuela, and the tariff policies his administration has used to reshape global trade frameworks.

Trump repeated a refrain about tariffs becoming his “fifth” favorite word, after others such as “wife” and “God”, to a mostly silent batch of bored Navy undergrads who came up from the Naval Academy in Annapolis to stand and hear the president talk.

“We're building more car plants than we ever have in history,” the president told his audience. “It's all because of my favorite word, my fourth favorite, maybe my fifth-- tariff. Without tariffs, we wouldn't be doing that.”

”The word tariff for us was has made us a rich country again, and rich in a lot of ways,” Trump added.

This is a developing story.

News.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor ‘accuses police of taking personal items’ during searches of his home
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has accused Thames Valley Police of taking personal items during searches of his home, it has been reported.

It comes as the former Duke of York takes legal action against the force.

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor, who is launching a bid to quash search warrants which led to his arrest, instructed lawyers after discovering officers had allegedly removed “private and confidential material unconnected to the criminal investigation”, according to the Telegraph.

He was arrested on his 66th birthday earlier this year on suspicion of misconduct in public office following allegations he shared sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein during his time as the UK’s trade envoy.

The King stripped his brother of both his right to be a prince and his dukedom late last year over his association with the convicted sex offender.

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor has been granted permission to challenge whether Thames Valley Police acted lawfully over the searches relating to his arrest in February.

A judge at the Old Bailey issued warrants which allowed police to raid Mr Mountbatten-Windsor’s residence on the Sandringham estate and his former Windsor home, Royal Lodge.

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor has been granted permission to challenge whether Thames Valley Police acted lawfully over the searches relating to his arrest in February ( PA )

On Monday, a judicial spokesperson confirmed a private hearing in Mr Mountbatten-Windsor’s legal claim is due to take place at 2pm on Thursday at the High Court, before Mr Justice Hilliard.

On the same day, it emerged that Mr Mountbatten-Windsor was warned not to use the King’s private money to fund his legal action.

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor receives an annual stipend – the amount of which has not been disclosed – provided by King Charles from his private funds, but a Palace source said it has been made clear that these monies should not be used to fund the judicial review.

The source added Mr Mountbatten-Windsor’s legal defence was a matter for him and his lawyers, and that Buckingham Palace has no role in determining its strategy or actions.

The clarification from the Palace source will be seen as an attempt by the King to distance himself from the legal proceedings.

When Andrew was arrested on February 19, the monarch issued a written statement, insisting “the law must take its course”.

Mr Mountbatten-Windsor and Thames Valley Police have been contacted for comment.

News.title: Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones briefly split after 13 years of marriage — why a separation can save some couples
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

When couples get married, they vow to stick together through the good, the bad and the ugly. But what happens if they can’t work through a rocky patch together, and need to work on themselves instead?

Michael Douglas has shed light on his several months-long split from his wife, Catherine Zeta-Jones, in his new memoir One Helluva Ride. The pair had been married for 13 years when they separated briefly in 2013 — around the time he told a newspaper his cancer had been caused by HPV he’d contracted through oral sex. Zeta-Jones was reportedly upset by his admission at the time, and he later said he regretted causing her embarrassment.

The Welsh actress had said in a statement the couple was “taking some time apart to evaluate and work on their marriage,” and they reunited a few months later. Asked how he rekindled the flame in a new interview with The Sunday Times, Douglas replied: “What, I won her back? It was a mutual … You know, we had our problems but I love her dearly and, 25 years, you know.” It seems to have worked out: they will celebrate their 26th wedding anniversary this November.

They are not the only Hollywood couple to take time apart to figure things out before coming back to one another. Ben Stiller and his wife Christine Taylor split in 2017 after 17 years of marriage but rekindled their relationship during the pandemic; Sylvester Stallone and Jennifer Flavin went back on their 2022 divorce announcement and said they were “extremely happy”; Kristen Bell and Dax Shepard came back from a breakup when they first started dating; Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel split in 2011 but wed a year later. There are others to add to that list: Gabrielle Union and Dwayne Wade; Pink and Carey Hart; Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor famously married twice.

When couples get married, they’re meant to work through tumultuous times, for better or worse. But if a couple is struggling — with communication, trust or a lack of spark — does staying together at all costs actually help, or can some time apart give partners the space to hit a hard reset?

open image in gallery Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones had been married for 13 years when they separated briefly in 2013. They rekindled their relationship months later ( Getty Images for The Hollywood R )

Taking a break in any type of relationship can be extremely beneficial, says Dr. Eli Kraiem, couples and relationship expert and adjunct professor at Ferkauf Graduate School in New York City. A split could be for a multitude of reasons — a break of trust due to infidelity, financial problems, poor communication or a lack of intimacy — but Kraiem says a brief separation could be an opportunity for both partners to step away and ask themselves a simple question: Do I really want to be with this person?

“A brief split could be really helpful because it gives each partner the space to reflect on the negative patterns that they got stuck in,” says Kraiem. “A break can help us kind of rediscover who we are, what we want, what our values are, what our true feelings are. It's also an opportunity to make an intentional decision about choosing your partner again.” Kraiem adds that deciding to pick a partner again can be extremely powerful and romantic.

“It creates a lot of hope to see your partner show up differently, or see yourself show up like that. It might be, ‘Wow, I didn’t know we were capable of this,’” he continues. But the relationship can’t go on as it previously was, of course. “The couple must choose to be different people, for the relationship to be different and to work on things that weren’t right in the past,” he says.

The therapist says he doesn’t prescribe rules to his clients when they take time apart, but he says the less contact, the better. “It’s so that you don't get engulfed by the relationship, even if you're physically apart, because you need to have the emotional space to process without feeling stuck in the relationship,” he says.

open image in gallery Ben Stiller and his wife Christine Taylor split in 2017 after 17 years of marriage but salvaged their marriage during the pandemic ( AFP via Getty Images )

Anna Elton, a Florida-based couples therapist and author of The Formula of Desire, does offer some loose rules for her clients who take relationship breaks. She says that 30 days could be the magic number for taking time apart and advises on minimum contact. “It gives you a chance to calm your nervous system down so you are not impulsive, and that you’re able to think clearly,” she says. “It’s an opportunity to step back and analyze the whole situation, the relationship and your thinking.”

Elton says she asks couples three things: “Why did you like the person?; Why did you commit to the person? And why are you still trying to make it work?”

The break needs to be significant so that you’re not reentering into exactly the same relationship that made you unhappy in the first place. She says that couples need to figure out what needs to change before they rekindle, so that they have a clear roadmap. “If nothing changes, you’ll just reenter the same scenario.”

“That honeymoon period of missing each other will be over very quickly,” she says. “After two weeks max, you will be back in the same cycle again.”

Elton’s 30-day break advice has no scientific research to back it up, but many of her clients try it. What Elton says matters more is how much work is actually done during the separation.

open image in gallery Sylvester Stallone and Jennifer Flavin went back on their 2022 divorce announcement and stayed together. They have been married for 29 years ( Getty Images )

“Are both people reflecting on why the relationship stopped working?” she says. “Are they changing the patterns that led to the split? And when they reconnect, are they coming back because something has actually changed, or simply because they miss one another?”

There are, of course, times when a relationship should not be salvaged. If microcheating, infidelity and more serious issues, like domestic abuse, have occurred, then there may be a point of no return (each relationship is different and would be judged by a therapist on a case-by-case basis). Couples who repeatedly break up and reconcile without resolving underlying issues may not reap the benefits of a fresh slate. A break can only work if both parties are intentional.

During an interview with The McBride Rewind podcast, Christine Taylor reflected on reconciling with Ben Stiller during the lockdown after four years apart, saying that the changes and pressures that came in adult life made them grow apart. “I met Ben when I was 28 years old … you have different chapters and stages in your life, and I feel that’s also true for adults and particularly women,” she said. “You get married, become a mom, for those who become mothers … career, put your career on hold, all those different chapters, and I think at that moment in time for us, we were just not on the same page with a lot of things.”

It was a similar story for Gabrielle Union and Dwyane Wade, who broke up in 2013 after dating for four years, got back together and were married one year later. “We kind of took a step back. We supported each other, but we took a step back for a little while,” Wade said on The Tonight Show. “At the end of day, we came back together and said, ‘Listen, we want to continue this. We want to try to continue to get better each day,’” he said.

As for Douglas and Zeta-Jones, who have a 25-year age gap, the Basic Instinct actor seems to think the reconciliation paid off.

“I never gave up hope that we would reconcile,” he wrote in his new memoir.

He told The Sunday Times: “We’re in good shape. It’s all I can say.”

News.title: Harry Kane scores twice as he equals England cap record in win over Czechs
News.content:
The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments that the rest of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more tonight to take him to 91, which means that there are only 12 other England players in history who have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France almost four years ago, so, yes, some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

News.title: UK not prepared for food shortages, experts warn
News.content:
Britain has no way to feed its population of 66 million people in a crisis, a letter addressed to the Prime Minister has warned.

Climate change, cyber-attacks, geopolitical shifts, and energy shocks could put Britain’s food supply at great risk – and the UK is “complacent”, the letter says.

The document was delivered to Andy Burnham on Monday and was signed by 180 experts including academics, farmers, local council leaders, and foodbank workers.

Britain’s food supply is now heavily globalised, with roughly 45-50 per cent of food imported from countries like Spain, the Netherlands and France, as well as South Africa, Columbia and Brazil.

The system provides a cheap and constant supply of food – seasonal or not – but if international supply chains are disrupted, the UK’s home production is “woefully inadequate in [being able to produce] many different food types” , the letter argues.

It adds that “international food supplies can be weaponised”.

Crucially, the UK operates a ‘just-in-time’ food system – meaning hardly any food is stocked and stored in reserves, but is constantly moving from farms and ports directly to supermarket and wholesale shelves when needed.

“When you go to a supermarket and check out, you think, well, ‘it’s adding up the bill’ – it is, but what it’s also doing is reordering,” Tim Lang, emeritus professor of food policy at City University, a signatory of the letter and author of the Just in Case report – a major review that analysed the UK’s food system for the National Preparedness Commission, previously told The Telegraph.

News.title: Kenya confirms first ever case of Ebola after man dies in Nairobi
News.content:
Kenya confirmed its first ever case of Ebola on Tuesday after a Kenyan citizen who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo died in Nairobi.

Kenya is the third country to record a case linked to the Ebola epidemic in eastern Congo, the second largest on record. Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths earlier in the year but was declared Ebola-free in August.

The patient had been ill for about a month before travelling ‌by road ‌from Congo to ⁠Uganda’s capital, Kampala, and then flying to Nairobi on Saturday, health minister Aden Duale told a news conference.

After arriving at Nairobi’s international airport, he passed through health screening and was later taken by a relative to Nairobi ⁠Hospital. He was admitted with fever, chills and bleeding beneath the skin and was quickly placed in isolation, Duale said.

He died late on Monday.

News.title: Tories promise to scrap Labour’s mansion tax
News.content:
The Tories have pledged to scrap Labour’s “mansion tax” on homes worth more than £2m.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, pledged to abolish the “vindictive levy” in his keynote speech to the Conservative Party conference, warning it would hit people living in “ordinary homes”.

Under the tax, which was announced by Labour last year, properties valued at more than £2m face an extra levy on their council tax from 2028.

The shadow chancellor said: “They pretend it’s a mansion tax, but it will hit people here in Birmingham, in Manchester, and those living in ordinary homes making long commutes to our capital city. For many, it will be simply unaffordable.”

He pledged to follow in the footsteps of Nigel Lawson, Margaret Thatcher’s chancellor, and cut one tax at every Budget if the his party returns to power.

Elsewhere in his speech, Mr Griffith promised to scrap a net zero “grocery tax” which pushes up the cost of the weekly shop and cut the cost of a new build by £50,000.

The shadow chancellor also accused previous Tory leaders of failing to govern as free market conservatives, and said Andy Burnham and John Healey want to take Britain back to a “socialist fever dream of the 1970s”.

News.title: How worried should we be about the Russian plague lab leak?
News.content:
A fire breaks out at a laboratory in Siberia where secretive research into infectious diseases is taking place. A technician, racked with guilt over the accident, disappears into the tundra and shoots himself. Hunters discover his body, but what they don’t realise is it is infected with a manipulated version of the plague bacterium. The pathogen quickly spreads around the world, wreaking death and destruction at a scale unprecedented in human history.

This is the plot of Biological War: A Scenario, a recent book by US author Annie Jacobsen which imagines what could happen if a weaponised bacterium escaped from a laboratory.

The book describes an absolute worst-case scenario but the beginnings of this fictionalised pandemic share an eerie similarity with events in Russia over the last week. Reports have emerged about the death of a 28 year old female worker at the Antiplague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Shelekho, a city in Irkutsk. Rospotrebnadzor, the country’s infectious disease agency, said the woman was diagnosed with a “pneumonia of unknown origin”.

However, according to reports in Russian media the woman, identified as Daria Shipilova, died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube filled with live samples of the pathogen, Yersinia pestis. She was taken to hospital on Tuesday September 29 but died two days later. Nearly 200 contacts are now being monitored for signs of the disease, according to media reports.

So how worried should we be?

News.title: Extreme heat is increasing risks for pregnant women and babies, experts warn
News.content:
Soaring temperatures are increasing birth complications and defects in newborns, a new report has warned.

The report, which surveyed 1,000 doctors and midwives, found that at least 73 per cent of healthcare workers across Australia, Brazil, Britain, India and Zimbabwe had seen an uptick in heat-related complications in pregnancy and birth.

High temperatures can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can significantly decrease blood flow to the placenta and reduce oxygen and nutrients reaching the foetus.

This phenomenon can increase the risk of stillbirth, premature births, and low birth weight, the report, released by the Wellcome Trust, said.

Heat can also make it hard for newborn babies, whose bodies are already extremely fragile, to regulate their internal temperatures – which can significantly impact both their ability to breathe properly and feed from their mothers.

Extreme heat can also severely affect the health of a pregnant woman, placing heavy demands on the cardiovascular system and inadvertently increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The effects are more severe on women who live in places where temperatures are newly or rapidly increasing, as opposed to women who have always lived in hot climates and whose bodies have acclimatised to the heat over time.

Insufferable heat can also impact women’s access to critical healthcare during pregnancy.

More than a quarter of healthcare workers surveyed by Wellcome said they had seen first-hand how fewer women travel to hospitals and clinics during heat waves, particularly in the developing world where millions access healthcare on foot.

The world experienced its hottest August on record in 2026, when the average global surface air temperature reached 16.96 degrees Celsius – roughly 1.65 degrees above pre-industrial levels.

Britain also saw its hottest summer since records began, with five heatwaves recorded over the course of just 40 days, and temperatures reaching 38 degrees in some parts of the country.

A Wellcome-funded project studying pregnant women in Wales, known as MAGENTA, has found that women in the UK have experienced negative birth outcomes as a result of the persistent heat.

Initial research has linked exposure to elevated temperatures exceeding 25 degrees with higher rates of premature births and stillbirths. A 1-degree increase in heat exposure can boost the chances of a preterm birth by around 5 per cent, the research found.

Climate change has been identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as the greatest threat to global public health.

Between 2030 and 2050, experts project climate change will cause an additional 250,000 deaths every year.

The deaths will be due mostly to heat stress, malnutrition, and an increase in the prevalence of infectious diseases like malaria, which is spreading into new areas where mosquitoes can now more easily survive and spread disease, according to the WHO.

Dr Madeline Thomson, head of climate impacts and adaptation at Wellcome, said: “Extreme heat, fuelled by climate change, is impacting our way of life and our health - and yet many countries are not prepared. With El Niño pushing temperatures higher, the failure to act is costing lives.

“We already know many of the solutions to protect people - from early warning systems to cooler buildings.

“But the challenge is providing solutions to those who need them most, including pregnant women and newborns, who face serious risks but often receive inadequate information and support.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: ‘The dogs were eating their bodies’: Thousands of Yemenis flee war across the sea
News.content:
The Houthi militiamen had barely chased the government forces out of Alia Mohammad’s coastal village when the bombing began in a Saudi-backed attempt to recapture it.

Caught in the middle were Ms Mohammad, her family and their neighbours near the town of Dhubab, overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait, or ‘Gate of Tears’.

As the roar of planes split the sky over their heads and explosions shook their village, it took little time for them to decide what to do.

Born from generations of fishermen, they resolved to take to the sea and flee their homes in Yemen, to seek refuge across the strait in Djibouti.

More than 4,000 Yemeni refugees have arrived in the coastal Djibouti town of Obock in the past month, fleeing an offensive which has redrawn Yemen’s battle lines and strengthened Tehran’s hand in the Middle East energy crisis.

The offensive last month saw the Iranian-backed Houthi advance around 90 miles along the Red Sea coast in a 48-hour blitz that delivered what analysts have called the most consequential shift in Yemen’s front lines in years.

Sports.title: Eberechi Eze makes Anthony Gordon look even more undroppable as Arsenal star struggles to seize England chance
Sports.content:
Next

EBERECHI EZE had the chance to put some pressure on Anthony Gordon – but ended up making the man of the moment look even more undroppable.

Barcelona winger Gordon is in the form of his life having caused carnage in the other three England games during this elongated international break.



The electric wideman was bench here, though, presumably to manage his load in a game that turned out to be the routine victory many expected.

In his place came Eze, a man who Thomas Tuchel has shown more faith in than most players during his tenure.



Indeed, the Arsenal star has been called to every single one of Tuchel’s squads since the German took charge.

His start here meant the 28-year-old has featured in 16 of the 26 games the ex-Chelsea boss has presided over for our country.

Yet his performance was OK at best here and certainly would have not had Gordon sweating over his place.

While the plethora of other talents queueing up to be Tuchel’s back-up left-winger will have not been left disheartened.

Eze did not do anything wrong, as such. He worked hard and kept England’s shape well enough, even filling in in central midfield late on.

But his display down the left wing had none of the dynamism that Gordon produced to put the fear of God into Croatia in Rijeka on Saturday.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Granted, Eze does not have Gordon’s rapid pace. They are very different kinds of players.

He is an inventive playmaker though, capable of moments of ingenuity, as proven by his time at Crystal Palace, even if we have seen it less regularly at Arsenal.

A technician who has it in his locker to play the kind of first-time cross Morgan Rogers fired in for Harry Kane’s first here, or the clever swivel Gunners team-mate Myles Lewis-Skelly pulled off to have the crowd oohing and aahing early into the second half.

Eze offered a brief hint of his flair with a tasty little dribble round two players around the hour mark, and a late dribble into the box which failed to win a penalty.



His inability to stretch teams like Gordon meant England were far less dangerous than they have been of late.

Gordon also has a strong understanding with left-back Lewis Hall from their years together at Newcastle, which, understandably, Eze could not emulate.

Eze was involved in the opening goal of what proved to be the easy win many expected.



But, if anything, he should have actually done better in the move.

Kane had fired in a cross which Eze ought to have strained every sinew to get on the end of but instead eased up.

Unaware he was under no pressure from Eze at all, ex-West Ham full-back Vladimir Coufal comically fired into his own net.

Eze looked at his best in a central area, rather than out wide, late on when the Czechs were tiring.

Tuchel loves him for his ability, attitude and versatility.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Remember, the Gunners man is yet to start a Premier League game this season and still there was almost no doubt he would be in this squad.

But with an embarrassment of riches we have in reserve for the attacking trio behind Kane, including Morgan Gibbs-White, Rio Ngumoha and Cole Palmer, it does not seem unreasonable to expect a little more from Eze to justify his spot as a squad undroppable.

Sports.title: England 3 Czechia 0: Kane marks record-equalling night with classy double to all but seal Nations League quarter-final
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE marked his record-equalling night with a brilliant cross for ex-West Ham defender Vladimir Coufal to score with an equally impressive finish, albeit accidentally.

Yet the England captain was never going to let one of the proudest nights of his career drift by without scoring at least once.



Just 13 minutes after that first half own goal, Kane struck for the 90th time in international football, casually dispatching the ball into the corner from close range.

It was so obvious that he was going to score, manager Thomas Tuchel, did not even bother getting off his seat and just applauded over the top of his head.



Yet like London buses, one Kane goal is normally followed by another. His 91st goal was courtesy of a clever header and he hung in the air for so long it felt as though he was being lifted up by a cable from the Wembley roof.

And in the 82nd minute every fan inside the stadium – although a few had sneaked off early – got off their seat to give the captain a standing ovation when he was replaced by Dominic Calvert-Lewin.



This straightforward win also completed a decent four-game Nations League spell for Tuchel, who started this international break under pressure following the result against Argentina at the World Cup.

Although the 3-2 defeat to Spain illustrated England’s strengths up front and weakness at the back, a couple of solid results over the Czechs and spectacular demolition of Croatia has helped put a positive spin on England life less than three months after the World Cup.

Jude Bellingham played well but was still quiet by the ridiculously-high standards he has produced recently, but it is just good to see him enjoying playing for England.

He is being touted as potentially being the best player in the World Cup, but here was another reminder that he has a hell of a lot of work to do just to catch up with his superstar team-mate Kane.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Kane is in the conversation for England’s greatest ever player, although until he actually wins something the obvious argument is that Bobby Charlton and Bobby Moore are ahead.

Yet the nation’s record goalscorer, aged 33, will rewrite history – again – when he picks up cap No126 against Croatia at Wembley on November 12, a game which unusually for England, will be on a Thursday.

The Czechs were less of a threat than a week ago when they caused a few problems until Pavel Sulc was sent off.

Trent Alexander-Arnold, who started for the first time in two years last week, was back at right-back after missing out against Croatia and saw a free-kick turned away by Lukas Hornicek, although it was not going in.



With England lacking ideas, Coufal helped out by turning Kane’s cross past bewildered-looking Newcastle keeper Hornicek.

In his five years in east London, Coufal did not strike at the correct end but he did score two own goals, both against Manchester City.

Kane’s cross from the right was put into a dangerous area but even so, Coufal only played the ball because he wrongly assumed that Eberechi Eze would try and get a touch.

Yet Eze just gave up, which may not please Tuchel, meaning Coufal could have let keeper Hornicek deal with the cross.



The odds for Kane scoring would not have been very generous and sure enough, he had an easy chance when the Czechs, inexplicably, left him unmarked.

Kane was not finished there, obviously, as his appetite for goals never diminishes, as shown by his 73 goals for club and country last season which means he is in the running for winning the Ballon d’Or this month.

The former Tottenham striker fired a shot against the top of the bar following a move which started with some lovely individual skill from Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Yet not long after, he got his double by leaping above Jin Slama to meet Lewis Hall’s cross, although keeper Hornicek should have done better.



Kane now returns to Germany to play for Bayern against Augsburg on Saturday although the one he will be looking forward to is a home Champions League game against Arsenal on October 21.

And we all know what happens when Kane faces Arsenal. David Raya will have his work cut out if he wants to keep a clean sheet.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And then a few weeks later, Kane will be back in London to face Croatia in what will be a special night for someone who has grown into a true leader on and off the pitch.

Will Kane score in that one? It is just a case of how many.

Sports.title: England ratings: Harry Kane has hand in all three goals as Morgan Rogers injects new threat into Three Lions’ attack
Sports.content:
Next

HARRY KANE crowned his record-equalling 125th England cap with a brilliant double as England cruised past Czechia at Wembley.

The Three Lions barely put a six-point buffer on their spot in second place in the Nations League Group 3 with a simple 3-0 victory.



Kane equalled Peter Shilton’s record for the most caps in England history and cemented his legacy as one of the nation’s best ever players by continuing his exceptional scoring record.

The Bayern Munich striker netted twice as well as being the cause of the opener when he forced Vladimir Coufal to blast into the back of his own net with a dangerous cross.



Thomas Tuchel will have been watching without a worry as England barely got out of second gear and picked up all three points.

Here’s how SunSport football reporter Joshua Hall rated each individual England performance.



JORDAN PICKFORD – 6

With Tuchel testing out James Trafford, Pickford will know he has more pressure on him than he has in a long time.

He does not look comfortable with the ball at his feet and had a few shaky moments, but ultimately navigated the game without any mistakes – as he always does.

TRENT ALEXANDER-ARNOLD – 7

There is always a conversation about whether Alexander-Arnold’s attacking threat is negated by his defensive frailties and that was on show early on.

The Real Madrid ace forced a tipped save onto the post from Lukas Homicek with a whipped free-kick, but then caused a sloppy turnover with loose pass a few moments to give Alex Kral a free shot.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It seems as if that conversation around his game will never go away, but this was ultimately a positive performance.

JARELL QUANSAH – 7

After playing right-back against Croatia, Quansah was back in the centre of defence as he showed his versatility at the back.

A solid performance from the Bayer Leverkusen man, filling Ezri Konsa‘s gap without any hiccups.



MARC GUEHI – 7

The Manchester City man was dominant in the air at times, dealing with Czechia’s swinging crosses really well.

He and Quansah looked cool, calm and collected whenever the opposition tried to threaten.

LEWIS HALL – 7

There is something admirable about the tenacity and desire Hall shows to try and win every single loose ball that comes anywhere near him.

His lofty delivery to find Harry Kane from a corner ij the second half was unconventional , but effective.



ELLIOT ANDERSON – 7

Could and should have scored when he blasted the ball over the ball from just six yards out in the first half.

However, he atoned for his errors with a delightful first-time chipped pass to find Morgan Rogers and set up Kane’s 90th England goal.

His floated pass was akin to pitching wedge on a golf course – delightful.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 7

It is remarkable to think that Lewis-Skelly has only played a handful of senior football matches in central midfield and is already starting for England in the position.

Although this performance was nothing spectacular, it was a reminder that he can be a solid option despite being just 20 years old.

A particularly nice moment when he shrugged off three Czechia players with one Cruyff turn in the second half.

JUDE BELLINGHAM – 7

It was always going to be hard to replicate the phenomenal performance Bellingham put in last time out, but this was still impressive.

The Real Madrid superstar was running circles round the Czechia midfield at times and busting a gut to be involved in every England attack.



His brilliant floated ball to the back post to set up a golden opportunity for Morgan Rogers, who fluffed the chance by trying to play the ball back across the face of goal.

EBERECHI EZE – 6

Other than big moments in the occasional game, it is hard to remember when Eze put in a standout performance for England.

The Three Lions missed Anthony Gordon‘s blistering pace and willingness to make runs in behind.

Eze could have had a goal in the first half when Vladimir Coufal blasted the ball into his own net, but held his run and was nowhere near getting to Kane’s cross.



MORGAN ROGERS – 8

A strong performance from the Chelsea man who made a mess of a few chances, but ultimately came up with the good when it mattered.

His first-time pass across the face of goal to set up Kane was exactly what was needed to inject some threat into England’s attack.



HARRY KANE – 9

A record-equalling 125th cap for Kane, who is undoubtably one of the greatest England players of all time.

It was his hard work that helped open the scoring when his whipped cross from the right flank that was inexplicably turned into the net by Czechia’s Vladimir Coufal.

He crowned his special night with a 90th and 91st goal for England when he turned home Rogers cross in the first half and powered in Lewis Hall‘s corner in the second spell.

SUBSTITUTES

JARRAD BRANTHWAITE (for Guehi, 63rd min) – 6

Looked comfortable when he came on and can be a great option for Tuchel.

JAMES GARNER (for Anderson, 63rd min) – 6

Had to slot in at left back late on, but did a good job.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo admits he signed off on EIGHT-POINT statement for Jorge Jesus to read in press conference
Sports.content:
“As I promised, I decided to recount, in the first person and directly, the circumstances surrounding the last training camp of the National Team. After the 2026 World Cup I prepared a letter to the Portuguese people, which I still keep, with the words I want to address to them when I leave our team for good.

“At the end of the competition, already on the flight back from the United States, the President of the Federation asked and insisted that I reconsider the decision to leave, because the FPF wanted me to continue.

“Right afterwards he asked me for my opinion on the name of the current head coach, which he was considering alongside other names he did not reveal to me. I told the President of the Federation that, in my opinion, it would be the right choice.

“That is why, on the day the current head coach was presented, I was genuinely happy with the choice. It was the right option, as the results are confirming. A few days later I received a first contact from the new national team coach saying he would like to meet me in person. I said yes and we scheduled it for the end of my holidays.

“We met at the Cidade do Futebol, where my club was holding its pre-season training camp. That day the coach told me he was counting on me and that my presence was fundamental to his project.

“He presented me, right there, with a plan for my participation. He told me I would play the first match and the last one, and that for reasons of physical management he would always make three to four changes per match.

“At that point he raised the possibility of me not travelling with the national team to Norway and Denmark. He proposed that I play the first match and stay in Portugal, then rejoin before the match at the Dragão. I refused this proposal immediately.

“It seemed obvious to me that I could not accept it. It was not because I would not play the matches abroad that I would stop captaining our team. That privilege of staying in Portugal would not be a good example. The coach ended up agreeing with my analysis.

“This conversation was attended by Simão Coutinho, sporting director of Al Nassr, the person to whom the current coach reported throughout last season and one of those responsible for his signing by the club in 2025. On the eve of the start of the camp the coach came to my house in Lisbon, at his request, for another conversation with me. The conversation was calm and all the principles agreed in August were maintained.

“I played the match at Alvalade and, although substituted, I made no problem of it. I put the armband on Bruno Fernandes myself, far from imagining that I might be taking my last steps as a player and captain of the National Team.

“What mattered to me that day was our victory. Winning is always good; in Portugal and for my country, even better. At lunchtime on the day of the match in Norway, an assistant to the coach came to the table where the group was having lunch and informed me that the coach wanted to speak to me.

“To my absolute surprise, the coach asked me if I was fit to play 30 minutes. I was fully focused on my physical recovery, integrated with my teammates as always, and thinking that I would not play that day. Without any problem.

“This request was something outside my physical recovery and training plan — because I was only going to play on the 4th at the Dragão — but of course I said yes. He replied that I should then be ready because I would play 30 minutes.

“The rest everyone knows. I warmed up from half-time, watched the minutes go by, and was not called.

“The coach had broken his word to me.”

“The coach had broken his word to me. At the end of the match I only wanted everything to finish with the victory and to be alone. I did not go to greet the fans. A failing that is solely my responsibility and that should not have happened.

“I apologise to the Portuguese who supported us intensely there, I apologise to the fans, and I apologise to those who, without being Portuguese, may have travelled there to see me and whom I may have disappointed. Forty-eight hours later we had a conversation — myself, the coach and Simão Coutinho — since he had been the one accompanying our conversations in August.

“It was a deep moment, very frank, without any kind of filter. We agreed that there was only one way to close this “case”: that the coach repeat what he had just told me in private, in the presence of Simão Coutinho, but in the press room. What was agreed was simple: the coach would begin the press conference with this subject, seeking to close the matter by telling the truth.

“He would say that I never asked to play any minutes, that it was the coach and no one else who proposed the plan for this camp to me, and that it was a mistake to put me on to warm up and then not bring me on, and that if it happened again he would not do it.

“We ended that meeting with the coach asking me for a hug, promising me that he would say at the conference what he had just said to me, and that the matter would be overcome. I would not play in Denmark and I would play the match at the Dragão.

“All of this in the presence of Simão Coutinho, always. At the coach’s request, a meeting then took place between himself, Simão Coutinho and Tiago Craveiro by videoconference, in which what we had discussed was summarised. A short document was produced which I myself validated and which, with my knowledge, was delivered to the coach, as he had requested.

“The conference was what is known: the posture had nothing to do with our meeting; I heard expressions and an aggressiveness that I do not believe I deserved, an attitude of ‘I want, I can and I command’ that he never showed me, not even remotely, in private the day before.

“The notes I validated were the following: I think it is important, also because it is the truth, to clarify a few things before talking about Denmark.

“1. I myself, and no one else, proposed to Cristiano a plan for him this sporting season with the National Team. It was a long and very good conversation.

“2. I know how much he lives and loves the national team and the weight he has in the world, and even more the weight and the positive influence he has had on the national team for 24 consecutive years.

“3. The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted.

“4. He never questioned my options. He was exemplary, loyal and professional.

“5. The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.

“6. I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pelé or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game. If it were today I would not do it.

“7. To close the subject: I want Cristiano in the National Team. In fact I do not want him a little, I want him a lot. Fortunately he also believes in me. He believed at Al Nassr and he does here as well.

“8. About not greeting the fans. We have already spoken about that. Someone who has played more than 230 matches for the national team does not receive lessons from me on love for Portugal. It was a moment of frustration that erases nothing.

“He is the player who gives the most autographs, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let us not invent problems where they do not exist.

“When we are not happy we react. That was all. None of these notes, therefore, said that the coach should even apologise to me. It was the second time he had broken his word to me.

“I decided to leave the camp without waiting for any further breach of word. For me the truth is still the most important thing in the relationship between people.

“However much it hurts, let them tell me the truth. In fact, in a conversation I had with the President of the FPF and with the coach on the morning of the day of that press conference — they can certainly confirm this — I reaffirmed that if they did not want me there they should tell me. It was enough for them to be frank with me.

“I would accept that and I promised that we would prepare something beautiful, as I dream will happen, and no one would be left angry. I remember it as if it were today. They replied in unison that no. That my place was in the National Team.

“Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career.

“I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.

“I also owe an apology to my national team teammates for having left the camp. Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it.

“The responsibility is exclusively mine. I apologise to the Portuguese people once again, but the breaking of one’s word has, for me, a defining impact. I felt that, from that point on, my remaining would only harm the working group, and I did what I have always said I would do if I did not feel useful: I packed my bags and left.

“The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors. I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor.

“I have already apologised, but I know that attitudes must have consequences. Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.

“On this subject, I have heard a great deal of talk about farewell matches, that I must have a dignified farewell and that the Federation wants to give me that opportunity.

“I learned in life, often hungry and with nothing to eat, that no one gives anything to anyone. I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that.

“But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing. That is what I thought on the day I was given the news of my father’s death. I was at a camp with our national team and I decided to stay there until the end of the match the following day. I did for the country what I would never do for any club.

“Therefore, if I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team.

“This is, believe me, the purest of truths. Cristiano Ronaldo”.

Sports.title: ‘Stupid’ Portugal star sent off for two yellows in 3 SECONDS despite Man City ace running length of pitch to stop him
Sports.content:
Next

RUBEN DIAS tried his best, but he could not stop his Portugal team-mate from seeing red against Norway on Sunday.

Francisco Conceicao was handed two yellow cards in the space of three seconds in the dying embers of the Nations League clash.



Portugal led 2-1 at the time and were attempting to see the game out before the Juventus winger clashed with the referee.

Dias sprinted over to try and stop his team-mate from doing anything silly – but it seems his best attempts did not work.



Conceicao then stuck his thumb up at the referee just as he was administering the yellow card.

That enraged the official who quickly followed up the yellow with another, resulting in one of the fastest red cards from two yellows you’ll ever see.



Conceicao threw his hands out by his side in disbelief after receiving his marching orders, but luckily his country held on for a 2-1 win.

It has been a trying spell for Portugal after Cristiano Ronaldo withdrew from the camp on the grounds he was an unused sub.

It was the first time in Ronaldo‘s long, glorious career that he was an unused sub for his country and the striker is believed to have been told he would be getting the last 30 minutes of their first encounter with Norway in this international break.

Manager Jorge Jesus neglected the chance to bring him on and held on for a 2-1 away win.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ronaldo held showdown talks with Jesus and the Portuguese FA and then decided to leave the camp.

Since then, Portugal have won both of their games without the iconic 41-year-old forward.

However, Ronaldo released a statement on Tuesday evening explaining that two broken promises from Jesus had led him to his course of action.

It remains to be seen if the former Manchester United and Real Madrid star will be offered the chance to add to his 234 caps and 146 goals for his country.



As for Dias, he will now return to Man City where the club is in nothing short of turmoil.

Enzo Maresca will address his troops ahead of the weekend for the first time since it emerged the club has been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges against them for financial breaches.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reveals he’s already written retirement letter as he speaks out after Portugal bust-up
Sports.content:
Next

CRISTIANO RONALDO has revealed he has already written a retirement letter as he issued an apology after leaving the Portugal camp.

The icon’s 1,996-word apology was released on Tuesday night as he outlined what had happened, the fact he’s already prepped for retirement and that he ought to be punished.

He said: “The consequence of this act of mine must be assessed and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation. I understand that the punishment should have no mitigating factors.

“I am not just any player; I am team captain, and that constitutes an aggravating factor. I have already apologised, but I know that attitudes must have consequences.

“Anyone who is in football as I am knows that, regardless of each person’s status, the rules are the same for everyone.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Ronaldo also took the time to apologise to his team-mates and the Portuguese fans: “I also owe an apology to my national team team-mates for having left the camp.

“Despite the absolute breach of trust in the coach’s word, as those who witnessed these conversations can attest, I should not have done it.

“The responsibility is exclusively mine.

“I apologise to the Portuguese people once again.”

Sports.title: Simon Jordan fumes Premier League needs to be DISBANDED after Man City scandal exposed need for ‘whole new set of rules’
Sports.content:
Next

SIMON JORDAN has sensationally called for the DISBANDING of the Premier League as we know it following the bombshell verdict in Manchester City’s financial scandal.

City were last month found GUILTY of over 100 breaches of Prem financial regulations during a nine-season period.



It was revealed that the Etihad club, who have officially APPEALED the verdict, hid over £900MILLION in “sham” deals from 2009 to 2018.

The Prem’s Financial Fair Play rules were introduced to stop clubs from spending above their means and preventing rich owners from injecting exorbitant amounts of cash to buy their way to glory.



But talkSPORT host Jordan believes they’re no longer fit for purpose, saying: “My overriding argument is, you have made this league so fabulously successful, you’ve made it the most investable league in the world, you’ve made that success off the back of that, and you’ve turned the tap off.

“And you’ve turned it off, for what reason? Because there’s this mythical idea that everyone is going to go bust unless you control it.



“Now, if you want to control things, you can do redistributions.

“Really, the only way to evolve this game is to disband the Premier League, recreate it with a whole new set of rules that are fit for purpose rather than tacking on rules that have existed for 125 years and keep trying to finesse them to meet ownership models that are so much more sophisticated now.”

City, unless they win their appeal, will receive the biggest sanctions in Premier League history for their repeated breaches – including the possibility of having the titles they won during the period taken away from them.

Jordan, however, doesn’t see the benefit of scrubbing City’s achievements from the history books, asking: “What does that achieve? They’ve been slaughtered.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

What are Man City charged with? THE Premier League claim Man City hid £900m in 'sham' deals across a nine-year period. They were found guilty on 114 of the initial 115 charges – with the number now up to 130 charges – which fit into six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

“Do you think the idea that Abu Dhabi’s sole focus in life is to own an English, beautiful, shiny football club that’s now been built into a wonderful machine in the City Football Group, has now been diminished and damaged beyond all reparations?

“And you look at it and say Abu Dhabi are going to come away from this with any currency, even if they buy the Premier League out and turn around and say, ‘We’ll give you £1billion in compensation and every club can have a double dip of £50m each.

“They’re never going to get out from underneath.”

Despite not seeing the merits of stripping of City of the three titles they won during their period of breaches, Jordan agrees wholeheartedly with the notion that an incredibly harsh deterrent needs to be set.

He said: I don’t think it’s pointless. I just don’t know what it achieves.



“It’s about what we do now going forward.”

Sports.title: ITV pundits Roy Keane and Ian Wright forced to run off mid-coverage before England vs Czechia clash at Wembley
Sports.content:
Next

ROY KEANE and Ian Wright were forced to flee their position by the side of the Wembley pitch to avoid getting soaked live on ITV.

The Manchester United and Arsenal icons were working for the broadcaster during England‘s clash against the Czech Republic.



But while live on air, presenter Mark Pougatch was the first to notice a sprinkler was not going to bypass them.

While Three Lions stars warmed up on the pitch behind them, Pougatch was heard saying: “Be careful Wrighty you might be getting a shower.”



Keane, 55, and Wright, 62, then looked behind themselves and saw the sprinkler in full flow moving towards them.

Wright was heard saying: “Oh mate,” while former football hardman Keane didn’t fancy getting his suit wet and quickly shifted out of the way.



The trio managed to avoid the worst of it and had a laugh about it afterwards.

They had better luck than some of their compatriots in 2014.

Then presenter Adrian Chiles was appearing on ITV with Lee Dixon, Glenn Hoddle and the evergreen Wright when the quartet were doused with water as sprinklers turned on before an England Euro 2016 qualifier against Switzerland.

That game happened away in St Jakob Park, with the Three Lions winning 2-0 thanks to a Danny Welbeck double.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

It was a special occasion at Wembley with captain Harry Kane drawing level with Peter Shilton for the record of most England caps, tonight being No125 for the 33-year-old.

He even got on the scoresheet as he doubled the hosts’ lead shortly before the break before he grabbed another on the stroke of the hour as he headed home a Lewis Hall cross to make it 3-0.

Sports.title: King Kane marks milestone match with star display as England beat Czech Republic
Sports.content:
Harry Kane marked his record-equalling 125th cap with a sensational display as he led England to a 3-0 win over Czech Republic at Wembley.

The England captain's century and a quarter of caps is now level with Peter Shilton's all-time record that stood for 36 years - and it was a fitting display as he was involved in every single goal on the night.

Kane set up the first - his versatility to peel off to the right wing was rewarded as his cross was comically put into his own net by Czech defender Vladimir Coufal. Wembley almost unanimously laughed at the former West Ham man as the replays were shown on screen.

Image: Harry Kane doubled the lead before half-time

And Kane's moment came five minutes before half-time, as a sumptuous move involving Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers resulted in the latter crossing for his captain - who had all the time and space to finish.

It wouldn't be long until Kane sought to double his tally after the break. He struck the bar from distance but he eventually made it three when he headed Lewis Hall's delivery into the bottom corner at the far post.

Thomas Tuchel's England end the lengthy international break with three wins from four and 14 goals to show for it. Even though Spain beat Croatia 2-1 with a late comeback win to lead the group, England are all-but assured of a quarter-final spot anyway - needing one point from their last two games to qualify.

But this was Kane's night. No hat-trick for him as he was taken off with 10 minutes left - but he's now passed the 90-mark for international goals. He wants a century of goals to add to his appearance - and he's definitely going to get it.

Image: Harry Kane doubled the lead before half-time

More to follow.

The big moments from Wembley

5: CLOSE! Alexander-Arnold whips a free-kick over the Czech wall and it's tipped away by Hornicek.

27: OWN GOAL! Kane's cross is put into his own net comically by Coufal, who was under no pressure as he tried to clear.

30: OVER! Anderson misses a great chance to double England's lead but blazes over.

40: GOAL! Kane gets the goal on his big night as Anderson chips the ball over for Rogers down the right, who finds the England captain with acres of space to smash home.

54: OFF THE BAR! Kane is denied a second as his effort from the edge of the box clips the bar after great work from Myles Lewis-Skelly to start the free-flowing attack.

56: NEARLY! Rogers crosses for Bellingham whose deft flick is smartly denied by goalkeeper Hornicek.

57: GOAL! Kane heads in Hall's corner to double his tally on England's special night.

81: KANE OFF! The England captain is substituted for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, getting a standing ovation from Wembley. It won't be his last.

Tuchel's first post-World Cup camp assessed

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at Wembley:

This is Harry Kane's night, no doubt about it. But has Thomas Tuchel earned back a few more fans after this lengthy international camp?

Fourteen goals in four games against decent opposition. Croatia, Spain and Czech Republic are major tournament regulars.

There's a bit more clarity in certain England positions. Alexander-Arnold and Hall have had very good camps - when so many questioned whether they were right for this level. When was the last time England had two fixed, natural right-backs?

Jude Bellingham looks up for it and all the headlines are him are positive again. Anderson, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Alex Scott have added depth to midfield.

And Kane keeps on doing the business. This set-up is built for him to thrive in. Are England back?

Sports.title: Who are the winners and losers of England's international break?
Sports.content:
It's been a long international break for England. But it could be a pivotal one in Thomas Tuchel's thinking.

England's four-game Nations League camp started with a defeat to Spain but ended with two wins over Czech Republic and a 7-0 demolition of Croatia.

But after countless withdrawals and changes to the squad, who is feeling more confident about their England squad status - and who is starting to look over their shoulder?

Here are the winners and losers of the latest England squad...

Winners

Anthony Gordon

Image: Anthony Gordon looks reborn after his move to Barcelona

It turns out that Anthony 'Barcelona' Gordon is a thing after all. For so long, England's left wing position was left open to debate. Nobody really claimed it as their own, even at the World Cup just gone.

Now the debate is over. That spot is Gordon's for as long as he stays fit and firing.

Three goals and one assist during this international break means the 25-year-old is at the peak of his powers. That form is even more surprising given he is yet to get off the mark for Barcelona this term.

Image: Do England have the best front four in the world?

Alex Scott

Image: Alex Scott looked the part when he started the 7-0 win over Croatia

It seems slightly odd to claim this international break a success for someone who has suffered a two-month injury during it. But Alex Scott is here to stay.

In the 7-0 win over Croatia, Scott showed he belonged at that level, playing the Declan Rice role to perfection.

His understanding with Elliot Anderson also shone through. That will be crucial for him going forward, given the pair were the midfield pivot for the most recent Euros-winning England U21 team.

It has worked for England at a major tournament before, it can work in the future. Scott's emergence has given Tuchel a real rotation option in that role.

James Trafford

Image: James Trafford was given a shock start against Spain

Tuchel's first post-World Cup team selection had one major talking point. For the first time in nearly a decade, England played a big game without Jordan Pickford in goal.

Was the decision to start James Trafford in goal against Spain the first sign of a changing of the guard in the England goal? Never before has an England goalkeeper had this big an opening to usurp Pickford.

After Trafford started the Spain and the Czech Republic games, Pickford returned to Tuchel's line-up for the last two internationals. The No 1 shirt is not Trafford's, but the fact this role is now somewhat shared is a huge plus for the Leeds 'keeper.

Lewis Hall

Do England finally have a left-back?

Part of the Three Lions' recent spike in form at left wing has a lot to do with Lewis Hall's form down that flank. After so many tournaments of inverted options and waiting for Luke Shaw to be fit again, England have a natural option on that side again.

The Newcastle defender deserved the assist for Kane's second goal against Czech Republic at Wembley. England look balanced on that side again, and if Hall can stay fit then the head coach has one less thing to worry about.

Trent Alexander-Arnold

So it turns out Trent Alexander-Arnold can play at right-back for England.

Two starts against the Czech Republic have got people talking about the much-maligned Real Madrid man in a more positive light again.

Alexander-Arnold looks back to his best, showing his creativity in Prague but the way he stretched Czech Republic at Wembley was also impressive.

He can play behind Bukayo Saka and impress. He can do the same with Morgan Rogers and also impress. Is this the camp where Alexander-Arnold's international career turned a corner?

And no, we haven't forgotten Harry Kane

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England head coach Thomas Tuchel says he can't find any more words of praise for Harry Kane, with the England captain set to equal Peter Shilton's all-time appearance record.

This wasn't a standout camp from the England captain, but it's not gone unnoticed how Harry Kane just keeps on winning in an England shirt.

That's 91 goals in 125 England caps now. He has scored in nine out of his 14 matches for England in 2026.

But delivering in every game has become normal for him now. Just give him the Ballon d'Or.

Losers

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo

Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among the first players to pull out of this England squad. Their withdrawals came not even 24 hours after they played most of the 1-1 draw with Fulham.

Is there a way back for either of the Manchester United players?

Not only is their form at United under scrutiny, but others have stepped up in their absence. For Rashford, Gordon has now pulled clear of the United man in terms of the left-wing battle. And with Morgan Rogers and Eberechi Eze among Tuchel's favourites, is there still a spot in the squad for Rashford?

For Mainoo, the performance of Scott against Croatia risks putting the United midfielder further down Tuchel's pecking order.

He was already pretty low on that list after a minute-less World Cup, with the likes of James Garner and Morgan Gibbs-White putting further pressure on both he and Rashford.

You wonder if either Rashford or Mainoo regret pulling out of this England picture so swiftly.

Cole Palmer

Image: Cole Palmer has only played in two of eight England camps under Thomas Tuchel

Chelsea's Cole Palmer was another player who pulled out of this England set-up early, with load management deemed to be the reason for his withdrawal.

But this international break has proven that Palmer is no closer to breaking the attacking midfield mould that Tuchel has in Jude Bellingham and Rogers.

Bellingham scored or created four out of the seven goals for England against Croatia. He remains untouchable in this team as a world beater. Rogers also scored in that game and is another Tuchel favourite.

After getting back to some form with Chelsea, this was a perfect window for Palmer to muscle his way back in. But he seems further back than ever in Tuchel's plans.

Reece James

Image: Could Reece James lose his England spot to Trent Alexander-Arnold?

Reece James started out as England's first-choice right-back. When he was fit, he started, no questions. But has he ended up much further down the right-back pecking order now?

Alexander-Arnold's displays at right-back during this England camp have brought him back into the right-back equation. That spells trouble for James' starting hopes for England.

And after Jarell Quansah impressed against Croatia, England's right-back situation is becoming crowded. Could James be the one to make way from Alexander-Arnold's form?

Why Tuchel is both a winner and a loser from this camp

This was always going to be a sticky camp for the England head coach, who came into the Nations League campaign needing to earn trust and confidence back after those substitutions against Argentina.

Because of that, this was branded a 'lose-lose' for Tuchel. Any standout win and people will question where that performance was in the World Cup semi-final. Any defeat would have sparked more doubts about his credentials and potential at this level.

There are still concerns about Tuchel's England. His confession that England are still a "danger" to themselves while in possession of the ball echoed his controversial 'DNA' comments from the summer. The Three Lions still feel a long way off Spain's level where they are efficient in both boxes at the same time against the very best.

But the 7-0 win over Croatia - which caught everyone by surprise - has breathed fresh momentum into the Tuchel England era. That would have got the world of football talking.

There's also a bit more clarity in certain positions. England have two natural full-backs again, the left wing position is sorted. Players like Rice and Saka can be managed more with adequate replacements such as Lewis-Skelly, Scott and Rogers.

After clarity though, must come consistency. Tuchel has picked these players - they must stay there. Only that creates cohesion ahead of Euro 2028.

Are England back?

Sports.title: Ronaldo breaks silence over Portugal walkout in extraordinary statement
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has broken his silence over his Portugal walkout in a lengthy statement in which he declares himself available for the national team.

The 41-year-old, whose actions had raised doubts over his international future, also accused Portugal's new head coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises in a 1,996-word statement to his 679m Instagram followers.

Addressing the uncertainty over his Portugal future, the Al Nassr forward said: "If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team."
