Sports.title: How FIA software bug caused chaos in Bahrain GP in Malaysia – and the emergency fix that saved the race
Sports.content:
The start of the first wet-weather race of the 2026 Formula 1 season descended into chaos. Leader Max Verstappen was the first to suffer from a lack of power while driving slowly during the formation laps behind the safety car, after which Lewis Hamilton came to a standstill and several other cars followed.

Race control was forced to stop the formation lap with a red flag, after which there was a 40-minute delay before fans actually got to see some F1 action.

Read Also: Formula 1 FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis confirmed to media including Autosport that a bug in the software supplied by the FIA and developed together with the teams over the course of multiple years was responsible for the chaos.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked because there's been very little wet running this year. There was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said during an impromptu media session post-race.

“Basically, on the formation lap, some cars went very slowly and almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars and some cars almost stopped completely. That bug prevented then the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again.”

This is closely related to the reduction in electrical power to 250kW in wet conditions.

Although the software required for this was tested by several teams, including Red Bull and Racing Bulls, it was not tested in the conditions behind the safety car – and therefore not at these extremely low speeds.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

At the Sepang International Circuit, those low speeds were reached in certain minisectors, with all the consequences that followed.

“It was mainly in some sectors where the full power was reduced. I don't know exactly what speed that was, but some cars reaching this very low speed somehow entered into a loop, which meant they couldn't re-accelerate and then it looked as if they came to a stop.”

In practice, this left drivers feeling as though the throttle pedal was no longer responding, something Oliver Bearman told the media with some surprise.

“I've never seen or felt anything like that. I was shocked that… I didn't even know that the FIA could control our throttle pedal. That was quite scary, actually,” the Haas driver said.

“My throttle pedal just stopped working. It was like it was not connected and the engine was just idling. It was so weird, I mean, shocking.”

One of the questions is why the internal combustion engine was also affected, when that should not be the case at extremely low speeds. The FIA does not yet have a formal answer to that question, but the initial suggestion is that the bug caused all throttle input to go towards recharging the MGU-K, which explains why drivers felt there was no response from the throttle pedal at all.

At first glance, it appeared as though the Mercedes-powered cars were less affected by the issue than other manufacturers, but Tombazis explained that there is no technical reason for that. It was simply related to the speeds reached in certain minisectors.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Not all cars reached the same low speeds on the formation lap. There was a bit of a concertina effect. I think Max slowed down quite a lot, being at the front, and then some cars braked harder as they were surprised and so on. That caused some cars to experience the problem and some others to not experience it.”

How the FIA provided F1 teams with an emergency fix

The FIA then had to react quickly to get the race near Kuala Lumpur under way after all, as Tombazis explained when asked by Autosport.

“Fortunately, our guys understood the issue very, very quickly. I think the update was done very competently. It was obviously a rush job. The priority was to get running as quickly as possible again, so I think the reaction time was quite fast,” he said.

“It wasn't a perfect job and, clearly, we didn't test the updates, but I think it was the way to handle such a case.”

In practice, the update meant that the FIA lifted the energy limit constraint – the restrictions associated with the 250kW limit – for the minisectors in which the low speeds had triggered the bug. Logically, this is not a watertight solution going forward, but it was an emergency measure to ensure the race could go ahead.

“In some of the sectors, some of these reductions of power were overridden,” Tombazis confirmed. “Clearly, we didn't have five days to do the updates. We only had a few minutes, but fortunately, I think we managed to do it without compromising any safety, any racing or fairness.”

How could this happen in the first place?

After the FIA update, all the teams still had to install the modified software, which explains the delay before the restart. The Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was saved as a result, but that still does not explain how the FIA could have missed this issue throughout all its preparations and why it only surfaced in round 16 of the championship.

“The software was tested. It just wasn't tested in those specific conditions,” Tombazis replied. “What caught us out was the fact that cars went in that very, very low speed, which was not normally contemplated.”

FIA Safety Car Photo by: Rudy Carezzevoli / Getty Images

During the tyre tests in which the software was tested, the extremely low speeds were understandably not reached. Nevertheless, there is a crucial counterargument to that: in the rain, the likelihood of a safety car – and therefore low speeds – is very high. Should the FIA not have anticipated that, and was that the governing body’s biggest mistake?

Asked that question by Autosport, Tombazis responded: “Well, any bug is a product of a mistake. I don't know of any software that doesn't have bugs and updates. Your computer probably gets updated every three days and those are all bugs.

“Of course, anticipating these things is what one hopes to do, but sometimes some very combination of events isn't properly anticipated and causes the problem. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Although the cause of this problem is now known and a temporary fix has been introduced, the FIA still has many questions to answer internally – also to ensure that it does not happen again.

“We would all like it to be simpler, but the fact is when you have as much electrical energy, it does make it more complicated. I think you appreciate that the race has now finished about one hour ago and we haven't done a full debrief of the situation to see how we can avoid such an issue.

“Every race, we have a long debrief afterwards where we identify criticalities. Obviously, that was a major criticality and we need to make sure we avoid it.

“But can I guarantee it will never happen again? This specific problem, yes. A problem, no. But we will do our best to avoid it, of course.”

Sports.title: The slick tyre gamble that hurt McLaren and Ferrari's chances in Bahrain GP in Malaysia
Sports.content:
When the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia eventually got going after an hour and 33 minutes of delays, it became apparent that the intermediate was the tyre to be on among the opening laps - even if the Sepang circuit had looked like it was drying out.

At the front of the field, Ferrari and McLaren chose to go all-in on the dry tyres for the restart; Ferrari opted for the soft compound, while McLaren went for the mediums. When the race got underway behind the safety car, both teams were left to rue their choices as the circuit was still too slippery.

McLaren bailed on the plan early, stopping before the standing start to ensure Oscar Piastri could get a set of intermediates back onto the car, but Lando Norris and the Ferraris stuck with their choices. Charles Leclerc duly fed into the pitlane at the end of the lap, as the slick-tyre runners were swamped and then left behind by those who'd stuck with the intermediate for the start.

Lewis Hamilton and Norris surmised that, since they'd made their beds, they'd lie in them. Hamilton was asked if he wanted to stop again, but the seven-time champion reasoned that Ferrari might as well stick with the gamble given that the team was well behind - and pitting would only cost more time.

By the end of the eighth lap, the slick times were now equal with the intermediate runners; Valtteri Bottas' subsequent off then presented the inter-shod drivers with the chance to switch to slicks.

Speaking about the decision, Norris stated that the idea of starting on the slick was "quite convincing" and that he was unsure of the performance of the inter; on his recon lap to the grid, the Briton reported that the green-walled tyre was already feeling the pain on Sepang's rough surface.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

"It felt maybe a little bit of a risk, because a slick on a wet track is always a bit of a risk," Norris said. "There was enough people on it that it was quite convincing at the time that it was possibly going to be the right decision.

"The laps to the grid on the inter when it was a similar kind of condition, they had so much grip and my Inter was completely shredded after one lap.

"I was convinced a slick tyre would work, but I think it was just the fact I've never really been on the inter before. Things just felt a lot better than they should have done in a way.

"If we would have had a read on an inter from a previous weekend, maybe I would have been able to understand it more. But that convinced us and it clearly convinced a lot of people.

"Oscar probably made the right decision in boxing and we got it wrong today, that's all."

Leclerc theorised that the roughness of the tarmac made it more difficult to read the track surface, as water pooled up in the gaps - and the drop in temperature that accompanied the rain ensured that the circuit took much longer to dry out than expected. Given the length of the downpour, any residual circuit temperature was swiftly extinguished.

Even though the Monegasque switched tyres, the time loss involved in pitting after the start kept him behind Hamilton, who ran longer on his set of soft tyres and quickly began to make up positions.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Carlos Sainz, Williams Photo by: Joe Portlock / Getty Images

Hamilton joked that he wasn't going to "go to the casino with the guys" after the team's gambles didn't pay off, although praised his team's strategy in keeping him out on the road. The Briton was ultimately less enamoured with the medium after making a stop on lap 31, but the late-race VSC (later a full safety car) presented a chance to return to the soft - which he put to use with a pass on Isack Hadjar for third.

"As we pulled out [of the pits], all the spray came out the back of Max’s car and I was like, 'okay, I’m done. My race is really in trouble,'" Hamilton recounted.

"We just had to stick with it. As everyone’s overtaken me, they [the engineers] were like, 'we stop.' I know we’ve already made another 26 seconds. What’s the difference from that with one minute 40 or whatever I was down? So I was just, 'Let’s just wait it out for the track to dry.'

"And once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great then after that. Really good pitstops from my guys in the garage and then good strategy. But for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case. Of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here.

"We’ll definitely have an open dialogue, and I’m really so proud of my team. The mechanics every weekend, just the work they’re putting in, the engineers that accompany here every weekend, the catering, everyone really, really comes and gives it their best.

"Their heart’s all in the right spot. We’ve definitely got areas that we need to improve and we know that, and we’re not in any denial of that. So I think we’ll have a constructive chat, we’ll regroup, we’ll take the positives from this weekend, which the car was really good, and we’ll come back next week fighting."

Read Also: Formula 1 FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay

Sports.title: FIA explains software glitch that caused Bahrain GP in Malaysia race delay
Sports.content:
The FIA has given insight into why Formula 1 cars experienced technical issues ahead of Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

The start of the Sepang race was delayed by 40 minutes due to a downpour; then a chaotic formation lap saw the likes front-row starters Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton suffer from a glitch which rendered throttle input ineffective, with numerous cars coming to a standstill. The red flag was waved.

The situation was branded “unacceptable” by Sergio Perez, who likened it to ‘being in a rental kart and running out of time’; Lando Norris described it “just horrible” and evidence that “we shouldn't have any of that stuff, the electronic side”, given this was linked to Formula 1’s new machinery, which features 47% electrical power.

FIA single-seater Nikolas Tombazis has now explained that, given F1 had never had competitive running in actual wet conditions this season, it was caught out by the power unit’s reaction to cars driving extremely slowly at that time. A software update therefore had to be carried out, hence a 53-minute delay to get the race restarted.

“We didn't manage to test the software as extensively as we would have liked, because there's been very little wet running this year, and there was a bit of a combination of circumstances which caused this bug to kick in,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“Basically, the formation lap, some cars went very slowly, almost came to a standstill. There was a bit of a concertina effect between cars, and some cars almost stopped completely. And that bug prevented the power to be redeployed and for the cars to start again. I think if we had had a bit more testing, we probably would have managed to catch it in time and not to have such a situation.”

Tombazis praised the FIA’s reaction when it came to fixing the issue as swiftly as possible.

“Once the problem happened, our guys realised very quickly what was happening and had to work under a lot of time pressure for an update to the software, which was issued to the teams, and the teams had to install it on their cars,” he added.

“So all of that took about 20 minutes. It may have felt like five hours for spectators waiting [for] a race and for everybody else, which is understandable, and we are sorry about that. But I think it was quite a fast reaction given the problem.”

Not everyone was so upset about some cars running into trouble, with eighth-placed Fernando Alonso joking at the end of an unusually good day for Aston Martin-Honda: “I had 50% DNFs this year, they never stopped the race for us.”

Sports.title: Russell: “You’ve got to laugh” at bad luck as F1 title drifts away
Sports.content:
Mercedes driver George Russell labelled his misfortune as laughable following Formula 1’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, where a power unit failure cost him a podium finish late on.

Russell was a lowly seventh on the grid at Sepang, but the correct choice of intermediate tyres on a damp track and a lightning getaway saw him surge to second into Turn 1, behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Russell was however passed by Max Verstappen as early as lap six, but the first safety car period gave him a chance to sweep past Antonelli around the outside of Turn 5 at the restart as the race leader dropped down to third – though the Italian youngster found a way back into second place just eight laps later.

Further drama did not disrupt the status quo in the top three, but a late safety car meant Russell had a chance to challenge his rivals for victory. However, the chance never came as a power unit failure took him out of the race before the final restart.

“You've almost got to laugh,” Russell told Sky Sports F1 after his third retirement this season – his second purely technical DNF. “It's beyond disappointment. It's just, so many times this season it's happened.

“Of course, it's a real shame, but… Just keep on fighting. Just keep on trying to go.

“The podium, of course, looked very certain. Solid race, not amazing race, but solid race.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Alex Bierens de Haan / LAT Images via Getty Images

“Not the first time, so I'm pretty used to this feeling and these questions, let's say.”

As he said, Russell will “keep on fighting”, but is equally aware of his deficit to championship rival Antonelli reaching an unprecedented 84 points.

The Briton steered clear of any sensational comments – he won’t say the title is out of reach – but his assessment is bleak nonetheless.

“I don't need to say I think it's gone or whatever,” he added. “But, of course, it’s exceptionally unlikely, and that's just the reality.

“I knew if I wanted to come back I needed luck on my side. Unfortunately, I've had luck not on my side. So, you know, a three-point loss today being behind Kimi turned into an 18-point loss. Of course, if the issue was on the other side, it would have been an 18-point gain.

“So, yeah, it's a real shame. It's a real shame, but that's just how it is.”

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia had been one of his “worst experiences” personally, as Red Bull claimed its first victory of the year over the Silver Arrows and Russell suffered that setback.

“I'm so massively annoyed,” Wolff told Sky. “I'm not in a happy place.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

“We didn't have the speed that we were hoping to have before the weekend, so there's a lot of homework to be done in order to recover, which I'm sure we will. Then the race literally went, if you consider the fight with Lewis [Hamilton] behind, went against us. We had such an advantage, one VSC, two safety cars. I mean, you couldn't be more unlucky. And to make things worse, PU failure with a few laps to go to the end with George, which is terrible for his championship and not good at all for our constructor points.”

After praising Antonelli for ‘doing the job’, the Austrian added: “It's just this overarching topic, the DNFs, that could cost us dearly also for the remaining seven races. A championship is quickly turned around against you or for you if you have a DNF, and that's why that can't continue.”

Perhaps Wolff was overdramatic there. At Sepang, Mercedes was outscored by Ferrari for just the first time since the summer break, and the Scuderia still is 151 points in arrears in the constructors’ championship. Meanwhile, Hamilton’s deficit to Antonelli in the drivers’ standings is up to 106 points.

Asked how to pull the team together after such a result, Wolff replied: “I think we have a good action plan. James [Allison, technical director] is really fully on top of it with his leadership team.

“That lifts my mood because I know we have such a tremendous group of people. In the same way as we have with HPP, they're going to sort it out. But that gives me real relief for the moment to know they are the best and they are going to find a solution. And I think we will come back strong.”

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Pursues Unranked Opponent Before Mandatory Defense
Sports.content:
Bektemir Melikuziev wants Jaime Munguia to defend his WBA super middleweight title against him, while the champion’s team reportedly negotiates a step-aside to squeeze in a fight with Keiber Gonzalez first.

That proposed opponent makes Bektemir’s frustration understandable. Gonzalez isn’t in the WBA’s published September top 15 at 168 pounds. Melikuziev is No. 1, yet he’s the fighter being asked to wait.

“The purse is not important, I am ready to fight for free. But please stop disrespecting me and the rules of the game!” Melikuziev wrote on Instagram. “Jaime Munguia, I was the mandatory for the title before you fought for it. You became the champion, respect me just like I would respect you or any other boxer if I was the champion.”

ESPN boxing reporter Salvador “Chava” Rodríguez reported on Instagram that Munguia’s team continues negotiating a step-aside with Melikuziev. According to Rodríguez, the negotiation window runs until October 21, with the aim of allowing Munguia to face Gonzalez before fulfilling his mandatory obligation.

Bektemir’s willingness to fight for free is an expression of how badly he wants the opportunity. It doesn’t establish that he has rejected every possible offer, but his message gives Munguia’s team little reason to assume money will settle this.

From Munguia’s side, Gonzalez looks like an easier defense before a more demanding fight. That may suit the champion, but it leaves Melikuziev waiting for a shot he had already earned before Munguia won the belt.

Even if Bektemir accepts payment to wait, that wouldn’t explain what Gonzalez has done to deserve the opportunity. The WBA would still have to justify approving an opponent outside its published top 15 while its leading challenger sits out.

Munguia has the title now. The responsibility that comes with it is facing the challenger who earned his turn. Asking Bektemir to watch Gonzalez get the next opportunity is a difficult sell, especially when Bektemir is publicly demanding the fight.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua Could Get Gassiev Next
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury or Anthony Joshua could face an easier opponent after their December 11 fight in Cardiff under a four-man WBA plan proposed by Eddie Hearn.

The proposal would pair Murat Gassiev with Jarrell Miller, with their winner facing whoever emerges from Fury–Joshua. That could provide a route to another heavyweight title victory without requiring either British veteran to beat Filip Hrgovic, Daniel Dubois, Fabio Wardley or Moses Itauma.

“I think any resolution would have to appease the parties involved. Then Jarrell Miller falls into that party as well because ultimately he’s number one,” Hearn said to Matchroom Boxing. “Is it a Gassiev v Miller, like two semifinals, AJ against Fury and the winners fight each other? So that’s something that’s possible, but we’ll have to see the official resolution from the WBA.”

Hearn said that there is no official WBA resolution yet. He also noted that putting a belt on Fury–Joshua would give Joshua the opportunity to become a three-time heavyweight champion.

A chance to become a three-time heavyweight champion gives Joshua a reason to back the plan. Facing Gassiev or Miller afterward would also look easier than taking on one of the division’s top contenders.

Gassiev has power, but his heavyweight record leaves him open to the paper-champion criticism. He has yet to demonstrate that he belongs alongside the best in the division. Miller, meanwhile, has not produced the kind of victory that would move the conversation away from his history of positive PED tests and toward his title credentials.

Neither would be harmless. Still, Joshua or Fury would have reason to like their chances against either man compared with the alternatives.

Dubois, Wardley, Hrgovic and Itauma would demand more physically from the two veterans. Those fights would offer a stronger test of whether the Fury–Joshua winner can still compete with the leading heavyweights.

That makes Hearn’s proposed WBA arrangement a good deal for Fury and Joshua. Either would have a good chance of beating the Gassiev–Miller winner, but selling that fight could be harder. A belt would give the promotion something to build around, while leaving more appealing opponents out of the picture.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Questions Zuffa’s Schedule and Spending
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn believes Zuffa Boxing has delivered too little for a promotion with substantial money, a broadcast contract, and access to Turki Alalshikh. His complaint is about the fights reaching fans, with the Matchroom promoter calling its first 10 months “absolutely abysmal.”

“With that money, with that contract, with those connections to Turki Alalshikh, the first 10 months have been absolutely abysmal,” Hearn told The Ariel Helwani Show.

Hearn identified July 26 as Zuffa’s last American show and questioned the lack of an announced U.S. return for the remainder of the year. Zuffa’s own results confirm that its July 26 New York event featured Edgar Berlanga against Steven Butler.

He pointed to Johnny Fisher against Pirotton and the upcoming Chris Billam-Smith–Chev Clarke fight as the promotion’s limited output during the following months. Billam-Smith and Clarke headline November 7 at London’s Copper Box Arena.

Billam-Smith against Clarke has competitive appeal, and Fisher has a following. But those are modest main events for a company whose resources invite expectations of something much bigger.

The American inactivity is the tougher part to explain. A promotion needs regular cards to give viewers a reason to keep watching. Signing recognizable fighters creates interest, but that interest can fade when there is no next date for fans to anticipate.

Shakur Stevenson’s situation adds to Hearn’s criticism. He claimed on X that Gary Antuanne Russell and Raymond Muratalla each want $3 million to face him, writing: “I would love to fight both them guys tho Zuffa gotta cough that 💰 up!”

Neither fight has been made. Shakur’s post does not establish that Zuffa refused to pay, but it identifies two opponents he wants and their asking prices, according to him. Signing Shakur gets Zuffa a recognizable name. Getting him into meaningful fights requires spending on the other side as well.

Hearn also took aim at White’s request to be judged over the next couple of years, describing it as a move away from an earlier 12-month timetable. That is Hearn’s interpretation, but it raises a fair question about how long Zuffa expects its launch period to last.

Hearn has an obvious commercial interest in making a rival look bad. Still, Zuffa needs an answer that comes through its schedule. More announcements could change the picture before December, but the money and connections only become useful to viewers when they produce fights worth watching.

Sports.title: Christian Mbilli Sees Age Catching Up With Canelo
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli sees an older, slower Canelo Alvarez than the fighter in the knockout highlights, and his pressure could test how much the Mexican star has left. Canelo is scheduled to challenge for Mbilli’s WBC super middleweight title on October 31 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Thus far, the fight remains scheduled.

“He’s not the same guy right now,” Mbilli said while watching Canelo’s best stoppages in a video shared by DAZN Boxing.

Mbilli has a point. Canelo still has the timing to catch opponents, but his speed and activity no longer look the same. He attacks in shorter bursts, and his power at super middleweight hasn’t produced the stoppages he once delivered against smaller opposition.

Canelo’s last stoppage came against Caleb Plant in November 2021. He finished Plant in the 11th round to become undisputed at 168 pounds, but even that victory required patience against an opponent who made him work. Nearly five years later, those highlights show what Canelo could do then. Mbilli has to prepare for what he can do now.

There’s accumulated wear to consider, too. The first two Golovkin fights were demanding contests, while Dmitry Bivol repeatedly caught Canelo with combinations and forced him to work at a pace he couldn’t maintain successfully. Those fights may have contributed to the decline, although there’s no way to separate their effects from age.

The concern against Mbilli is what happens between Canelo’s attacks. If he needs longer pauses, Mbilli can use those stretches to throw combinations and make him defend instead of recover. Canelo could land the better individual punch and still lose rounds through inactivity.

Mbilli’s aggression also gives Canelo chances. Walking forward carelessly would leave him available for counters and body shots, and an older Canelo remains dangerous when opponents give him clean targets.

But Mbilli doesn’t need to prove Canelo has lost all his power. He needs to keep working after being caught. If Canelo can no longer discourage that pressure or match the pace, Mbilli’s observation could become the story of the fight.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel’s Future Claim Looks Premature From Brown
Sports.content:
Agit Kabayel being described as the future of heavyweight boxing looks premature for a 34-year-old champion whose toughest tests could still be ahead. Spencer Brown offered that assessment at Tuesday’s kickoff press conference for Kabayel’s November 28 defense against Nelson Hysa.

“He is, for me, going to be the future of heavyweight boxing,” Brown said. “Since the day I met him, I knew greatness was coming. I really did. And he’s proved it to everybody.”

Brown also called Kabayel “the bogeyman of the heavyweights,” claiming nobody wants to fight him.

Kabayel has earned credit for his body punching, pressure, and ability to break opponents down. However, being at the top of his game now doesn’t mean he will stay there long enough to become the fighter Brown describes.

Zhilei Zhang exposed part of the concern last year. The 41-year-old dropped Kabayel with a left hand in the fifth round before being stopped in the sixth. Kabayel’s recovery showed toughness, but the knockdown also showed the danger of taking clean punches while trying to wear down a heavyweight.

Against an opponent who can keep throwing hard shots beyond the early rounds, that approach could become much more costly. Kabayel is hittable, and his pressure requires him to spend considerable time within punching range.

His best wins have come against Zhang, Frank Sanchez, Damian Knyba, Arslanbek Makhmudov and Derek Chisora. Sanchez’s knee trouble adds context to that victory; his co-manager subsequently disclosed that he underwent knee surgery.

It’s a useful collection of wins, but Kabayel still hasn’t faced Filip Hrgovic, Fabio Wardley, Daniel Dubois or Moses Itauma. Those fights would tell us considerably more about whether he can lead the division.

Beating the 42-year-old Hysa won’t settle that argument. Brown can talk about greatness, but Kabayel needs victories over the strongest available heavyweights to support it. At 34, he has less time to build that record than the “future” description suggests.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Fight Could Leave Paramount+ Waiting
Sports.content:
Zuffa Boxing could be left waiting several more months to put Shakur Stevenson on Paramount+ if his proposed fight with Devin Haney takes place on DAZN PPV, as Dan Rafael reports.

“For all the ‘reporting’ about a Haney-Shakur fight supposedly being deep in negotiations, somebody directly involved told me today nothing has changed in weeks & weight remains a major issue,” Rafael posted on X. “IF it happens, I was told it would be on DAZN PPV.”

That would be a letdown for Zuffa’s broadcast partner. Paramount+ is the promotion’s broadcast home in the United States, Canada, and Latin America, but it could miss out on a major fight involving one of Zuffa’s biggest signings.

If negotiations push the Haney fight into January 2027, Shakur would be returning after roughly 12 months out of the ring. Zuffa signed him in July, yet his eventual return could give DAZN the event while Paramount+ continues waiting.

The wait might not end soon afterward. Whether Shakur wins or loses against Haney, recovery time and another training camp could push his Paramount+ debut to May or later. May would be a possible date, rather than something Zuffa could count on.

Getting his next opponent agreed could take longer still. Shakur is a good fighter, but his demands over a catchweight and rehydration restrictions have complicated the Haney talks. If those demands follow him into another negotiation, Zuffa could face another drawn-out effort to get him fighting.

Ryan Garcia would hardly look like an easy agreement if Shakur wanted a 144-pound catchweight alongside a rehydration clause. Ryan has already experienced that combination against Gervonta Davis and has spoken against accepting those restrictions again.

A victory over Haney could make Shakur’s eventual Paramount+ appearance more attractive. Zuffa could also have a promotional role in a DAZN event, depending on the arrangements. Rafael’s report does not establish those details.

Still, signing Shakur and getting him onto Paramount+ are proving to be two different tasks. If his return happens on DAZN in January, Zuffa’s broadcast partner could spend much of the following year waiting for its turn.

Shakur has also said Gary Antuanne Russell and Raymond Muratalla each want $3 million to fight him. “Zuffa gotta cough that up,” he posted on X. He didn’t say Zuffa had refused to pay, but if those are the asking prices, moving on from Haney would leave Zuffa with another expensive fight to negotiate.

Haney could be considerably more expensive. If money is an issue for Zuffa, his asking price could become another obstacle alongside the weight dispute. There is also the question of what that money would buy inside the ring. Shakur and Haney both favor defense, jabs and controlling distance. They could spend long stretches waiting for the other to attack, like two magnets repelling each other.

Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela would offer Zuffa an in-house alternative that could cost less and produce more action. Rayo would be more likely to press Shakur, giving him someone to counter rather than another fighter waiting for him to lead.

Either result would give Zuffa something to build on. A Shakur victory would get its major signing fighting again, while a Rayo upset would raise the profile of another fighter under contract. Paramount+ would get the fight, and Zuffa would have the winner. The remaining question is whether Shakur would accept that option.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Awaits January Date for Jaron Ennis
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly has agreed to terms to face Jaron Ennis in a 154-pound unification fight, with an early January target as they wait for DAZN to set a date.

The proposed unification would give Ennis a chance to add Kelly’s IBF belt to his WBA and WBO titles at 154 pounds. The venue remains unconfirmed, but a British location could make this a more awkward fight for Ennis than the matchup looks on paper.

“We’ve had our terms agreed for the ‘Boots’ fight for some time,” Booth said to The Ring. “From what I’ve been told, he has agreed to his terms as well. It’s literally waiting for DAZN to give Matchroom a date. It’s frustrating, but that’s the nature of the business.”

Kelly needed minor surgery to fix a broken nose following his July 25 decision victory against Caoimhin Agyarko. Sliding the bout to January offers extra healing time, but holding Ennis at bay presents a massive challenge. His championship victory over Bakhram Murtazaliev failed to convince me he was genuinely superior inside the ring.

Outside of a quick flash knockdown, Kelly rarely launched meaningful attacks during long stretches. He spent large portions of every round circling on the back foot, stealing moments with late bursts right before the bell. When scoring that bout, Murtazaliev clearly landed the more effective blows throughout the contest.

Ennis likely needs a knockout if he travels across the Atlantic to secure a victory. Trailing Kelly across the ring plays into that retreat strategy, inviting judges to score razor-thin rounds for the hometown fighter.

Cutting off escape routes and digging hard hooks downstairs will slow that retreat early. Hunting purely with telegraphed power shots upstairs lets Kelly slip away cleanly. Ennis must remain centered, stringing four-punch combinations together rather than resetting after a missed blow, wearing down that slippery guard until it collapses completely.

Trapping Kelly against the ropes offers Ennis his clearest path to victory. Kelly easily ducks single, isolated punches along the perimeter, but layered combinations splitting head and body take away his room to breathe.

Ennis stopped Xander Zayas in seven rounds back in June. Kelly must limit exchanges to quick flurries before slipping away. Ennis has to plant his feet, trap him along the boundaries, and drag him into heavy inside exchanges.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Offers Shakur Stevenson 145-Pound December Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney has offered to face Shakur Stevenson at 145 pounds in December, lowering his proposed weight by two pounds while keeping his demand for no rehydration clause in a post on social media.

“Let’s do this 145 no rehydration clause @ShakurStevenson .. let’s see who’s the real pussy! December.. 2026. Somebody go wake Shakur up.. Tell him we got a deal,” Haney said on X.

The proposal moves Haney off the position he posted on October 4: “147.. no rehydration let’s get it done.” He is now offering to come below the welterweight limit, although the freedom to add weight afterward remains part of his terms.

That is a concession, but it only addresses part of the disagreement. Shakur would get a lower contracted weight without a limit on how much Haney could regain before entering the ring. If his concern is the size of the fighter facing him on the night, 145 pounds doesn’t settle that.

Haney would have to make the extra effort to lose those two pounds. Once the weight check is over, however, he could replenish without a contractual cap. The proposal could still leave Shakur facing a considerably heavier opponent.

From Haney’s side, this gives him something to point to when arguing that he is trying to make the fight. He has lowered his demand and named December as the month he wants. Shakur now has a specific offer to answer, rather than another challenge with no weight attached.

The December date adds urgency if both intend to fight this year. They would need to settle the remaining terms soon enough to arrange the event and prepare properly. A public callout can start that process, but it cannot substitute for their teams reaching a deal.

Haney is giving ground on the contracted weight while holding firm on rehydration. Whether that is enough depends on which concession Shakur wants most. If a cap on Haney’s weight gain remains a requirement, they could still be stuck despite moving closer on the official limit.

Ghana News.title: White House defends Trump comment to let Iran ‘take out’ LA and San Diego
Ghana News.content:
Donald Trump's remark that Iran could "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego has sparked fierce backlash from California politicians - and a strongly worded rebuttal from the White House.

California Governor Gavin Newsom condemned the comment - made by Trump at a campaign rally in Nebraska - as "deranged and dangerous," while LA Mayor Karen Bass described it as a threat and an attempt to "encourage attacks on American lives".

According to the White House, however, Trump was saying that American cities would have been threatened by Iran had he not launched a war there earlier this year.

Both LA and San Diego house major US military installations including Navy ports and Air Force bases.

Trump, while speaking on Monday in Nebraska about the Iran conflict, said: "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego."

There were cheers from sections of the audience as the comments about the two Californian cities were made.

The morning after Trump's statement, Governor Newsom announced that the "dangerous - if not treasonous" statement had prompted him to direct California's State Threat Assessment Center to "monitor the situation in the event that foreign actors interpret the remarks as an invitation" to target California.

The agency is designed to detect and prevent security threats in the state.

San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria wrote that the city was not collateral damage in a post on X, while demanding Trump keep it out of his "reckless war talk".

Trump is yet to respond to the statements made by California's leaders.

In a post on X, White House Communications Director Stephen Cheung described the "media freakout" over Trump's comments as "not rooted in reality".

"He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," Cheung wrote. "America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money".

The president and other administration officials often claim that disrupting Iran's nuclear programme was essential for US national security, and that any issues that have stemmed from the conflict were necessary.

A separate X post from the official White House rapid response account described journalists from the Los Angeles Times reporting on the comments as "buffoons" and again pushed back against the characterisation of the comments by Newsom and others.

"He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance," the account added.

San Diego, located 17 miles (27km) from the border with Mexico, is the eighth-largest city in the US and is home to Naval Base San Diego, the home port of the US Navy's Pacific Fleet, and Naval Amphibious Base Coronado - the main training centre Navy Seals on the West Coast.

It is also where Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton is located, a base where 70,000 service members and civilians work.

Located approximately 120 miles (193 KM) north of San Diego, Los Angeles is the second most populous city in the US.

It is home to the space system command headquarters of the US Space Force, as well as the Los Angeles Air Force Base.

Trump and Newsom met when the president visited California in January after the state was hit by wildfires

This is not the first time the US president and California governor, who may run for president in 2028, have publicly clashed.

Last year Trump described him as incompetent, saying he had failed to adequately respond after some of the Los Angeles anti-immigration enforcement protests turned violent.

Newsom accused Trump of a "brazen abuse of power" after military personnel were deployed to secure federal buildings during those protests.

Earlier this year, Trump mocked Newsom's dyslexia, saying presidents should not have learning disabilities, which led to criticism from dyslexia charities.

Ghana News.title: US televangelist Jim Bakker, disgraced from sex scandal and fraud, dies at 86
Ghana News.content:
US televangelist Jim Bakker's death was announced on Monday by his second wife Lori Bakker

US televangelist Jim Bakker, who built a multimillion-dollar media empire before being jailed for fraud and conspiracy, has died aged 86.

Bakker and his then-wife, Tammy Faye, founded a Christian television programme called The PTL Club in 1974, which, at its peak, attracted 13 million viewers per day.

The 86-year-old's death was announced on Monday by his second wife Lori Bakker, who described him as "a pioneer of Christian television".

By the late 80s, Bakker and Tammy Faye's empire began to fall apart after he became embroiled in a sex scandal and later convicted of mail and wire fraud. Tammy Faye, who divorced him in 1992, was never charged.

Bakker remarried in 1998, and alongside his second wife, Lori, launched a new TV ministry in 2003.

Lori Bakker described her late husband as "my best friend, and the man I was honoured to walk beside through so many seasons of life and ministry".

She did not specify the cause of death.

However, Bakker's first program The PTL Club - short for 'Praise the Lord' or 'People That Love' - was what cemented his fame with his first wife Tammy Faye.

The couple built their empire with 2,000 employees and a 2,300-acre (930-hectare) Heritage USA theme park complex in Fort Mill, South Carolina.

The Bakkers had a famously opulent lifestyle, owning a private jet, multiple homes, luxury cars, jewellery and even an air-conditioned dog house.

In 1987, Bakker resigned from the PTL ministry after revelations of a 1980 sexual encounter with a former church secretary, Jessica Hahn.

It later emerged Hanhn received a $265,000 payoff with ministry funds, resulting in Bakker being defrocked of his ministerial credentials and right to perform religious duties.

Jim and Tammy Faye Bakker had a famously opulent lifestyle, owning a private jet, multiple homes and luxury cars

Hahn also accused Bakker of sexual assault, though the evangelist denied this, claiming the encounter had been consensual.

Bakker was then convicted in 1989 of 24 counts of mail and wire fraud and conspiracy in a scheme involving their Christian theme park, and served more than four years in prison.

Tammy Faye stayed with her husband throughout the trial but divorced him in 1992 while he was in prison. She died of cancer in 2007.

Following Bakker's release from prison in 1994, he wrote a book titled I Was Wrong and married his second wife Lori in 1998.

The couple began a TV ministry together in 2003 and in 2008 they began taping The Jim Bakker Show.

Ghana News.title: Congolese-born golfer to represent Ghana at Turkish Airlines World Cup grand final
Ghana News.content:
Louanges Kous Mang, a Congolese-born golfer from the Republic of Congo

Ghana will be represented on the international golf stage this November by an inspiring golfer whose story crosses borders, cultures and communities.

Louanges Kous Mang, a Congolese-born golfer from the Republic of Congo who has made Ghana her home, has earned the honour of representing Ghana at the Turkish Airlines World Golf Cup Grand Final in Antalya, Türkiye, after winning the Ghana qualifying tournament.

Louanges emerged as the overall winner of the Ghana qualifier, competing alongside both male and female golfers, and secured her place at the prestigious international Grand Final scheduled to take place in Antalya in November 2026.

For Louanges, the victory is about much more than a golf trophy.

It represents a remarkable journey of passion, perseverance and faith, while also reflecting the power of Ghana to provide opportunities for people from diverse backgrounds to thrive.

“I am incredibly grateful for this opportunity to represent Ghana,” Louanges said.

“As a Congolese woman who has made Ghana my home, it is a tremendous honour to be able to carry the Ghanaian flag onto an international stage. I am proud of my Congolese roots, but I am equally proud to represent the country that has given me a home and where my golfing journey has developed.”

A Global Golfing Platform

The Turkish Airlines World Golf Cup is one of the world’s largest corporate amateur golf tournaments.

Since its launch in 2013, the competition has grown into a truly global event, with more than 750 tournaments held across 85 countries and 130 destinations, attracting over 60,000 amateur golfers.

This year alone, more than 10,000 golfers competed in over 122 qualifying events across 83 countries before the successful qualifiers earned their places at the Grand Final.

The Grand Final brings together some of the best amateur golfers from around the world in Antalya, one of Türkiye’s premier golfing destinations.

The 2025 Grand Final, for example, brought together 120 amateur golfers from around the world. Pakistan’s Adeel Shafqat was crowned the overall gross champion, while players from the United Arab Emirates, Algeria, Mexico, Jordan and China also claimed honours in their respective categories.

The tournament has evolved beyond a sporting competition, becoming a platform that connects people and cultures through golf.

Ghana on the World Stage

Louanges’ qualification adds another chapter to Ghana’s growing presence in international amateur golf.

Her journey also demonstrates the increasingly diverse nature of Ghana’s golfing community, where people from different nationalities and backgrounds come together through their love of the sport.

For Louanges, the opportunity carries a strong personal and national significance.

“I give all the glory to God for this incredible opportunity,” she said.

“To stand on the international stage representing Ghana is something I do not take for granted. I will go to Türkiye with gratitude, determination and the desire to make Ghana proud.”

Her qualification has also been warmly received by members of Ghana’s golfing community, who have celebrated her achievement and the opportunity it presents to showcase Ghanaian talent on the international stage.

As she prepares for Antalya, Louanges will not only be carrying her golf clubs. She will be carrying the hopes and support of the Ghanaian golfing community, while proudly acknowledging the Congolese heritage that forms an important part of her story.

From the fairways of Achimota to the international stage in Antalya, her journey is a reminder that sport has the unique ability to transcend borders.

Ghana News.title: Amazon wins global rights to stream Emmys in six-year deal
Ghana News.content:
Theagreement replaces the "Wheel Deal" system, which rotated the gala among major networks like ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC.

Amazon Prime Video has secured exclusive global rights to stream the Emmy Awards under a six-year deal, ending the ceremony's run on traditional US broadcast television.

Starting in 2027, the agreement replaces a rotation of the gala among major networks such as ABC, CBS, Fox, and NBC. The ceremony will instead stream live for free worldwide each September, with no Prime Video subscription needed.

Official terms were not disclosed. The BBC has contacted Amazon and the Emmys for comment.

The move is another indication of how live events are shifting to digital platforms as viewing habits evolve. The Oscars, for example, are moving to YouTube live globally starting in 2029.

Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester, said the existing setup had become out of sync with modern television.

"The shows driving the industry forward largely originate on streaming platforms, yet the awards themselves were tethered to broadcast television," Proulx said.

"That's why a leading streaming service like Prime Video makes sense for the Emmys' next act."

Cris Abrego, chair of the Television Academy, said the deal gives the ceremony "unprecedented global reach", allowing audiences in more than 200 countries to watch live.

"Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share," Abrego said in a statement issued by Amazon.

Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, said the platform is honoured to serve as the "global home" for the ceremony, adding that streaming the show for free delivers " the best entertainment to our customers worldwide."

The agreement marks a milestone for Amazon, giving Prime Video its first marquee entertainment broadcast after building a live-sports profile centred on the NFL's Thursday Night Football, NBA, and UEFA Champions League fixtures.

Amazon's latest earnings highlighted strong gains in live viewership, including record ratings for its inaugural NBA season, which peaked at 6.5 million viewers for Game 7 of the Eastern Conference Semifinals.

The Emmys deal positions Amazon directly alongside Google, whose video platform YouTube holds the upcoming Oscar rights.

YouTube relies primarily on an ad-supported model, whereas Amazon is leveraging free live access to draw massive global audiences into its wider ecosystem.

Like its live sporting events, the free broadcast will allow Amazon to build a substantial global advertising footprint.

Moving exclusively to Prime Video is significant for the Emmys, ending a rotation across the major legacy broadcast networks that has been in place since 1955 and marking the first time the gala will leave traditional broadcast television entirely.

First held in 1949, the Emmys honor achievements in acting, writing, and production, serving as a primary showcase for the global television industry.

Ghana News.title: European Film Festival returns to Ghana after a 5-year break
Ghana News.content:
The European Film Festival has returned to Ghana after a five-year break, with this year’s edition focusing on peace, tolerance and inclusion.

The festival was launched in Accra by the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, who says Ghana has no shortage of creative talent but needs more platforms to help young creatives develop their skills and gain exposure.

She believes opportunities that allow emerging filmmakers to interact with other players in the industry can help them build their expertise and take their work further.

“We’re not a short supply of creatives. We’re a short supply of the platforms that’s available to them. And I think that is why when we have these opportunities, we should seize them because it helps you to build your expertise, to see how other people are doing what they are doing and also to meet Ghanaian film producers.”

The Minister also urged young creatives to take advantage of opportunities created through the festival and other platforms available to them.

According to her, Ghana has the opportunity to correct distorted narratives by telling its own stories and presenting a stronger image of the country to international audiences.

EU Ambassador to Ghana, Rune Skinnebach, said the festival is about more than screening films.

He said it is also intended to create opportunities for artists to connect with their European counterparts and gain platforms to take their stories to wider audiences.

“But the festival is more than movies. The festival is about creating a platform for artists, Guinean artists, to be exposed to European artists, but also to get them a platform from which they can continue to tell their amazing stories to the wider audience. So this is why we have these movies tonight and this is why we have the European Film Festival also.”

The festival features film screenings and creative engagements aimed at bringing filmmakers, artists and audiences together.

The 2026 edition is expected to provide opportunities for creative exchanges between Ghanaian and European industry players.

Ghana News.title: PTA backs teachers’ strike, threatens street protest if gov’t misses October 30 deadline
Ghana News.content:
The National Council of Parents Teachers Association (PTA) has backed the concerns of striking pre-tertiary teachers, warning that parents will join the unions in street protests if the government fails to meet its October 30 deadline for resolving outstanding issues.

Secretary of the Council, Raphael Kofi Gapson, said parents recognise the legitimacy of the teachers’ grievances and believe government must honour its commitments.

Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story, he said parents initially supported the strike because they shared the teachers’ concerns and wanted government to take concrete steps to resolve the dispute.

“We saw that as a genuine concern,” he said.

Mr Gapson, however, urged teachers to consider returning to the classroom while negotiations continue, saying parents are hopeful the ongoing discussions will lead to a resolution by the end of the week.

“We only hope and pray that since the Finance Minister is part of these discussions and they've firmed up concrete measures, we cannot say that we would want to throw away the baby with the bathwater. There should be a way around it,” he said.

He said parents would give government until October 30 to demonstrate concrete progress in fulfilling its commitments to teachers.

Mr Gapson warned that failure to meet the deadline would compel the PTA to join the teacher unions in protest.

“We are telling government too that if by the 30th we don't see any concrete steps, we'll be on the street with the teacher unions to demonstrate against government,” he stated.

He stressed that teachers have legitimate financial obligations that must be honoured, arguing that the issue is one of national priorities.

Mr Gapson also expressed optimism that the negotiations between government and the teacher unions could resolve the impasse and allow schools to return to normal operations.

His comments follow renewed negotiations between the teacher unions, the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) and the Ghana Education Service (GES), which ended without an agreement on Tuesday.

The parties are expected to reconvene on Wednesday, October 7, as efforts continue to resolve the issues that triggered the nationwide strike.

Ghana News.title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger
Ghana News.content:
Paramount Skydance has officially taken over Warner Bros. Discovery in a $110bn merger that is set to reshape Hollywood and the media landscape.

The takeover - merging two of the biggest studios in Los Angeles - comes after months of legal disputes and widespread criticism over feared cuts and consolidation could harm competition and consumers.

It will alter streaming for millions, usher in a new chapter in the film and TV industry, and leave one of the biggest US news outlets, CNN, in uncertain territory.

The merger will also bring together a host of entities including HBO, CBS, Nickelodeon, Showtime, Comedy Central, DC Studios and Food Network.

Paramount will acquire ownership of iconic franchises that include Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, The Lord of the Rings to add to its existing catalogue of hit franchises which includes Indiana Jones, Mission: Impossible and Shrek.

The newly merged entertainment behemoth will be re-branded under the name Skydance Corporation, the company originally founded by David Ellison before he took over both Paramount and Warner Bros Discover.

Ellison, chairman and chief executive of Skydance, said the completion of the deal was "historic" for the film industry.

"From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality," he said.

Asked about the merger after it had been finalised, US President Donald Trump described the deal as "great".

"They're terrific people and it's going to be a great company," he said.

Last week, Ellison named the outgoing chief executive of Mattel, Ynon Kreiz, as co-chief executive.

Kreiz will focus on the company's day-to-day operations, including integrating the newly-combined businesses, while Ellison will focus on strategy and technology.

Mark Thompson - who once served as director general of the BBC - will continue in his role as chairman and editor-in-chief of CNN Worldwide, while Bari Weiss remains editor-in-chief of CBS News.

Casey Bloys, who has lead HBO and Max Content, will be the co-chair and chief content officer for direct-to-consumer content.

Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester Research, said that change "essentially means the HBO leadership team is now in charge of Skydance's combined streaming operation".

"While that bodes well for the HBO brand, make no mistake, Bloys will be pressured to find and deliver cost efficiencies that could affect content quality," he warned.

Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said the company has high debts at a time when interest rates are high.

"The combined entity, now called Skydance, needs to cut costs and make bigger profits to be able to get the debt down to more manageable levels," he said.

"The fact Tom Cruise movie Digger, Warner Bros' last release before the merger, has been a major flop is a reminder of how the film industry is not a guaranteed ticket to riches."

Rocky path to merger

While the company said it had received unanimous approval from competition authorities across the world, the long running takeover process has featured controversy since the beginning.

Netflix initially had a deal to buy part of Warner Bros Discovery, but Paramount Skydance launched a bidding war, leading to the streaming giant walking away.

Lawyers in about a dozen US states then filed lawsuits - led by California - aiming to block the deal, arguing it would stifle competition, raise consumer prices and cause "substantial" harm to movie theatres, cable distributors and "ultimately, audiences nationwide".

US states announced a settlement with Paramount and Ellison last month which paved the way for the merger to go ahead.

As part of the deal, Paramount has agreed to establish a "news editorial independence board" to "ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting" at CNN and CBS.

Politics and editorial independence has become an area of concern at CBS since the news broadcaster was taken over in 2025 as part of separate a merger between Skydance Media and Paramount.

Ellison, who hosted a dinner for President Donald Trump earlier this year, has sought to reassure people that editorial independence will be maintained.

Over its 103-year-old history, Warner Bros has won more than 100 Academy Awards - including dominating at last year's show with a record-tying 11 Oscars for One Battle After Another, Sinners and Weapons.

Paramount traces its roots back 1912 and also boasts more than 100 Oscars for classics spanning from The Godfather to Titanic, though the studio has not mirrored the same recent spate of Hollywood honours.

The studio was not nominated for any projects last year by the Academy. Its last win came in 2022 with Top Gun: Maverick.

The deal with US states aims to ensure the merged studios will produce "real, robust movies" that will generate economic activity and put people back to work, said California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the lawsuit and settlement.

To prevent the studio from fulfilling its annual quota with low-budget or automated content, the deal includes strict guardrails against "AI-generated" films.

As part of the agreement, Paramount must release at least 30 films each year. If it fails to meet its annual production quota, it will be forced to sell its 49% stake in Miramax, the film company founded by disgraced Hollywood mogul Harvey Weinstein and his brother Bob.

Paramount also must ensure 20% of all film production takes place in the US for the first two years, rising to more than 30% through the following three years.

Ghana News.title: Suspend offshore gold exploration licence – NAFAG urges gov’t
Ghana News.content:
The National Fisheries Association of Ghana (NAFAG) has appealed to the government to suspend an offshore reconnaissance licence granted to Gold Coast GRC Ghana Ltd. for gold exploration along Ghana’s shallow continental shelf, pending further consultations with the fishing industry.

In a petition dated October 6, 2026, signed by the association’s President, Nana Joojo Solomon, and addressed to the President, NAFAG demanded clarification of the potential implications of the exploration programme for fisheries resources, marine habitats and coastal livelihoods.

The association, which represents five major fisheries groups, said its concerns centered on the size of the licensed area, stakeholder consultation, and the application of fisheries and environmental safeguards.

NAFAG said the company held 10 offshore reconnaissance licences covering about 10,000 square kilometres along approximately 300 kilometres of coastline between Half Assini and Winneba, extending about 33 kilometres offshore.

It said the company’s published map appeared to indicate that parts of the licensed area could fall within the Inshore Exclusion Zone (IEZ), which extends up to 12 nautical miles, or about 22 kilometres, from the coastline.

The association said the precise extent of any overlap should be established through the publication of the official cadastral coordinates and licence instruments.

NAFAG also raised concerns about the proximity of the licensed area to Greater Cape Three Points, where Ghana launched its first Marine Protected Area at Busua on April 14, 2026, as part of efforts to strengthen marine conservation.

Assessment

NAFAG’s concerns also relate to Section 50 of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146).

The provision requires a person planning an activity, other than fishing, that is likely to have a substantial impact on fishery or other aquatic resources to inform the Fisheries Commission before the activity begins. The Commission may subsequently require a Fisheries Impact Assessment or make recommendations to prevent or minimise potential adverse impacts.

NAFAG said it had not established whether the applicable fisheries assessment process had been completed in relation to the project and called for clarification from the relevant authorities.

NAFAG also questioned the consultation process, saying that although a stakeholder meeting was held at the Accra City Hotel on July 9, 2026, it had not received the report of the meeting.

NAFAG therefore called on the government to establish the precise location and conditions of the licences, clarify the applicable fisheries and environmental safeguards, and ensure meaningful consultation with affected stakeholders before the programme advances.

It urged President Mahama and the relevant agencies to suspend further exploration pending those steps, arguing that Ghana’s marine resources must be managed in a manner that protects fisheries, food security and coastal livelihoods while allowing responsible investment in the country’s natural resources.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
