World.title: Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason
World.content:
Former German spy chief August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.

Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.

Prosecutors allege that he used classified intelligence to "draft an analysis" for one foreign intelligence service and maintained contact with another foreign spying service. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.

Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D, accusing him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents for money.

Manfred D, who was Hanning's bureau chief and remained in the BND until this year, is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.

Local media reported Hanning was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near MÃ¼nster while Manfred D was arrested in Bavaria. Hanning is due in court on Wednesday and Manfred D will appear on Tuesday.

Prosecutors say Manfred D, who also served as the chief of staff for Hanning's successors between 2012 and 2026, used his role to gain access to highly confidential information which he then passed on to Hanning "in exchange for remuneration".

"The current findings suggest that, over the years, Manfred D provided Hanning with approximately 2,000 documents, many of which contained classified information to be used exclusively by the Federal Intelligence Service for internal purposes," the statement says.

"On one occasion, Hanning used classified intelligence ... to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service," prosecutors said, noting it was not clear if "the material reached the intended recipient".

Hanning is also accused of being "in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D, for several years".

Local media say Hanning's alleged possession of intelligence documents came to light during a separate case relating to German steakhouse heiress Christina Block.

Hamburg public prosecutor's office accused Block of orchestrating the kidnapping of her two youngest children in 2023 due to a custody dispute. Investigators allege Hanning was involved in an earlier attempted kidnapping of the children, which he denies.

State criminal police officers reportedly discovered an electronic data storage device containing sensitive information including recent BND documents.

It is not the first time the BND has faced similar controversy. A high-ranking German intelligence officer was charged with treason in 2023 for allegedly passing state secrets to Russia.

Prosecutors alleged Carsten L shared intelligence about the war in Ukraine and the Wagner mercenary group and received roughly â¬400,000 ($450,000; Â£340,000). His trial is ongoing.

World.title: Ship sinks and crew missing after Black Sea drone attack
World.content:
A civilian cargo ship has sunk and its crew is missing after being attacked by drones in the Black Sea, Bulgarian officials say.

A second vessel - carrying grain - was also hit within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Its 18 crew were rescued.

Radev did not say who was behind the attacks, which come as Russia intensifies strikes in the Black Sea, particularly the eastern side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

Moscow has not commented on the latest incident, a day after it was accused by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of striking a civilian vessel carrying corn. EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the attacks were "unacceptable".

Air and sea drones were involved in the attacks at about 03:00 (23:00 GMT), some 70 miles (112 km) off the coastal town of Byala in eastern Bulgaria, Radev said.

The sunken ship was flying under the flag of Togo, he said. Named the Alfa Watan, it was a Turkish-owned general cargo ship and was reportedly heading for Sulina, Romania.

It is not clear what the Alfa Watan was carrying or how many people were on board.

A Bulgarian vessel was close by, but when they arrived all they saw was an overturned boat and rafts as well as life jackets. A search operation has been launched.

Radev said Bulgarian sailors had rescued the crew members from the second ship - including two who were injured in a fire on board. Eleven were Turkish and seven Indian nationals. That ship, the Able, was flying the flag of Palau and transporting grain.

Its last reported position was five nautical miles (9km) from the Alfa Watan.

Radev condemned the strikes as "a flagrant violation of maritime law".

He told reporters: "Such an attack within the Bulgarian exclusive economic zone is absolutely unacceptable."

He did not accuse Russia of carrying out the strikes, but referred to the war in Ukraine, saying: "As I have long maintained, if this war is not halted in time, it will continue to expand its geographical reach and increase risks, including the risk of a global conflict."

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on X: "The situation in the Black Sea is increasingly concerning.

"Commercial ships â and innocent crews â are being targeted, with lives already lost at sea," she said. "While exact circumstances of these incidents are still being established, the developments are very concerning."

"Attacks on civilian shipping are unacceptable."

Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea is just over 29,000 sq km (11,197 sq miles), about 6% of the total size of the Black Sea.

World.title: Lawyer for one of Cornell 7 calls for special prosecutor to be removed over previous comments
World.content:
A lawyer for one of the seven men accused of participating in a Cornell University gang rape has called for the special prosecutor on the case to recuse herself over past public comments.

The lawyer had said a social media post from New York Attorney General Letitia James throws into question her investigation's "integrity and independence".

In the 28 September post, James wrote that "what this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable" and told survivors that "we stand with you".

The university's administration is under fire over its alleged mishandling of the October 2024 incident and, according to US media, now faces a no-confidence vote by Cornell faculty.

The university's Faculty Senate, a governing body comprised of professors and other academic staff, will vote on a resolution of no confidence next week, according to reports. Cornell is an Ivy League university, alongside Harvard and Yale, and its faculty includes Nobel laureates and other distinguished researchers.

A majority no-confidence vote would be a largely symbolic gesture, signalling the broader faculty's discontent and applying pressure on university leadership to act.

Cornell University announced on Tuesday that it was hiring Sally Yates, a former deputy attorney general, to lead an independent review of the university's practices and procedures on sexual assault and related conduct.

"Yates and her team will conduct a detailed review of the University's response to the allegations involving Jane Doe", the university said in a statement, "including whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to the matter".

Allegations made in a lawsuit against seven men and the university have rocked the campus in New York state, with hundreds of students and faculty members gathering there on Monday in protest, and sparked anger across the country.

World.title: Finland orders halt to work on two Google data centres
World.content:
Finnish authorities have ordered a halt to building work at two planned Google data centres amid concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest.

The sites form part of Google's record â¬13bn (Â£11bn; $15bn) investment in Finland, announced less than a month ago and described by the company as its largest single investment in Europe.

The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) said work at one site was carried out without a mandatory environmental impact assessment and ordered measures that would "significantly alter the environment" to be suspended by 23 October.

Google said it had "fallen short of our own high standards in this instance" and would follow the agency's guidance.

The orders relate to preparatory work carried out at the planned data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani.

According to LVV's head of environment Tommi Muilu, work at the sites included the removal of trees and topsoil, the construction of site roads and storage areas, and changes to ditches.

Tuike Finland, the company behind Google's data centre projects, has been asked to provide an explanation and set out how it intends to proceed by 14 October. The agency said it could begin "enforcement proceedings" if the company failed to comply with its demand.

Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, had previously told the AFP news agency that "nature sites which should be preserved" had been felled. The conservation group had previously called for work to be halted while the environmental requirements were examined.

In a statement to the BBC, Google said: "We understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance."

It said it had "acted in good faith under the Forestry Act", carried out nature surveys and put measures in place to protect areas of high environmental value.

World.title: Kenya confirms its first Ebola death as outbreak spreads
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed its first ever case of Ebola - a Kenyan citizen who has been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo for the past seven years.

Health Minister Aden Duale said the patient, who fell ill a month ago, and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo, died days after arriving in the capital, Nairobi.

Duale said the patient boarded a flight on Saturday and underwent normal public screening at the main airport in Nairobi before he was transferred by a relative to a hospital in the city.

Kenya's health ministry says it has since stepped up surveillance at airports and border crossings.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak of the disease.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died. However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

Since then, all known cases of the highly infectious disease have been in DR Congo.

The virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

World.title: 'Ghost particles' from space telescope wins physics Nobel
World.content:
On the rare occasions when a neutrino strikes an atomic nucleus, it produces fast-moving charged particles. It is these racing through the ice, which give off a blue glow, which sensitive light detectors can pick up.

The pattern and timing of that light allow scientists to estimate the direction the neutrino came from â helping them trace its origins in the cosmos. But these interactions are so rare that the observatory needed an enormous volume of clear ice.

Halzen's idea was to use a vast natural ice sheet in Antarctica. So began an audacious plan to build a neutrino observatory at the geographic South Pole, with thousands of light sensors embedded deep in the ice.

The neutrino's ghostly nature, the very thing that makes it so hard to detect, also makes it a powerful messenger from the distant Universe.

Neutrinos rarely interact with material in its way, so they can go right through dense regions that light cannot easily penetrate.

And because they have no electric charge, magnetic fields do not bend their paths through space. That means their direction of arrival can point scientists back towards their source.

Their energies carry further insight into the processes that created them - helping scientists investigate how exploding stars and the environments around giant black holes accelerate particles to extraordinary energies.

Louis Barson, director of science at the Institute of Physics in London, said the IceCube Observatory had enabled astronomers to investigate phenomena that conventional telescopes cannot see.

"The discoveries that have followed are helping us understand some of the most energetic and mysterious processes in the universe - and that's thanks to Professor Halzen's work," he added.

Prof Subir Sarkar, physicist from the University of Oxford, quoted the French novelist Marcel Proust in describing his assessment of Halzen's contribution to science:

"'The only true voyage of discovery, the only fountain of Eternal Youth, would be not to visit strange lands but to possess other eyes, to behold the universe through the eyes of another, of a hundred others, to behold the hundred universes that each of them beholds, that each of them is'.

"Francis Halzen has led the IceCube collaboration on just such a voyage of discovery and opened a new window on to our Universe".

World.title: PNC 2026: NCDMB, DMG affirm collaboration with Bayelsa govt, unveil new activities
World.content:
As preparations intensify for the 2026 edition of the Practical Nigerian Content (PNC) Forum, slated for 30 November – 3 December 2026, the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB) and its partner, DMG Events, have strengthened their long-standing collaboration with the Bayelsa State Government, to ensure seamless hosting of the flagship industry gathering.

This commitment was affirmed on Tuesday during a strategic engagement between officials of NCDMB and DMG Events with the Deputy Governor of Bayelsa State, Peter Pereotubo Akpe, at the Government House in Yenagoa.

The meeting was convened to appreciate the State Government for its close partnership in convening the PNC over the past 15 years and to solicit continued assistance for the 15th edition, which will hold at the NCDMB Conference Centre, Yenagoa, Bayelsa State.

Leading the delegation to the meeting, General Manager, Corporate Communications Division, NCDMB, Obinna Ezeobi, highlighted the economic impact of the PNC Forum, as well as other NCDMB’s activities and programmes in Bayelsa State.

He conveyed the appreciations of the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, Felix Omatsola Ogbe to the Bayelsa State Government for its significant contributions to the PNC, particularly in hosting the opening banquet and supporting the Youth PNC segment, which exposes young persons in the Niger Delta region to emerging opportunities in the oil and gas industry and core competencies for successful careers in other key sectors of the economy.

Ezeobi also alluded to new initiatives introduced for the 2026 PNC Forum, designed to invigorate the conference and enhance value for participants, while Senior Manager, Zonal Coordination, NCDMB, Mr Adebayo Joseph, spoke on plans for the Youth PNC.

Leader of the DMG team, Ms Olamide Oloko, outlined the main PNC programme and the new ideas such as the Local Content Roundtable for November 30 and the twoday programme for Local Community Contractors (LCCs), to help scale their operations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Other innovative initiatives at this year’s PNC include the breakout session, designed to gather stakeholders’ perspectives that will shape the trajectory of Nigerian Content over the next decade, and the Townhall Session with key industry leaders, including the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, the Group CEO of NNPC Ltd, the Chief Executive of NUPRC, the Chairman of OPTS, and the Chairman of PETAN.

In his response, Deputy Governor Akpe pledged Bayelsa State’s continued collaboration, assuring delegates of adequate security and reaffirming the State’s tradition of hosting the gala dinner and actively participating in the main conference as well as the Youth PNC. He commended NCDMB for integrating some participants from the 2025 edition of the Youth PNC into its capacitybuilding programmes, and demanded for increased participation of senior oil and gas industry officials in the welcome gala dinner.

The Practical Nigerian Content Forum, hosted annually by NCDMB and DMG Events, serves as a strategic platform to review and track local content implementation and chart new directions for investment and growth in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry. The 2026 edition is expected to deepen collaboration, strengthen local participation, and enhance value retention across the sector.

World.title: Otti mourns Abia-born Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje, commiserates with FG over plane crash
World.content:
The Governor of Abia State, Alex Otti, has expressed deep sadness over the death of Abia-born Squadron Leader Ahamefule Aham Man-Ugwueje, one of the pilots of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft, NAF 931, which crashed in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on Monday, 5 October.

In a statement on Tuesday by Ferdinand Ekeoma, his special adviser on media and publicity, Mr Otti described Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje’s death and those of other military personnel aboard the Nigerian Air Force plane as painful and devastating.

According to the Governor, “This accident is both painful and devastating, because it has brought untold sorrow and anguish to the victims’ families, their friends and loved ones, the Nigerian Air Force, and the nation at large.”

Governor Otti regretted that Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje perished in the air disaster just about two weeks after he wedded his beloved wife, Flight Lieutenant Damilola Adekunle, in Abuja, a sad development that has robbed the couple of the opportunity to spend their lives together as husband and wife.

Governor Otti, on behalf of his family, the Government and people of Abia State, sends his deepest condolences to the families of the victims, the people of Umuahia where Squadron Leader Man-Ugwueje hailed from, the Nigerian Air Force and the Federal Government of Nigeria, and prays for the peaceful repose of their souls in God’s bosom.

World.title: Nigeria has reduced reliance on oil revenue – Tinubu
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu says Nigeria has significantly reduced its reliance on oil revenue as his administration pushes to diversify the economy and attract more investment into other sectors.

He said the government would continue to develop the petroleum industry but use its resources to support broader economic activity rather than depend on crude oil as the main driver of growth.

The President, represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the fifth anniversary of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC).

“We have already reduced our dependence on oil revenue, and we intend to go further,” President Tinubu said.

He said the government’s diversification strategy was focused on agriculture, manufacturing, digital and creative industries, while the oil and gas sector would continue to provide energy, foreign exchange and revenue for the country.

The claim comes as the administration continues to pursue reforms aimed at increasing oil production, improving revenue remittances and attracting fresh investment into the petroleum sector.

In February, President Tinubu issued an executive order directing oil and gas revenues due to the Federation to be paid directly into the Federation Account.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The order also ended certain deductions previously retained by NNPC Limited, including a 30 per cent management fee on profit oil and profit gas.

Oil remains important to Nigeria’s finances

Despite the government’s push to reduce dependence on oil, petroleum remains an important source of public revenue and foreign exchange.

The sector has, however, faced challenges including fluctuations in crude production and oil prices, as well as security and operational problems.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in March that oil and gas revenue remittances had fallen significantly below projections in the first two months of 2026. While N937.10 billion was budgeted as oil and gas revenue for the period, actual remittances stood at N137.41 billion.

President Tinubu said improved security and cooperation among oil producers, host communities, security agencies and the NUPRC had helped stabilise production.

He said the government’s efforts had also helped attract investors who previously left Nigeria, adding that the country had ranked first among Africa’s leading destinations for upstream investment for two consecutive years.

Push for more oil and gas investment

The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Oil, Heineken Lokpobiri, said Nigeria currently produces about 1.7 million barrels of crude oil per day and has more than 37 billion barrels of oil reserves.

Mr Lokpobiri said more investment, additional licensing rounds and increased exploration were needed to unlock the country’s petroleum resources.

The NUPRC has also reported increased investment activity in the upstream sector.

In August, the regulator said it had approved more than $57 billion in Field Development Plans since 2024, with 22 major offshore projects expected to come on stream between 2026 and 2030. The projects are estimated to attract between $30 billion and $50 billion in investment.

Nigeria’s oil and condensate reserves stood at 37.01 billion barrels as of January 2026, while gas reserves increased to 215.19 trillion cubic feet, according to NUPRC data.

Tinubu declares decade of gas

President Tinubu said gas would be central to the government’s energy strategy, describing the period ahead as a decade of gas.

“With the largest gas reserves in Africa, we will expand gas supply for power, industry and clean cooking, reduce flaring and methane emissions, and grow renewable energy alongside it,” he said.

He added that the government would pursue an energy transition suited to Nigeria’s circumstances, arguing that the country should meet its climate commitments without compromising energy access and economic development.

He also noted that a stronger upstream industry could create jobs for Nigerian engineers, fabricators and oilfield service companies.

President Tinubu said the Petroleum Industry Act had provided a foundation for reforms in the sector but noted that legislation alone could not guarantee investment.

According to him, investors had raised concerns about high costs, lengthy contracting processes and uncertainty around fiscal terms for complex projects.

He urged the NUPRC to maintain clear regulatory processes, provide reliable timelines and work with other government agencies to reduce overlapping requirements.

The President also said operators benefiting from government incentives must meet their obligations on work programmes, local content, environmental protection and host communities.

He urged the commission to remain independent and accountable in its regulatory decisions.

World.title: What I’ll do with my ₦90m cash prize — BBNaija season 11 winner Temi Nkem
World.content:
Big Brother Naija Season 11 winner, Temi Nkem, has revealed how she plans to spend and invest her ₦90 million cash prize after winning the “Show Ya Sef” edition of the reality television show.

Temi won the finale with 25.87% of the votes, defeating Aikou, who finished as first runner-up with 23.68%, while Sheba placed third with 9.80%. Her victory made her the fifth female winner in Big Brother Naija history.

Her ₦160 million prize package includes ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and other sponsored prizes. The cash prize was reduced from the original ₦100 million after ₦10 million was allocated to the season’s Most Influential Player of the Week (MIPOW) fund.

Temi said she plans to invest a substantial portion of the money, support her parents, complete her university education and set aside some money for herself.

Investment

Speaking in an exclusive interview with PREMIUM TIMES at the official prize presentation ceremony in Lagos on Tuesday, the Accounting and Finance student said she had already started thinking about how to divide the money before leaving the Big Brother house.

“I will be investing a very big sum of my money because obviously, if everybody already knows, I already said that I studied a degree in Accounting and Finance, and I took an extra degree called Treasury.

“So, yeah, that’s finance. So I know how to work with my money. And honestly, I want to get my money to grow. I’m going to finish my uni. I’m going to go back to my studies,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The London-born Nigerian added that she would support her parents with part of the money while also allowing herself some personal enjoyment after her 70-day stint in the reality show.

“I’m also going to give my parents, and then obviously I’m also going to spend on myself. I need a little treat for myself. I need a holiday. I do, a few,” she said.

‘I thought I wouldn’t win’

Reflecting on her victory, Temi said she did not expect to win the competition, particularly because of perceptions surrounding housemates who were born or raised abroad.

She said comments from people who told her that contestants from abroad rarely win the show made her lower her expectations.

“It shows you that you have a chance. Coming into the show, if you guys heard it a lot of times, people were telling me that people who come from abroad don’t really win the show. You might not have a chance.”

According to her, the perception only strengthened her resolve to enjoy the experience and remain true to herself.

“So that dawned on me. So as I was hearing that, I was thinking, you know what? Might as well have my fun.

“Still, the show was called ‘Show Ya Sef’, so I might as well still show myself. So that’s what I did. And guess what? I still won,” she said.

Temi, who was born and raised in London before coming to Nigeria, said her victory should encourage young Nigerians who may feel that their background could prevent them from succeeding.

“If that is not determination to you guys, courage for you guys to do this, just do whatever you want to do. Do whatever you put your heart on. Keep doing what you need to do. Pray, everything. You’ll be sorted. You’ll be good,” she said.

‘70% was me, 30% the game’

Temi also addressed how much her behaviour in the house was part of a deliberate strategy.

According to her, much of what viewers saw was her personality, not a carefully constructed game plan.

“I would say maybe 30 per cent was a game, 70 per cent was actually me genuinely being curious,” she said.

She explained that she often asked questions in the house because she genuinely wanted to understand situations, rather than because she was deliberately creating a character for the cameras.

However, she admitted that she also understood the importance of not appearing too threatening to her fellow housemates.

“In the house, I didn’t want anyone to think I was a threat,” she said.

Temi said she sometimes doubted whether viewers would keep supporting her, especially because she believed she spent a lot of time sleeping and relaxing in the house.

“I really thought I was boring, I’m not going to lie. But guys, I was giving you guys quality content. But yeah, it doesn’t stop here. It only starts.

“I thought I was Sleeping Beauty,” she joked. “I thought I was sleeping a lot, waking up, going to the arena, sleeping again. I thought you guys hated that. But it seems like you guys were still finding something.”

Biggest moment

Asked which moment from her time in the house she would like to relive, Temi immediately pointed to her victory in the betPawa Friday Night Arena Game.

The 21-year-old said she entered the competition simply intending to participate and give her best, without expecting to win.

“I feel like that was my own bonus, and I felt amazing after that. I went, I screamed, I told everybody that I got them,” she said.

Temi said the experience helped change her perception of what she was capable of achieving in the house.

House relationships

Temi also reflected on the friendships and romantic situations that became part of her BBNaija story.

She identified Bluethopia, Bells, Shibi, Godessa and Araga among the housemates with whom she developed genuine connections, although she acknowledged that some friendships developed later in the competition.

She also addressed her much-discussed relationships with Barry, Kivo and Tram.

According to Temi, she initially found Barry attractive but stopped pursuing the connection after she felt he was not taking enough initiative in their conversations.

She said she was also attracted to Kivo when he entered the house but eventually became frustrated by what she described as his attempts to tell her what she should or should not do.

On Tram, whose relationship with Temi drew significant attention during the season, she said she was physically attracted to him but did not develop romantic feelings for him.

“I’ve been telling the people that I’m here for fun,” she said.

Beyond BBNaija

Temi said her immediate plans include returning to her studies and building a future around finance, while also exploring opportunities created by her new public profile.

She revealed that although her university studies are in the UK, she can complete the programme online.

“I do want to stay here for a minimum of two years. See what Africa has for me. See what Nigeria has for me. Build on that. And the sky’s the limit. I got good content, good vlogs,” she said.

Temi was crowned winner of Big Brother Naija Season 11 on Sunday, 4 October, after 70 days in the house. Her victory earned her the ₦160 million grand prize package, comprising ₦90 million in cash, a brand-new SUV and other sponsored prizes.

The ₦90 million cash component and the SUV were formally presented to her at the prize-giving ceremony in Lagos on Tuesday.

World.title: Russia 3-3 Nigeria: Late Akor Adams goal rescues Super Eagles
World.content:
The Super Eagles fought back from two goals down to secure a 3-3 draw against Russia in an entertaining international friendly at the Nizhny Novgorod Stadium on Tuesday.

Nigeria looked set for another disappointing result after Russia established a 3-1 lead early in the second half, but the Super Eagles produced a spirited late comeback to rescue a draw.

Kelechi Iheanacho put Nigeria ahead after 10 minutes, giving the Super Eagles an early advantage.

Russia responded through Lechi Sadulaev in the 30th minute before Matvey Kislyak completed the hosts’ turnaround with a goal in first-half stoppage time.

The hosts extended their advantage nine minutes into the second half when Aleksei Miranchuk found the net to make it 3-1.

Nigeria, however, refused to surrender and continued to push forward in search of a way back into the contest.

Their persistence paid off in the 78th minute when Peter Edokpolor reduced the deficit to 3-2, setting up a tense finish.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Super Eagles then completed their remarkable comeback deep into stoppage time when Akor Adams scored in the 94th minute to level the scores at 3-3.

The draw gives Nigeria a measure of redemption after their recent 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau and ends the international window with the Super Eagles showing character to recover from a difficult position.

Russia, who had entered the game on the back of a 6-0 victory over Namibia, will be disappointed to have surrendered their two-goal advantage.

For Nigeria coach Eric Chelle, the match provided another opportunity to assess his squad, while the late fightback offered encouragement ahead of the team’s next competitive assignments.

World.title: Kenya confirms first imported Ebola case linked to DRC outbreak
World.content:
Kenya has confirmed its first imported case of Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus, as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to spread across the region.

According to a statement published Tuesday by the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Office for Africa, the patient was a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the DRC and fell ill there.

The patient travelled by road to Kampala, Uganda, before flying to Nairobi, where the patient was isolated after developing symptoms. Samples tested positive for Bundibugyo virus at Kenya’s National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute.

Despite supportive care, the patient died on the night of 5 October and was buried on Tuesday in line with Kenya’s Ebola safe and dignified burial protocol, according to WHO.

“The government of Kenya notified WHO of the case in line with the International Health Regulations (2005) on 6 October 2026,” it noted.

Kenya becomes fourth country affected

According to WHO, Kenya is the fourth country to confirm a case of Bundibugyo virus disease in the current outbreak.

The DRC continues to battle the largest outbreak, while Uganda, where the virus was first detected in 2007, ended its latest outbreak in August. France also reported a travel-related case in June.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

WHO noted that most of the cases reported in Uganda were imported from the DRC, while a smaller number were locally acquired among contacts and health workers linked to imported cases.

In the DRC, the outbreak has continued to expand. As of 23 September, the country had recorded 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths, giving a case fatality ratio of 48.1 per cent.

The outbreak had affected 63 health zones across seven provinces, with two of the latest affected areas bordering other countries. WHO said the expansion had increased the risk of cross-border transmission.

Kenya traces contacts

Following confirmation of the case, Kenyan health authorities have listed 28 contacts, including family members and health workers who cared for the patient.

They are also tracing 23 passengers and four crew members who were on the same flight as the patient.

WHO said Kenya had been on high alert since May, when Ebola outbreaks were declared in the DRC and Uganda.

As of Tuesday, Kenya had screened more than 652,000 travellers entering the country, tested 267 suspected samples and trained about 5,000 health workers on Ebola prevention and management.

WHO said it has also supplied about 1,000 Ebola tests and 1,000 personal protective equipment kits to high-risk counties in Kenya.

Nigeria on high alert

Nigeria has also strengthened surveillance in response to the regional outbreak.

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said in a public health advisory issued in September that the country was on high alert and had activated enhanced surveillance measures.

It introduced a health declaration system under which travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola transmission may be required to complete a form before boarding.

The form requires travellers to provide information about their recent travel history, transit countries, destination in Nigeria and health status.

The NCDC said the measures are intended to strengthen surveillance and prevent the importation of Ebola into Nigeria.

World.title: Police commissioner in Bayelsa orders crackdown on cult groups
World.content:
Police Command in Bayelsa State has ordered intensified operations against cultism and cult-related violence across the state as part of efforts to sustain peace and prevent killings and reprisal attacks.

This is contained in a statement signed by the command spokesperson, Musa Muhammad, a deputy superintendent of police, on Monday.

The Commissioner of Police, Adewale Ajao, directed divisional police officers and tactical commanders to increase patrols in vulnerable areas, identify emerging threats and act promptly on credible intelligence concerning planned clashes, initiation ceremonies and recruitment activities.

The directive, according to the command, is part of renewed efforts to prevent killings, cult clashes and retaliatory attacks and to sustain peace across Bayelsa.

Mr Ajao directed police formations to increase patrols in flashpoint areas, strengthen intelligence gathering and act swiftly on credible information concerning planned cult clashes, initiation ceremonies and recruitment activities.

The commissioner also ordered closer engagement with community leaders and other stakeholders to enable the police detect emerging tensions before they escalate into violence.

The command warned cult groups contemplating attacks or reprisals that the police would pursue not only those who carry out such acts but also individuals who finance, organise or facilitate them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also declared that there would be “no sacred cows” in the ongoing crackdown, stressing that the law would be applied without regard to an individual’s status, influence or connections.

According to him, anyone reasonably suspected of organising, financing, facilitating or participating in cult-related crimes would be investigated, while suspects against whom sufficient evidence is established would be prosecuted before the appropriate court.

The police also drew the people’s attention to the Bayelsa State Secret Cults/Societies and Similar Activities (Prohibition) Law, 2012, as amended in 2018, which prohibits membership and sponsorship of secret cults and prescribes criminal penalties upon conviction.

The command warned residents against taking the law into their own hands following any cult-related attack.

READ ALSO: Police in Akwa Ibom probe alleged extortion of operatives by commanders

The police urged the public to avoid reprisal attacks, harbouring suspects and spreading unverified information capable of inflaming tensions.

“Parents and guardians are also advised to closely monitor their children and wards and warn them against being lured into cult groups.

The police called on residents, community leaders and other stakeholders to provide timely intelligence on planned attacks, recruitment drives, initiation ceremonies and other suspicious activities.

“The message from the Command is clear: report threats before they become bloodshed. Do not wait for violence to erupt before speaking up.

“Members of the public are encouraged to report suspicious activities or imminent threats to the nearest police station or contact the police command.”

(NAN)

World.title: Akwa Ibom approves N50,000 ‘wardrobe allowance’ for 20,000 teachers
World.content:
Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has approved N50,000 wardrobe allowance for each of the 20,000 teachers employed by the state government.

Mr Eno stated this on Monday during the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration in Uyo.

He said teachers must continue to appear neat and smart to inspire confidence among pupils and students in their various classrooms.

“I have approved another N50,000 per teacher as wardrobe allowance for all the 20,000 teachers employed by the Akwa Ibom Government.

“I have been briefed that there are 1,776 registered private schools. For each of those schools, they will receive the sum of N500,000 so that they can also spread love to their teachers,” Mr Eno said.

The governor expressed delight over the indelible contributions of resourceful teachers in the state, saying their efforts aligned with the administration’s ARISE agenda.

He described teachers as agents of change, wondering what the world would have become without them.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“A governor who leads a state like my humble self is leading well because a teacher once instilled the discipline and knowledge which we are now applying in leading the people.

“The same goes for the brilliant scientists, doctors and other professionals who help keep the chain of excellence moving smoothly. They were all taught by teachers,” he also said.

Mr Eno thanked the teachers for “endorsing” his candidacy, as well as that of President Bola Tinubu and Senate President Godswill Akpabio, for a second term in office come 2027.

“Together we will continue to deepen the depth of knowledge you instill in our children, the competitive spirit and the spirit of excellence.

“The trite saying has been that ‘teachers’ rewards are in heaven. No! Teachers’ rewards are here!

“Our belief and conviction is that your reward begins here on earth, and we have taken concrete steps to actualise those rewards,” Mr Eno said.

He said his administration had built and furnished 38 model primary schools, with at least one in each local government area of the state.

According to him, the state government have released N15 billion as a matching grant, and SUBEB has intervened in over 100 schools.

The governor also said that the administration had upheld free and compulsory education, including the payment of WAEC and NECO fees for 172,000 students from the state.

“We have approved the recruitment of 1,000 teachers before, and I have granted approval for another 2,000,” he added.

The governor advised qualified teachers to apply for the vacancies, take the Computer-Based Test and follow due process to be employed in line with civil service rules.

READ ALSO: Police in Akwa Ibom probe alleged extortion of operatives by commanders

Ubong Umoh, the commissioner for education, commended Governor Eno for transforming the school system through the construction of model primary schools.

“You are a leader who is leading progressively through continuity to ensure that there is a transformation in education in Akwa Ibom.

“You have already made a long stride towards the freedom of teachers, the teaching profession and the educational system. We are proud of you,” Mr Umoh, a professor, said.

Edet Emenyi, the chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Akwa Ibom Wing, thanked the governor for his interest in the welfare of teachers.

“Since I took office seven years ago, you are the first governor to personally come and honour the teachers in the state.

“In view of your friendly disposition towards teachers, we are endorsing you for a second term in office in the 2027 general elections,” Mr Emenyi said.

The NUT chairman appealed to the governor to do more for teachers in his second tenure and assured him of their continued support.

Akwa Ibom was in the spotlight recently following the poor performance of its students in public examinations. The state’s performance in 2026 NECO examination plunged from 12th nationally in 2025 to 36th, raising fresh questions about the implementation of its decade-long education roadmap, teacher interventions and spending priorities.

(NAN)

World.title: Libya’s parliament speaker ousted after 12 years
World.content:
Libya’s parliament speaker, a supporter of eastern strongman Khalifa Haftar, was ousted on Tuesday after 12 years in the post, in what experts said may be a sign of a shifting political balance.

MPs voted to replace Agila Saleh with Al-Salhin Abdelnabi al-Obeidi, the parliament’s spokesman announced on X.

Libya has been beset by violence and instability since the overthrow of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

It remains divided between the UN-recognised government in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, and a rival administration in the east backed by military commander Haftar.

Haftar’s camp relies in particular on the parliament, which sits in the eastern city of Benghazi under their control.

Saleh, 82, has long been considered a staunch ally of the Haftar clan, but he appeared to be weakened as Haftar’s sons, in particular Saddam Haftar, consolidated their positions.

Emadeddin Badi, an analyst at the London-based Chatham House, said: “Agila Saleh appears to be the latest casualty of Saddam Haftar’s drive to centralize decision-making in eastern Libya and bulldoze his way into a political role.”

His removal comes as a US initiative aimed at reviving the political process and unifying Libya’s institutions is under discussion.

World.title: Ondo Crash: ADC questions NAF aircraft maintenance funding
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has questioned the implementation of defence budgets for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft following Monday’s crash of an ATR-42 aircraft at Igbokoda, Ondo State.

The opposition party said the tragedy should not only prompt investigations into the immediate cause of the crash but also renewed scrutiny of how much money meant to keep military aircraft operational is actually released and spent.

In a statement released in Abuja on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the crash as tragic and unfortunate and expressed condolences to the families of the victims.

The party said official figures showed that as of December 2025, only N4.5 billion, representing about 13.98 per cent of the N34.71 billion budgeted for the maintenance of Nigerian Air Force aircraft, had been released.

By contrast, it said N20.74 billion was allocated for the maintenance of the Presidential Air Fleet, with N20.27 billion, representing 97.76 per cent, released within the same period.

“Put simply, while the fleet that serves a handful of people in power got almost every kobo it asked for, the fleet that serves and protects 200 million Nigerians was left with crumbs,” the ADC said.

The party stressed that it did not want to prejudice the ongoing investigation into the crash but said the incident provided another opportunity to examine the funding and maintenance of military equipment.

“While we do not intend to prejudice ongoing investigations into the cause of this tragic crash, we believe that this sad moment also provides an opportunity to raise, yet again, questions about the non-implementation of the defence budget and the perennial neglect of military equipment,” it said.

The ADC said the safety of military personnel should receive the same level of attention as the safety of political leaders.

“The safety of the President matters. But what also matters is the safety of the pilots and airmen who put their lives on the line in defence of the country. Patriotism does not replace spare parts, and condolence messages do not take the place of accountability,” the party maintained.

The party therefore called for the crash investigation to go beyond determining the immediate cause of the accident to examining the maintenance of defence equipment, particularly the Nigerian Air Force fleet.

It also demanded an audit of maintenance expenditure and budgetary releases to determine whether funds appropriated for the upkeep of military aircraft were released and properly utilised.

World.title: Go out, collect your PVC irrespective of who you want to vote — Makinde
World.content:
Gov Seyi Makinde

By Efe Onodjae

Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, has urged Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, ahead of the 2027 general elections, irrespective of their preferred candidates.

Makinde made the call in a short video shared on his official Instagram page, where he was seen displaying his PVC.

He said the voter card remained an important tool through which Nigerians could exercise their constitutional right to choose their leaders.

According to him, Nigerians should not allow their political preferences to discourage them from participating in the electoral process.

Makinde said: “Fellow Nigerians, INEC has said October 9, 2026, as the date for people to start collecting their PVC.

“This is your power, irrespective of who you want to vote for. Please go out, collect your PVC, and you will use it wisely in the 2027 election cycle.

“Thank you and God bless.”

World.title: Cristiano Ronaldo opens door for Portugal return, apologises for walk-out
World.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed his continued availability for Portugal after explaining his decision to leave the national team camp and accusing head coach Jorge Jesus of breaking an agreement over his playing time.

The 41-year-old Al Nassr forward had raised questions about his international future following his departure from the squad, but said he remained committed to representing Portugal.

“If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team,” Ronaldo said in a statement shared with Reuters.

Ronaldo also apologised to his teammates and the Portuguese public for leaving the camp, adding that he would accept any disciplinary action imposed by the Portuguese Football Federation.

The forward left the squad after remaining an unused substitute during Portugal’s 2-1 away victory over Norway in the Nations League on September 27.

According to Ronaldo, he and Jesus had previously agreed that he would miss the Norway and Denmark matches as part of a plan to manage his fitness.

However, Ronaldo said the coach changed the arrangement on the day of the Norway match and told him he would play for 30 minutes.

“Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from halftime onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” he said.

“The manager had broken his word to me.”

Ronaldo said it was the second time he believed Jesus had failed to honour an understanding between them and that the coach’s public comments did not correspond with their private discussion.

“It was the second time he had broken his word to me. I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises,” he said.

Jesus, however, denied after Portugal’s victory over Norway that he had reached such an agreement with Ronaldo, while leaving the door open for the veteran forward to return to the national team.

Ronaldo also rejected suggestions that he had interfered with tactical or technical decisions during his international career.

“Never, at any moment, have I interfered in any technical or tactical decision of any coach or national team manager in almost 25 years of career,” he said.

“I accept, for better or worse, what they propose that I do. I respect the decision, and when they break their word to me, I feel that my place is not there.”

Addressing speculation about a possible farewell to international football, Ronaldo said he expected to have one or more farewell matches in the future but remained focused on competing for Portugal.

“I can promise all my fans, naturally and especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches; there will be time for that. But when I think of the national team, what I really think of is competing,” he said.

Ronaldo, Portugal’s record goalscorer and most-capped player, has scored 146 goals in 234 international appearances.

He also recalled remaining with the Portugal squad following the death of his father during an international camp, saying his commitment to the national team had remained strong throughout his career.

The dispute between Ronaldo and Jesus has cast uncertainty over the forward’s immediate international involvement, but his latest statement makes clear that he intends to remain available for Portugal, subject to his fitness and any disciplinary sanction.

World.title: WADA seeks tough anti-doping stance from Kenya
World.content:
Kenya as future hosts of the World Athletics Championship must strive for zero tolerance for drugs in sport, the World Anti Doping Agency (WADA) boss said on Tuesday.

Despite a long-running doping crisis, Kenya were last month awarded the 2029 World Athletics Championships, the first time the event will be held in Africa.

“Kenya proudly calls itself the Home of Champions. But for that home to remain respected and credible, it must also be clean,” WADA chief Witold Banka said at the end of a three-day visit to the east African country.

“That is why Kenya needs a strong culture of clean sport, zero tolerance for doping, and a more determined approach to preventing and fighting doping.

“Kenya is a great sporting nation full of great athletes and you become, the more important area of sport when it comes to organising major sporting events.

“It’s a big honour for you but it’s a bigger responsibility as well and brings pressure and big requirements from our side as well”, Banka added.

Banka said that joint cooperation with Kenyan authorities would help lay the foundations for a cleaner sport.

“WADA or ADAK (Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya) alone cannot achieve its vision if we do not cooperate with those who have the power to go against those who are producing, smuggling and trafficking dangerous steroids to your athletes,” he said.

“We’ve found a common understanding and we are on the same track and there’s a clear goal within Kenya for zero tolerance for doping policy and it has to be established immediately with joint actions and a more aggressive approach to those who are destroying the image of the country and the reputation of the athletes.”

More than 140 Kenyan athletes, mainly long-distance runners, have been suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) since 2017.

World.title: ‘2026 is the new 1789’: French students take school anger to Paris streets
World.content:
TOPSHOT – Anti-riot police officers face protesting students carrying out blockading action outside the secondary school Le Corbusier, in Aubervilliers, northern Paris on October 1, 2026. Since late September, students have staged protests outside schools over grievances ranging from timetables, class sizes and a shortage of teachers to overheated classrooms during this year’s heatwaves. The protests started in the Ile-de-France region around Paris but have now spread to other cities nationwide. (Photo by LOU BENOIST / AFP via Getty Images)

As drums pounded and chants rang out, 16-year-old Yanis, flanked by a knot of friends, rattled off why he had joined tens of thousands surging through the streets of Paris on Tuesday to demand better learning conditions.

“There are no toilets, no toilet paper, everything is broken,” he said, his schoolmates nodding and chiming in.

“We go to class from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm with a one-hour break.”

“There are 36 of us in class. We can’t study,” the teenager from the northern Paris suburb of Sarcelles told AFP, calling conditions at his high school “unacceptable”.

He was among some 56,000 people who poured onto the streets of Paris on Tuesday as part of a protest movement that began in late September.

Across France, students and teachers have blocked the entrances to hundreds of high schools for 15- to 17-year-olds, protesting against teacher shortages, overloaded timetables, ill-equipped classrooms and buildings not designed to cope with rising temperatures.

On Tuesday, protesters flooded into the Place de la Republique in central Paris, hoisting signs.

“2026 is the new 1789,” declared one, a nod to the French Revolution.

Another placard took the form of an oversized middle finger.

The scent of merguez sausages — a fixture of French demonstrations — drifted through the square.

Demonstrators danced and clapped to pounding drums, breaking into chants calling for President Emmanuel Macron to resign and denouncing the far right ahead of presidential elections next year.

– ‘I don’t have a future’ –

But beneath the festive atmosphere, some of the young protesters struck a bleaker note.

Fidele, 15, who had come with Yanis, dreamt of becoming a lawyer but said conditions at his school had left him pessimistic about whether he could get there.

“When I see the system, I tell myself that I don’t have a future” in this country, he said.

Nearby, 16-year-old Noham had his sights set on becoming a computer engineer, but worried that overcrowded classrooms and teacher shortages were putting that ambition out of reach.

“Without access to an education, I can’t have the job I dream of,” he said. “It’s an enormous amount of stress.”

Nadine Zilliacus, an educator for 20 years, said she had seen the same disillusionment take hold among even younger pupils, who increasingly expressed a “really dark” view of what lies ahead.

“We tell them you have to prepare for the future with a job you like,” she said.

“Even in middle school they tell us: ‘There’s no point, anyway we won’t have jobs’.”

– ‘We’re neglected’ –

Further along the route, the crowd pressed towards the march’s endpoint, clapping and chanting before voices swelled into a rendition of the Marseillaise, France’s national anthem.

From a balcony overhead, a silver-haired woman leaned out to encourage the protesters below.

Spotting her, the crowd turned their faces upwards and broke into chants of “Mamie! Mamie!” — an affectionate French term for grandmother.

Among those making their way through the crowd was Ami, 17, who had travelled into Paris with a group of friends to protest against conditions at her high school in the city’s suburbs.

“Compared with schools in central Paris, we’re neglected,” she said.

As the march reached the Nation roundabout, the festive mood began to shift, with police carrying riot shields barring the route and some protesters throwing stones at the officers.

As Ami and her friends drew closer, the boom of tear gas canisters fired by police cut through the singing.

The girls screamed and stopped in their tracks, unsure whether to keep moving forward.

Nearby, a middle-aged woman had mascara streaking down her face after being caught in the tear gas, while a young man comforted her.

Ami said she did not understand the police response.

“We’re just protesting, we’re singing, and that’s all,” she said, adding that she was scared.

After a day of drums, chants and dancing through the capital, she was ready to leave.

“We just want to go home,” she said.
