World.title: Benue govt, PDP clash over threat to pull down billboards
World.content:
Gov Hyacinth Alia of Benue State

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The Benue State Government and the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have sharply disagreed over the planned removal of unauthorised billboards across the state, with the PDP alleging the exercise was politically motivated and targeted opposition campaign materials ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The state government, through the Benue State Signage and  Agency, Benue State Internal Revenue Service, BIRS, and the Urban Development Board, had on Tuesday issued a two-week ultimatum to owners and operators of unauthorised billboards to regularise them or face removal.

The directive, contained in a statement signed by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Chief Solomon Iorpev, said enforcement would commence on October 20, 2026, with the removal of every billboard that had not been regularised.

But the PDP, through its State Publicity Secretary, Bright Antyo, described the directive as “a desperate, anti-democratic and politically motivated attempt to cripple opposition campaigns ahead of the 2027 governorship election.”

The party urged the state government to abandon what it described as an attempt to intimidate political opponents and monopolise public spaces.

Explaining the government’s position, Iorpev said the relevant agencies had “observed with concern the arbitrary erection of billboards across the State by individuals, groups and political parties.”

According to him, “These structures have been put up without a permit from the Signage and  Agency, without clearance from the Urban Development Board, and without payment of the prescribed fees.”

“This practice breaches the law. It deprives the State of legitimate revenue, endangers public safety, and undermines the orderly development of our towns and cities,” he added.

The government, however, said it was giving billboard owners the opportunity to comply rather than immediately commence enforcement.

Iorpev explained that the authorities were “prepared to assume that many of those responsible acted out of ignorance of the law and not out of deliberate defiance. For this reason, the Agencies are giving everyone who has erected a billboard a grace period of two weeks, beginning today, Tuesday, 6th October 2026,” he said.

The commissioner urged owners and operators of unauthorised billboards to use the period to “retrace their steps and do the right thing” by approaching the Benue State Signage and  Agency to begin the permit process, obtain clearance from the Urban Development Board, and pay all required fees.

He warned that the deadline would not be extended saying “Let it be clear that there will not be another notice before enforcement which will commence on Tuesday, 20th October 2026. The enforcement teams are expected to begin removing every billboard that has not been regularised from the set date.

Billboards taken down will be at the owners’ cost, and no further notice will be given.

“Anyone who ignores this window should expect no sympathy and no exception, regardless of status, affiliation or political party. We are a law-abiding people, and we believe every Benue citizen wants to do the right thing. This grace period is a sign of the Government’s goodwill and of its preference for compliance over confrontation. We urge all concerned to make use of it,” the commissioner stated.

However, the PDP rejected the government’s explanation, arguing that the timing of the directive suggested a political motive.

In its reaction signed by Antyo, the opposition party said it had “noted with alarm the directive issued by the Benue State Government threatening to commence the removal of billboards and posters across the state from October 20, 2026.”

The PDP said it “condemns this action in the strongest possible terms” and described it as “a desperate, anti-democratic and politically motivated attempt to cripple opposition campaigns ahead of the 2027 governorship election.”

According to the party, opposition billboards carrying “messages of hope, security, economic revival and political change” had recently appeared in major towns and communities across the state.

It alleged that rather than address issues raised by residents, Governor Hyacinth Alia’s administration was attempting to intimidate political opponents.

“The sudden two-week ultimatum issued by the government is not a coincidence. It bears all the markings of a calculated operation aimed at clearing public spaces of opposition campaign materials and restricting the visibility of alternative political voices as the 2027 election approaches,” the PDP alleged.

The party questioned the timing and manner of the government’s proposed enforcement saying, “If the Alia administration was genuinely interested in enforcing signage laws, why did it wait until now?

“Why were these regulations not vigorously enforced before opposition campaigns began gaining traction? Why has the government suddenly become eager to dismantle structures carrying messages that challenge its record?” the PDP asked.

The PDP claimed the directive targeted political opponents, alleging that the administration was unsettled by what it described as growing dissatisfaction with the government and increasing acceptance of alternative political options ahead of the 2027 election.

The party further alleged that government institutions could be deployed against political opponents, describing the directive as “draconian, vindictive and dangerous for democracy.”

It said: “It creates the impression that government agencies are being mobilised, not for public service, but as instruments of political warfare against perceived opponents.”

The opposition party also warned the governor against what it described as an attempt to restrict political competition.

“Benue State is not a monarchy, and Governor Alia is not the only candidate who will participate in the 2027 election.

The people have a constitutional right to hear different voices, evaluate competing visions and make informed choices at the ballot box.”

The PDP argued that political contests should be determined by public confidence and performance, not by the visibility or removal of campaign materials.

“We remind the Governor that democracy is not sustained by pulling down opponents’ billboards and posters. Democracy is sustained by winning the trust of the people through good governance, accountability, transparency and tangible results.”

The party also used the controversy to raise several issues it said were confronting the state, including insecurity, the condition of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), abandoned projects, debt, infrastructure and the economic situation.

“Today, Benue people are asking hard questions about insecurity, the plight of IDPs abandoned projects, mounting debt, neglect of 22 local governments, deteriorating rural infrastructure and the worsening economic situation. Destroying opposition campaign materials will not make these questions disappear,” the PDP said.

The party therefore warned that “any selective removal of opposition campaign materials under the guise of enforcement will be interpreted as a direct attack on democratic freedoms and a dangerous abuse of state institutions for partisan purposes.”

It called on civil society organisations, election observers, the media, security agencies and other stakeholders to monitor the implementation of the directive.

“We call on civil society organisations, election observers, the media, security agencies and all defenders of democracy to closely monitor the excesses of Governor Alia and his administration and ensure that no government agency is used as a tool for political persecution,” the party said.

The PDP urged the state government to reverse course, saying, “The Governor must abandon this path of political intolerance. Any attempt to intimidate opponents, monopolise public space and create the illusion of an unchallenged political landscape will fail because democracy belongs to the people, not to those temporarily entrusted with power.

“Benue belongs to all the people. The democratic space belongs to everyone. No government has the right to reserve it for itself,” it stated.

World.title: Rival clubs demand title stripping, transfer bans for Man City
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Rival Premier League clubs are calling for Manchester City to face a range of punishments, including title stripping and transfer bans, if the club’s appeal against its financial breaches verdict fails, according to the BBC.

An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

City have appealed against the verdict.

However, sources told BBC Sport that a number of Premier League clubs want any eventual sanctions to cover both the period in which the breaches occurred and City’s future participation in the competition.

There is also a feeling in at least four Premier League boardrooms that a single points deduction resulting in relegation to the Championship would not be sufficient punishment given the scale of the findings.

One senior club source said City should be stripped of the titles they won during the period covered by the verdict.

The source added that there was “no great rush” among clubs to redistribute the trophies, but rather to take the honours away and leave them vacant.

The source warned that the credibility of the Premier League would be undermined if City were allowed to retain the eight major trophies they won during the period in which they were found guilty of the breaches.

However, BBC Sport said it had previously been told there was little appetite among some other clubs for City to be stripped of their titles, highlighting the differing views across the league.

On future sanctions, some Premier League figures believe a points deduction imposed in only one season would amount to a “bump in the road” for City, given the likelihood of the club returning to the top flight at the first opportunity.

As a result, some clubs believe any points deduction should be spread over multiple seasons.

There is also support in some quarters for transfer bans covering several windows, which could make it harder for City to rebuild and return to the Premier League quickly if they are relegated.

One club source described it as “bizarre, almost obtuse” if City were allowed to operate in the January transfer window while the process remained ongoing and sanctions had yet to be imposed.

Another proposal being discussed is a “tariff-based system”, under which City’s past league finishing positions could be adjusted through a points deduction.

Rival clubs could then receive compensation from City based on where they would have finished compared with their actual positions.

City have consistently maintained their innocence and are challenging the independent commission’s findings through an appeal.

Meanwhile, BBC Sport understands City manager Enzo Maresca will address his players collectively after they return from international duty on Thursday, ahead of Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool at Anfield.

The match will be City’s first since the verdict became public.

Merseyside Police said it had received queries about the fixture and confirmed it would have “an appropriate policing operation in place on the day”.

Liverpool sources told BBC Sport the club was treating the fixture as “business as usual”, with no additional measures planned.

One source said supporters had “the right to express their feelings” but hoped they would not overstep the mark.

World.title: Tinubu: Nigeria Has Witnessed Major Drop In Crude Oil Revenue Reliance
World.content:
.Vows to pursue energy transition suited to the nation’s needs, expand gas supply for power, industry

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday announced a massive drop in the nation’s reliance on crude revenues, signaling a decisive shift toward a diversified economy that his administration intends to push even further.

He noted that, driven by the Renewed Hope Agenda, the administration has built a diversified, high-growth economy—unlocking the potential of agriculture, manufacturing, and the digital and creative industries to shift the landscape away from single-sector dependence.

Speaking in Abuja during the fifth anniversary of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), the President, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, explained that through the joint effort of security agencies, operators, host communities, and the Commission, oil production is now steadier and stronger.

To thi end, he declared that investors who once abandoned Nigeria in search of better deals were now returning, a development, he said, has ranked the country first among Africa’s leading destinations for upstream investment for two years running.

Announcing a massive drop in oil revenue dependence, Tinubu said, “These gains matter well beyond the oil and gas industry. Under the Renewed Hope Agenda, we are building a diversified economy in which agriculture, manufacturing, the digital and creative industries all play their part.

“We have already reduced our dependence on oil revenue, and we intend to go further. But a diversified economy still needs energy, foreign exchange and investment, and that is where this sector serves the nation. Our gas can power homes and factories. Petroleum earnings support a stable naira and help fund the Federation.”

According to him, a well-run upstream industry is capable of creating jobs for Nigerian engineers, fabricators, and service companies, as his administration plans to use petroleum resources to build the wider economy, rather than depend on them.

He promised to “pursue an energy transition that is just and suited to Nigeria’s needs,” declaring that this is the decade of Gas.

“With the largest gas reserves in Africa, we will expand gas supply for power, industry and clean cooking, reduce flaring and methane emissions, and grow renewable energy alongside it. Nigeria will meet its climate responsibilities without sacrificing the development and energy access our people deserve.”

The President also vowed that his administration will not rest on its oars until Nigeria becomes the destination of choice for hydrocarbon investment, maintaining that in the next phase, the government will insist on compliance and accountability.

“Operators who enjoy incentives must deliver on their commitments to work programmes, local content, the environment and host communities, and the Commission must also account publicly for its own performance. We will uphold the rule of law and the sanctity of contracts, so that disputes are fewer and, where they arise, are resolved quickly and fairly,” he stated.

Identifying the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) as a strong foundation for the achievements recorded in the sector, Tinubu observed, however, that a foundation is only the beginning, as laws only set the rules, while investors decide on commercial terms.

He described his administration as “a listening government,” just as he said, “Investors told us plainly that good rules were not enough while costs remained high, contracting took too long and fiscal terms for complex projects were uncertain. We listened, and we acted.”

Noting that policy, no matter how sound, will achieve little rules it is implemented, the President noted that “the responsibility rests in large part with,” NUPRC, referring to the Commission as “the bridge between government policy and investment on the ground”.

He charged the Commission “to keep its processes clear and its timelines reliable, to work closely with sister agencies so that investors are not caught between overlapping requirements, and to remain firm, fair and independent in its decisions.”

“Acknowledging that five years was a short time in the life of any institution, President Tinubu applauded the NUPRC for using the period well, urging the Commission to “approach the next five years with the same commitment, integrity, and sense of purpose.”

Earlier in his speech, Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Oil, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, said NUPRC has recorded significant achievements in the last five years, attributing the progress to the leadership and reform agenda of the Tinubu administration.

According to him, Nigeria, with crude oil production of about 1.7 million barrels per day and over 37 billion barrels of oil reserves, still requires increased investment, additional licensing rounds, and intensified exploration to unlock the full potential of the nation’s petroleum resources.

The Minister urged the Commission to build on its successes by adopting decisive regulatory measures and eliminating bureaucratic bottlenecks that might discourage investment.

On his part, Chairman of the NUPRC Governing Board, Senator Magnus Abe, said the creation of the Commission under the PIA was evidence that Nigeria was making progress in reforming the oil and gas sector.

He credited the Commission’s success to President Tinubu’s dogged leadership and his decision to shield the regulator from political interference.

Abe commended the management and staff of NUPRC for what he called their exceptional commitment to transparency, professionalism and operational efficiency over the last five years.

Also speaking, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Gas, Senator Jarigbe Agom Jarigbe, said the reforms introduced through the PIA has improved transparency, regulatory certainty and investment inflows into Nigeria’s oil and gas sector.

He expressed the National Assembly’s satisfaction with the performance of the NUPRC as the upstream regulator, particularly its contribution to improving operational efficiency and creating greater certainty for investors.

Representing the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Gas, Ekperikpe Ekpo, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry, Mrs. Patience Oyekunle, said the establishment of the NUPRC under the PIA represents a significant transformation of Nigeria’s petroleum industry.

She explained that the clear separation of policy, commercial and regulatory responsibilities under the new framework had strengthened regulatory stability, with expectations of increased production and greater value for investments in the sector.

The Minister reiterated the Federal Government’s determination to maximise Nigeria’s vast gas resources and urged regulators to sustain efforts aimed at building trust and strengthening investor confidence through regulatory excellence.

The anniversary event also featured the presentation of awards to former Directors of the Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR), which was transformed into the NUPRC, in recognition of their contributions to reforms in the upstream petroleum sector.

World.title: EFCC Challenges Diezani’s Presentation of UK Court Judgment
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has challenged the move by former Minister of Petroleum, Diezani Alison-Madueke, to present court documents of a Southwark Crown Court judgment in London, United Kingdom, which recently discharged and acquitted her from corruption charges.

The anti-graft agency in a further counter-affidavit to Diezani’s request to present the UK favourable judgment is arguing that the purported acquittal of Diezani by a foreign criminal court was not material or relevant to the specific issues for determination before the instant court.

Recall that Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court, Abuja, had few months ago granted permission to Diezani present evidence of the London court judgment.

Recall also that the UK court had, on June 17, discharged and acquitted the ex-minister in respect of criminal allegations of bribery brought against her by the UK authorities.

Based on her acquittal, Diezani, in a suit filed before Justice Ekwo, sought to reclaim her assets forfeited to the Nigerian federal government following an order of court.

In the amended originating motion marked: FHC/ABJ/CS/21/2023, she sued the EFCC as sole respondent.

At the last adjourned date, Godwin Iyinbor had moved a motion seeking the court’s permission to file a further/supplementary affidavit for the purpose of bringing fresh and material development with respect to Diezani’s acquittal by the UK court.

After Mofesomo Oyetibo, SAN, did not raise objection to filing the application, the judge granted Iyinbor’s prayer.

Upon filing the further/supplementary affidavit, the EFCC then responded with a further counter-affidavit deposed to by Oyakhilome Ekienabor, a litigation officer in Oyetibo’s law firm, the EFCC opposed Diezani’s request to present the evidence.

When the case was called on Tuesday, Mrs Queen-Ubokutom Uwe, who appeared for Diezani, informed the court that the matter was slated for the hearing of the EFCC’s preliminary objection and their originating motion.

She, however, told the court that the commission had just served them with a motion prior to the commencement of hearing.

Uwe said the motion was the respondent’s further counter-affidavit to their further/supplementary affidavit.

She equally reminded the court of their motion to regularise their processes.

Responding, the court adjourned till November 11 for hearing of the motions.

The EFCC in its further counter-affidavit, dated and filed October 5, stated that some of the depositions in Diezani’s application were misleading, immaterial and irrelevant to the substantive issues for determination in her present suit.

“The proceedings before the Southwark Crown Court, London, United Kingdom, and the purported acquittal of the applicant therein, are in respect of a proceeding that is not being prosecuted before any Nigerian court and have nothing to do with the substantive suit before this honourable court.”

According to the litigation officer, there is nothing in the public sale notice indicating that any of the properties listed therein belong to the applicant (Diezani).

Ekienabor submitted that “the order for forfeiture relates exclusively to items of jewelry and does not extend to any other category of assets or properties.”

He argued that parties are not permitted to expand the scope of a matter before a court.

“The applicant’s further/supplementary affidavit introduces irrelevant facts into this suit, thereby diverting attention from the core issues before this honourable court,” he said.

He, therefore, prayed the court to discountenance Diezani’s further/supplementary affidavit seeking to present evidence of her acquittal in the UK court.

Diezani had in the 10-ground motion filed by Prof. Mike Ozekhome, challenged among other things, the public notice issued by the EFCC for the public auction/sale of properties and/or personal effects affecting her proprietary rights.

“A major plank of the applicant’s case before this honourable court is that the respondent had sought to visit the applicant with grave proprietary consequences without conviction, without fair hearing, and without strict compliance with the relevant statutory provisions regulating forfeiture, management and disposal of properties.”

The lawyer said Diezani had filed her amended originating motion on February 19, 2025, pursuant to the leave of the court granted on February 17, 2025.

“After the filing of the applicant’s processes and while this suit was still pending before this honourable court, a subsequent and material event occurred, to wit: the applicant was acquitted by the Southwark Crown Court, London, United Kingdom, on June 17, 2026, of criminal allegations of bribery brought against her, a proceeding of obvious material relevance to the allegations repeatedly referenced in relation to the applicant.

“The said subsequent development is material and relevant to the applicant’s case, particularly as it relates to the issues of absence of conviction, fair hearing, due process, propriety of irreversible proprietary deprivation, and the need for strict compliance with statutory safeguards before disposal of properties affecting the applicant’s proprietary rights.”

He said the ex-minister did not seek by this application to invite the court to sit on appeal over the said foreign decision or to treat same as automatically conclusive of the Nigerian proceedings.

He, however, said it was to place before the court subsequent material fact which would assist the court in doing substantial justice.

According to Ozekhome, the said fact was not available at the time the applicant filed her earlier processes and could not have been pleaded or deposed to earlier.

He submitted that the court had the power and discretion to allow a party to file the application where such facts would assist the court in the just determination of the issues before it.

While submitted that the commission would not be prejudiced by the grant of the application, he urged the court to grant the application in the interest of justice.

World.title: Tinubu to Review National Defence Framework, Evaluates Ongoing Operations
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has unveiled plans by his administration to review the national defence framework, evaluate the progress of ongoing counter-insurgency and anti-banditry operations, and align inter-agency security strategies to sustain peace and security across the nation.

Tinubu made this disclosure during a high-level strategic meeting with the Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), at the Presidential Residence in Lagos.

Speaking during the visit, President Tinubu expressed satisfaction with the steady progress recorded in securing vulnerable communities across Nigeria and reaffirmed his administration’s unwavering commitment to providing full support to the Ministry of Defence.

According to a statement by the Special Assistant on Media to the Minister of Defence, Leah Katung-Babatunde, the Minister provided a comprehensive briefing on current defence initiatives, frontline operational logistics and proposed reforms aimed at boosting troop morale, modernising military hardware capabilities and strengthening military infrastructure across all regions.

General Musa (Rtd) expressed gratitude to the President for his continuous guidance and support for the nation’s security apparatus, assuring the public that the Ministry of Defence remains resolute in executing its mandate with determination and integrity.

The meeting forms part of President Tinubu’s ongoing security briefings and policy alignment sessions with key government leaders, aimed at ensuring swift and decisive action against security and economic challenges nationwide.

World.title: Expert Tasks Nigerians on Healthy Eating Habits
World.content:
Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

A medical expert, Dr. Ademola Tosin Ojo, has urged Nigerians to embrace healthy and balanced eating habits, stressing that proper nutrition is essential to preventing diseases and maintaining overall wellbeing.

Ojo, while speaking on ‘Healthy Eating and Nutrition-Food as Medicine’, explained that a healthy diet should include vegetables, fruits, beans, fish, eggs, whole grains and other nutritious foods, while excessive salt, added sugars and unhealthy fats should be limited.

According to him, good nutrition supports energy, growth, immunity and normal body functions, while also helping to reduce the risk of conditions such as heart disease and type 2 diabetes.

He advised Nigerians not to completely eliminate carbohydrates from their diets, but to choose nutritious, high-fibre sources and maintain appropriate portions.

The medical expert also encouraged people to make water their main beverage and reduce their consumption of sugary drinks and highly processed foods.

Ojo noted that healthy eating does not have to be expensive, stressing that affordable locally available foods such as beans, seasonal vegetables, fruits and eggs can provide essential nutrients.

He further advised people living with hypertension and diabetes to adopt appropriate dietary habits while following the treatment plans prescribed by their healthcare professionals.

He then urged Nigerians to make healthy eating a lifestyle, summarising his message in three principles: eat a variety of nutritious foods, control portions, and limit excessive salt, added sugars, and unhealthy fats.

World.title: NGX Urges East African Investors to Key into Dangote’s Vision of Locally-sourced Capital
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

Chairman of the Nigeria Exchange Group (NGX), Alhaju Umaru Kwairanga, has urged East African investors to embrace the vision of billionaire industrialist, Alhaji Aliko Dangote, by largely relying on locally-sourced capital rather than expensive and unstable foreign loans.

Kwairanga spoke during a high-level investment engagement at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE), Kenya recently.

The NGX Group Chairman underlined the transformational impact of the Dangote Refinery in Nigeria, and expressed confidence that a similar one planned for Kenya will have the same positive impact on the whole of East Africa.

He is also taking that even further by relying to a large extent on locally sourced capital rather than expensive and fickle foreign loans.

He said: “We have already seen the transformational impact of the Dangote Refinery in Lagos Nigeria and I am confident that the one planned for Kenya will have the same positive impact on the whole of East Africa.

“He (Aliko Dangote) is also taking that even further by relying to a large extent on locally sourced capital rather than expensive and fickle foreign loans.

“I invite our East African investors to key into this vision and give leaders like this the capital and support to take Africa to another higher level of development.

“You will be making a good investment decision for yourself and for future generations of Africans.”

He recalled that in recent years, African leaders such as President William Ruto of Kenya and Nigeria’s President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, advocated for Africa to come together and work towards solving its developmental challenges.

That call, he noted, is being met in many practical ways by visionary entrepreneurs like Alhaji Dangote.

“In Nigeria, we have seen how he has led Nigeria’s turnaround from a cement importing nation to one that is self sufficient in cement and even exports the product.

“Now he is doing the same in fertilizer and petroleum products and spreading that vision of an industrialised African continent led by African visionaries across the continent,” he said.

World.title: FMC Yenagoa Seeks FG’s Intervention, Bemoans Non-release of Funds for Capital Projects,
World.content:
Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

The Medical Director of the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, Dr. James Enimi Omietimi, has raised concerns over the non-release of the centre’s 2025 capital allocation, saying the development has negatively impacted the progress of ongoing projects and the overall operations of the medical facility.

Omietimi, who made this known when he received the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC) team conducting physical verification of select Federal Government projects in the South-south region, particularly called for the timely release of capital allocations, to enable the institution complete its ongoing projects and provide effective healthcare services.

The FRC verification team, led by the Head of the Strategic Communication Directorate of the commission, Mr. Bede Ogueri Anyanwu, visited the FMC, Yenagoa, as part of the commission’s ongoing exercise to ascertain the level of implementation of some capital projects funded by the Federal Government.

According to a statement from the FRC,

Omietimi said the delay in the release of the 2025 capital funds had made it difficult for the centre to sustain the momentum of work on its ongoing projects.

The situation, he said, has also exposed the institution to operational challenges, making it increasingly difficult to provide the expected level of healthcare services to residents of Bayelsa State and neighbouring communities.

The statement quoted him as saying:

“We should not pretend because things have not been too good lately,” adding that the realities confronting healthcare institutions on the ground were sometimes different from what was being portrayed in the media.

He explained that the day-to-day realities of running a tertiary healthcare institution were demanding, noting that the centre had been struggling to keep the system functioning effectively amid the prevailing financial constraints.

Omietimi also expressed concern over the changing attitude of some residents towards orthodox medicine, noting that some patients now resort to traditional medicine practitioners before seeking professional medical attention.

He said many patients only return to FMC Yenagoa when their health conditions have deteriorated and require advanced medical intervention.

He appealed to the Federal Government to urgently intervene by ensuring adequate funding for the centre, particularly the timely release of capital allocations, to enable the institution complete its ongoing projects and provide effective healthcare services.

Earlier, the leader of the FRC verification team, Mr. Bede Ogueri Anyanwu, explained that the purpose of the exercise was to ascertain the extent to which funds appropriated and released for Federal Government projects were being utilised and to ensure that the projects deliver value to Nigerians.

Anyanwu said the exercise was part of the commission’s statutory responsibility of promoting transparency, accountability and prudent management of public funds, in line with the provisions of the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007.

He said that the presence of the FRC team at FMC Yenagoa was not intended to persecute the management of the centre or any government institution, but to establish the facts on the ground regarding the implementation of the selected projects.

“Our mission is to promote transparency, accountability and prudent management of public funds as contained in the mandate of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission and the Fiscal Responsibility Act, 2007,” Anyanwu said.

He added that the team was particularly interested in determining whether funds released for the projects had been appropriately utilised and whether the projects were achieving the intended objectives for which they were approved.

According to him, physical verification provides an opportunity for the commission to establish the actual status of projects, identify challenges affecting implementation and ensure that government investments translate into tangible benefits for citizens.

World.title: Senate Suspends National Security Summit Over NAF Crash
World.content:
• New date to be announced later

• Senate mourns fallen military personnel

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Senate has postponed indefinitely its planned two-day National Security Summit following the tragic crash of a Nigerian Air Force (NAF) ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, which claimed the lives of 25 officers and seven crew members.

The National Security Summit, originally scheduled for Monday, October 12, and Tuesday, October 13, was convened by the upper chamber to examine Nigeria’s worsening security challenges and develop practical measures to strengthen the protection of lives and property across the country.

The Leader of the Senate and Chairman of the Senate Ad hoc Committee on the National Security Summit, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, announced the postponement in a statement he personally signed on Tuesday in Abuja.

Bamidele said the decision followed the declaration of three days of national mourning by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in honour of the military personnel who died in the crash.

The president had also directed that the national flag be flown at half-mast nationwide as the country mourns the fallen officers and crew members.

Explaining the Senate’s decision, Bamidele said the summit had been fully planned after the completion of the zonal public hearings, but the tragedy involving the NAF aircraft made it necessary for the Senate to suspend the event.

“The Senate has resolved to defer the National Security Summit till further notice in honour of the victims of the tragic crash involving a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State,” he said.

The Senate Leader said the postponement was also in recognition of the gravity of the national tragedy and the period of mourning declared by the president.

He added that a fresh date for the summit would be announced in due course, urging stakeholders who had prepared to participate in the event to bear with the Senate.

The summit, according to the Senate, was designed to bring together key stakeholders to review Nigeria’s perennial security challenges and develop pragmatic recommendations capable of addressing threats to lives, property and national stability.

The upper chamber had already undertaken zonal public hearings as part of preparations for the summit, with the ad hoc committee concluding arrangements for the national gathering before Monday’s aircraft disaster.

Bamidele expressed the Senate’s condolences to President Tinubu, the Nigerian Armed Forces, particularly the Nigerian Air Force, and the families of the deceased personnel.

The Senate, he said, mourned the officers and crew members who “paid the supreme price in active service to the fatherland”.

The Senate Leader stated: “The Senate extends its heartfelt condolences to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR; the Nigerian Armed Forces, particularly the Nigerian Air Force; and the families of the gallant officers and crew members who paid the supreme price in active service to the fatherland.”

He appealed to all stakeholders who had been expected at the summit to take note of the national disaster and understand the decision to defer the meeting.

“We appeal to all stakeholders to take note of the national disaster and bear with the Senate during this period of national mourning,” Bamidele added.

The postponement means that the Senate’s planned national conversation on the country’s security challenges will now await a new date.

The summit was expected to provide an opportunity for federal and state authorities, security agencies, lawmakers, experts and other stakeholders to assess the country’s security architecture and propose measures for improving the safety of Nigerians.

No new date was announced in the statement, with the Senate saying the details would be communicated in due course.

World.title: 2027: Ex-Gov Bello Returns Home, Ready for Senatorial Election
World.content:
Ahead of the 2027 general election, the immediate-past Governor of Kogi State, Yahaya Bello, has relocated to Okene, the headquarters of Kogi Central senatorial district in preparation for the electoral battle ahead.

Bello, who returned home to a massive reception organised by the supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 Kogi Central senatorial election, expressed gratitude for the support.

The homecoming, which attracted a huge crowd across the district, was marked by colourful displays, chants, and enthusiastic supporters who trooped out in large numbers to welcome the former governor and APC senatorial candidate.

Bello, who governed Kogi State from 2016 to 2024, emerged as the APC candidate for the Kogi Central senatorial seat after winning the party’s May 2026 primary.

They enumerated some of the legacy projects of Bello when he governed the state, declaring that the senatorial hopeful is naturally loved by the residents of Kogi State many years after meritoriously completing his two terms in office.

Many stakeholders and residents across Kogi Central who led their constituents to welcome Bello vowed to further demonstrate their gratitude for the “good works” of the former governor by voting for him massively next year.

In his remarks, former Kogi State APC Chairman and Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Abdullahi Bello, described the reception as a demonstration of the affection and confidence the people of Kogi Central have for the former governor.

“This is the homecoming of a leader that liberated the whole Ebiraland, and we all trooped out to welcome him. It is not an easy thing. We love him, and we have to demonstrate that,” Abdullahi Bello said.

He declared that the APC structure in Kogi Central was fully prepared for the forthcoming election, stressing that the district remained a stronghold of the party.

“I will not flatter you with words, but obviously, as you can see for yourself, Ebiraland in Kogi Central is the home of the All Progressives Congress. APC is here. APC lives here; and we preach APC,” he said.

According to him, the massive crowd witnessed during the homecoming was not merely a political gathering but an indication of the level of acceptance he said Bello enjoys among the people.

He expressed confidence that APC members and supporters across the five local government areas of Kogi Central would mobilise behind Bello at the polls, saying: “APC is 100 per cent prepared to vote Alhaji Yahaya Adoza Bello to the Red Chamber next year.”

Bello’s emergence as the APC flag bearer followed a direct primary in which he was declared winner with 72,399 votes across the district.

He said: “The era of using professional influence or advantage, I think, is over. The law will put an end to that when you beat a candidate mercilessly with a very clear margin. Then I think you’ll learn some lessons, and that is going to happen in this election.”

Addressing the overwhelming crowd that welcomed the former governor, the former APC chairman said he was not surprised by the turnout, insisting that Bello’s political appeal cuts across age and gender.

“I am not surprised because Alhaji Bello has done so much to the extent that every Ebira person, both young and old, man and woman, believes so much in him. Even if you hear his name, you just have to join the queue,” he said.

He further claimed that the message of the APC campaign was already resonating with party members and supporters across the district.

The former chairman also linked the reception to what he described as the security situation in Kogi Central during Bello’s tenure as governor, recalling that the area had previously experienced episodes of violence and insecurity.

“Before now, especially 2007 and 2008, this district used to be a battlefield, with burning of houses and killing of innocent people. But the coming of Alhaji Yahaya Bello put an end to all that,” he said.

Responding, the former governor expressed happiness at the show of love by his people, describing the massive crowd that came to honour him as “organic” and proof that the sense of appreciation of the people of the state, especially in Kogi Central, is “inborn.”

Addressing journalists at the palace of the Ohinoyi of Ebira Land, Bello emphatically stated that all APC candidates for the 2027 general election would emerge victorious at the polls, saying: “I have never doubted that my people are with me and supporting the APC 100 percent. I have never doubted that my people will support and vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu 100 percent, and I have never doubted that my people are with my governor, Governor Ahmed Usman Ododo 100 percent.”

“I have never doubted that my people are going to vote for me as the senator representing Kogi Central and all of our other candidates on the platform of the APC because they know very well what this party has done to liberate our people and bring infrastructure to the people and ensure that the dividend of democracy is

delivered to our people and still being delivered to our people,” Bello pointed out.

Last Friday’s homecoming, according to stakeholders, provided a striking display of the mobilisation surrounding the former governor, with supporters turning out in large numbers to receive him as he formally reconnects with his political base ahead of the 2027 National Assembly election.

World.title: Tebello Motsoane’s father reflects on painful coincidence [video]
World.content:
Sylvester Motsoane, father of the late Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane, has reflected on how the anniversary of his wife’s passing painfully coincides with the murder trial of his son, which began on 5 October 2026.

Tebello’s mother, Rayhab Niniwe Motsoane, passed away in October 2023, just months after losing her son. The celebrity chef was fatally shot alongside rapper AKA in February 2023 in Durban.

Their untimely passing shook the nation, their families and the entertainment industry, as both men were regarded as trailblazers in their respective fields.



The trial is taking place at the Durban High Court, where seven accused are facing multiple charges, including two counts of murder, attempted murder, conspiracy to commit murder, and firearms and ammunition-related offenses.

TEBELLO MOTSOANE’S FATHER SPEAKS OUT

In an interview with eNCA, Sylvester Motsoane fondly reflected on the close bond Tebello shared with his wife.

“My son was close to my wife. They were like a team. I was like an outsider. Today is the worst day to remember my son because today, the 5th of October, is when my wife passed on, and it coincides with this court case, so that’s why I decided, no, maybe my son is watching over me somewhere, and my wife is watching from somewhere to see if I follow her son’s death (trial).

When asked, “What will justice look like to you?” he responded, “Justice is something that is very difficult to say because it’s in the hands of the judges,” he said.

“If they give good justice, I’ll be happy; if they don’t give good justice, I have no word. It’s out of my control, but I’d like to see them have penalty for whatever they’ve done,” he added.

Sylvester Motsoane, father of Tebello “Tibz” Motsoane, says October 5 marks three years since his wife’s passing – an anniversary that now coincides with the start of the long-awaited trial into the murders of Motsoane and rapper Kiernan “AKA” Forbes. Seven accused are facing a string of serious charges, including conspiracy to commit murder, two counts of murder, attempted murder, and firearms and ammunition offences. Tune in to #eNCA on #DStv403.  October 5, 2026

RAYHAB: ‘THE BEGINNING OF MY MISERY’

During an interview on Carte Blanche shortly after Tebello’s passing, his parents reflected on losing their son, with his mother saying:

“I felt numb. I couldn’t cry. [A] feeling of disbelief: ‘No, it can’t happen to Tebello.’ That was the beginning of my misery,” she said.

World.title: WATCH: Severe hailstorm batters Zimbabwe, damaging homes and vehicles
World.content:
Hailstorms cause extensive damage to homes, vehicles and other property. Image: AI illustration

A severe hailstorm tore through Masvingo in neighbouring Zimbabwe, damaging homes, vehicles and infrastructure and leaving some families in need of temporary shelter.

The storm struck on Monday evening, 5 October, bringing heavy rain, strong winds and large hailstones to parts of the city.

I am deeply saddened to hear that our people in Masvingo, in the south-eastern part of Zimbabwe, have been hit by a severe hailstorm.



I pray that there have been no fatalities and that the government will move quickly to assist those affected. If you have family or friends in… pic.twitter.com/cyFVR0OwtJ  October 5, 2026

Homes and vehicles damaged by severe hailstorm

Masvingo City Council said the storm caused extensive damage to homes, private property and critical city infrastructure.

Strong winds ripped roofs from some homes, while hail damaged windows, sliding gates, vehicle windscreens and solar panels.

Some families were left with their homes exposed to the weather following the storm.



The storm also uprooted trees and brought down power infrastructure in parts of Masvingo. Businesses in the city centre were also affected, with broken windows reported at shops and other buildings.

Flash flooding was also reported in several parts of the city after the heavy rain.

No injuries reported in early assessments

Speaking to NewZimbabwe.com, Civil Protection Unit chief director Nathan Nkomo said authorities initially received reports of damage to 60 households.



“We received calls that 60 households have been affected. The wind uprooted trees and a car was damaged in the process. No injuries have been recorded so far,” Nkomo said.

Authorities continued assessing the damage following the storm.

Temporary shelters opened

Masvingo City Council opened Mucheke Hall and Rujeko Hall to provide temporary shelter for families whose homes suffered severe damage.



The halls are also available for residents to store furniture and other household belongings while assessments continue.

Masvingo Mayor Aleck Tabe described the extent of the damage as “significant and deeply distressing”, adding that several families had been left with their homes exposed to the elements.

Tabe urged residents to remain cautious and help vulnerable members of the community, including children, older people, people with disabilities and families whose homes suffered severe damage.



Masvingo City Council and the Masvingo District Civil Protection Unit continued assessing the affected areas to determine the extent of the damage and the immediate needs of residents.

World.title: Clifton beach chaos: Booze, brawls and matric mob [videos]
World.content:
Clifton beach was the destination for thousands of underage youth last weekend. Images via TikTok

Police clamped down on unruly behaviour as thousands of minor beach-goers, many of whom were matric learners, descended on Camps Bay, Clifton and surrounding Cape Town beaches over the weekend.

According to city officials, five underage individuals were arrested for assault and driving under the influence, while dozens of fines were issued for drinking in public. Over 1000 units of alcohol was confiscated.

CLIFTON CHAOS: BOOZE AND BRAWLS TAKE OVER THE BEACH

According to reports, close to 4 000 underage youth descended on Clifton’s first through fourth beaches, as well as neighbouring Camps Bay and Maiden Cove, to celebrate the last weekend of the third term school holidays.



Much of the crowd were Matric learners who returned to their fourth and final school term this week.

Western Cape SAPS spokesperson Sergeant Wesley Twigg said that a 16-year-old had been arrested for driving under the influence. Four other minors were arrested for assaulting law enforcement personnel.

Twigg added that 64 fines were issued for alcohol-related offences whilst police confiscated around 1 000 units of alcohol.

Cape Town City Law Enforcement spokesperson Wayne Dyason stated that between 3 000 and 4 000 youth descended on the Clifton and surrounding beaches over the weekend.

The City was alerted to the planned youth gathering and had implemented a contingency plan that included City Law Enforcement, Metro Police, Traffic Services, and Camps Bay SAPS, who covered several popular beach areas along the Atlantic Seaboard.

Take a look at various videos taken over the weekend…



MATRIC SAFETY

Mayoral Committee Member for Safety and Security for the City of Cape Town J Smith, issues a stern warning to minors and matric learners following the Clifton Beach incidents over the weekend.

Smith urged the youth to be responsible during the outdoor social activity.

He shared on Facebook: “A little bit of ‘innocent fun’ can sometimes have lasting consequences. Don’t lose sight of the mission. Many matriculants are gathering at our beaches to celebrate reaching this final milestone with their friends. Make those memories ones you can look back on with pride, not regret.

“Alcohol is not permitted in our bathing areas.

“More importantly, alcohol impairs judgement, slows reaction times and can dramatically increase the risks associated with swimming, driving and other activities.

“Every year, too many lives are lost on our roads because of alcohol. So, if you encounter our enforcement officers on the beach and they confiscate alcohol, understand that it is about more than simply enforcing a by-law. It is about protecting you.

“You are the leaders, professionals, entrepreneurs, parents and citizens who will shape our city and our country tomorrow. We want you to get there”.

TEEN PRESUMED DROWNED AT CAMPS BAY

Meanwhile, the search continues for a teen boy who was swept out to sea at Camps Bay.

The 18-year-old from Mfuleni is presumed to have drowned after he disappeared in the surf in a strong rip current at Glen Beach over the weekend.

On Monday, 5 October, city officials confirmed that an 8-year-old had drowned in the Camps Bay tidal pools.

World.title: Police hunt suspect after deadly Ottosdal farm attack
World.content:
Parliament’s police committee chair Ian Cameron has called for stronger rural policing after the killing of Hannetjie van Zyl near Ottosdal. Image: Facebook/Ian Cameron

Parliament’s police committee chair Ian Cameron has condemned the killing of Hannetjie van Zyl, who died after an attack at Doornpan Farm outside Ottosdal.

Police are investigating murder after officers responded to a complaint of a possible farm attack on Monday evening, 5 October.

Van Zyl, 55, was attacked while opening a gate at the property.



Her husband rushed her towards hospital in Klerksdorp, but she later died from her injuries.

Cameron calls for action

Cameron said Van Zyl was attacked shortly after 19:00 when she stopped to open the gate.

He said information circulated by the local emergency network indicated she was struck over the head by her attacker or attackers before being rushed to hospital.

“A woman went home, stopped to open a farm gate, and was attacked and killed,” Cameron said.

He said rural communities should not be expected to accept violent crime as part of daily life.

Cameron called for stronger rural policing, better crime intelligence, properly resourced detectives and functioning rural safety structures.



“Those responsible for attacks like this must be identified, arrested and successfully prosecuted,” he said.

He also extended his condolences to Van Zyl’s family, friends and the farming community.

Cameron currently serves as chairperson of Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Police.

SAPS hunts attacker

SAPS confirmed that officers received a complaint of a possible farm attack and went to Doornpan Farm.

Police spokesperson Sergeant Kelebogile Morake said Van Zyl had already been transported to hospital by the time officers arrived.

Police said she was allegedly stabbed with an unknown object while trying to open the gate.

No suspects had been arrested.

“Police investigations are continuing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and to identify and apprehend the suspect or suspects,” Morake said.

Couple targeted before

The Van Zyls had reportedly faced violence at the same property before.

According to a report, Sarel and Hannetjie van Zyl were attacked on the farm in July 2020.

Three suspects were arrested following that incident.

Police have not indicated that the earlier attack is linked to Van Zyl’s murder.

The latest investigation continues.

World.title: CheckPoint Podcast | Are We Raising Boys For Violence? Prof Malose Langa On How Masculinity Is Made
World.content:
Violence Prevention Starts Long Before The Police Station

South Africa often talks about violence at the moment it becomes visible: after an assault, a murder, an arrest or another national outcry. By then, however, the story may already be years in the making.

That is one of the more uncomfortable implications of psychologist Professor Malose Langa's work with boys growing up in Alexandra. His research did not begin by asking which boys would become violent. It asked what it meant to be a boy, and then listened closely enough to discover that the answer changed depending on who was in the room.

Individually, boys could express relatively progressive ideas. In groups, Langa found that some shifted towards familiar masculine expectations: toughness, multiple girlfriends, fighting and other performances of what a boy was supposedly meant to be. He describes this tension as a difference between a public and private script. Beneath the bravado, he encountered shame, uncertainty, vulnerability and the emotional cost of trying to perform an approved version of masculinity.

That finding matters because it moves the violence conversation upstream.

If masculinity is partly learned, reinforced and policed socially, prevention cannot begin only when someone reaches the criminal justice system. Langa points instead towards the institutions surrounding children much earlier: homes, schools, churches, streets and early childhood development spaces. His argument is not that these institutions mechanically produce violent men. It is that everyday messages about strength, fearlessness, gender and acceptable behaviour accumulate long before society encounters their possible consequences.

South Africa's own policy architecture increasingly recognises that prevention must be broader than policing. The National Strategic Plan on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide includes prevention and rebuilding social cohesion as one of its central pillars, while a Cabinet-approved Programme of Action has called for greater engagement with men and boys to challenge harmful norms.

The problem, then, is not simply recognising prevention as important. It is turning that recognition into sustained practice.

There is evidence that this can work. Langa refers to Stepping Stones, an intervention evaluated by the South African Medical Research Council, as an example of programmes that created spaces for young people to discuss relationships, gender, sexuality and violence. SAMRC reporting on the intervention found changes in young men's sexual practices and violence perpetration, while cautioning that further research remained necessary.

Langa's own research offers another lesson: boys cannot be reduced to the worst stereotype available to describe them. His earlier academic work with 32 adolescent boys in Alexandra found multiple and sometimes contradictory masculinities, including boys simultaneously complying with and resisting dominant masculine norms. Wits University later summarised his decade-long work as a challenge to the homogenised portrayal of young black men as inherently violent or destructive.

This does not minimise violence or excuse perpetrators. It changes the prevention question.

Instead of asking only how to punish violence after it occurs, institutions also need to ask what they reward, tolerate and teach before it occurs. What does a five-year-old learn about being a boy? What behaviour wins approval at school? Which emotions are permitted among friends? Which versions of manhood are celebrated in communities and popular culture? And where can boys practise something different without being humiliated for it?

Late in his CheckPoint conversation with Nkepile Mabuse, Langa's frustration shifts from individual behaviour to institutional implementation. Researchers, he argues, repeatedly produce findings and examples of interventions, yet the country can behave during every new crisis as though no answers exist.

That may be the larger accountability question. South Africa has invested heavily in understanding violence. The next test is whether institutions can become as serious about preventing its social production as they are about responding once the damage has already been done.

References

· Malose Langa, Becoming a man: exploring multiple voices of masculinity amongst a group of young adolescent boys in Alexandra Township, South Africa, University of the Witwatersrand.

· South African Medical Research Council, Stepping Stones evaluation.

· South African Government, National Strategic Plan on Gender-Based Violence and Femicide and Programme of Action on GBVF.

· CheckPoint: The Podcast, interview with Prof Malose Langa, 6 October 2026.

World.title: Number Of The Day | R6.4 million | 06 October 2026
World.content:
What Does A R6.4 Million Cow Actually Buy You?

A cow selling for R6.4 million sounds almost impossible to reconcile with ordinary agricultural economics. But Queen Arusha is not an ordinary cow, and understanding why someone would pay millions for her requires looking beyond the animal standing in the auction ring.

The Ankole heifer comes from Ntaba Nyoni, the cattle operation owned by President Cyril Ramaphosa. Her multimillion-rand sale provides a window into a specialist part of agriculture in which the value of an animal can lie as much in what it may reproduce as in the animal itself.

When The Product Is Genetics

For commercial cattle farmers, value can be closely connected to familiar outputs: meat, milk, fertility, weight gain and the efficiency with which animals turn feed into something that can be sold. Elite breeding introduces another commodity: genetics.

Queen Arusha's family illustrates the economics. Her brother, the Ankole bull Optimus Prime, also featured in the conversation between Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd on Number of the Day. Sexed semen from the bull reportedly sold for R250,000 a straw.

That changes the way a valuable breeding animal should be understood. A buyer is not necessarily spending millions for the economic output of one cow. The investment can include the offspring she may produce, embryos carrying sought-after genetics and the possibility of extending a prized bloodline across future generations.

Edwards compared the market with thoroughbred horse breeding, where the value attached to lineage can vastly exceed the immediate productive value of an individual animal. As he put it, buyers are purchasing “the lineage”, “the genetics” and “future generations”.

Modern reproductive technology can multiply that potential. Herd pointed to the cattle equivalent of assisted reproduction: embryos can allow valuable genetics to be reproduced beyond what would be possible through a cow's natural calving cycle alone.

The R6.4 million price therefore represents something more complicated than the purchase of livestock. It is a wager on future genetic value.

Scarcity Can Become An Asset

That also introduces risk.

An extraordinary auction price does not guarantee an extraordinary return. Breeding outcomes are uncertain, reproductive programmes cost money and the future value of offspring depends on buyers continuing to prize a particular lineage and breed.

Scarcity matters too. When desirable genetics are difficult to obtain, buyers may be prepared to pay a premium to enter that bloodline. As those genetics spread through breeding programmes, however, the economics can change.

This makes elite cattle breeding an unusual combination of agriculture, biological inheritance and asset valuation. The physical animal matters, but so does the market's belief about what that animal could produce tomorrow.

When The Farmer Is Also The President

Queen Arusha carries another dimension that most multimillion-rand cattle do not: the operation that sold her belongs to South Africa's sitting president.

That inevitably returns attention to Phala Phala, where the theft of foreign currency linked to a buffalo transaction triggered years of political and legal controversy. In the podcast discussion, Edwards raised the question that follows naturally from Queen Arusha's sale: how much involvement may a sitting president have in private business interests?

The distinction matters. Ownership of an economic interest is not automatically the same thing as personally performing paid work for that business. Herd described the position advanced by Ramaphosa's lawyers as being that his farming interests constitute business interests rather than prohibited paid work.

That question should not be collapsed into an assumption that Ramaphosa personally received R6.4 million from Queen Arusha's sale. An auction price is business revenue, not automatically the owner's personal income or profit. Nor does ownership by itself establish that the President manages the operation day to day.

Yet the scale of the transaction explains why the distinction attracts public attention. Queen Arusha is not merely evidence that unusual cattle can command unusual prices. Her sale demonstrates that the President retains an interest in an agricultural operation dealing in potentially very valuable assets.

That leaves two very different questions standing side by side. Agricultural economics asks how a cow can become worth R6.4 million. Democratic governance asks how a country should manage significant private economic interests when their ultimate owner occupies its most powerful public office.

One remarkable animal manages to illuminate both.

World.title: To hike taxi fare or not to hike? Industry in talks amid fuel price pressure
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - This week taxi operators are mulling over one big question; this is to hike taxi fare or not to hike taxi fare?

It comes amid the latest announcement of fuel price increases, which are set to kick in at midnight.

SANTACO national spokesperson Rebecca Phala said they find themselves in a difficult position.

While they have to navigate the fuel price hike that continues to add pressure on taxi operators, they also need to consider commuters, whose household budgets she said are already stretched.

Taking this into account, Phala said they have to be "incredibly careful to strike some sort of balance despite the difficult circumstances".

READ | Govt warns against panic buying as record fuel prices take effect

According to Phala, the taxi association has not yet made a decision on whether or not to hike fare prices, but those conversations are already underway.

“There are a number of things that we want to exhaust from our end. We'll be engaging with the leadership of all provinces tomorrow. “So far, though, the national office bearers, which is the highest decision-making body, have already decided to say, we are going to engage with those in the fuel sector, because the industry does have buying power, considering the number of vehicles that we have and the consumption that we do to fuel. But we're also going to engage with the government.”

With engagements with relevant sectors taking place, Phala said they will have a decision by Thursday at the very least.

READ | Fuel price increase could push up cost of goods, freight industry warns

“The reason why we're not immediately announcing whether we'll be increasing fares or not is that we know that our commuters complained already. I mean, since March, when these increases started to be announced, we've only ever increased once, and they were already complaining about that.

World.title: 'We are struggling with population expansion' - Joburg Water
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg Water has partly blamed Ebony Park residents for years of erratic water supply.

The Johannesburg community has had intermittent water flow for three years.

This has made them suspicious that the problem is manufactured for financial gain.

But Johannesburg Water spokesperson Nombuso Shabalala said water challenges are not only bound to Ebony Park.

She said similar issues are also witnessed in Kaalfontein and the greater Ivory Park.

READ | Joburg inner-city power outages leave thousands without water

According to Shabalala, this is because the system that supplies these areas, which is President Park Reservoir and Tower, is highly constrained, leaving the water utility to resort to throttling daily in order to build capacity.

“We throttle the system every day at two o'clock, and we open it again at four o'clock the following morning. This is so that the reservoir is not completely depleted.

World.title: Rand holds steady
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Rand may be getting its mojo back.

The currency has strengthened more than half a per cent against the US dollar.

After showing resilience during most of the war in the Middle East, expectations of higher interest rates had placed the currency under pressure.

READ | Rand falls to weakest level in two months

The Rand was trading close to R16.70 to the dollar at the start of October, its lowest level since late July.

But in recent days, it has regained ground and today strengthened to below R16.50 to the dollar.

A weekly auction of government debt spurred on the currency, attracting the strongest demand in four months.
