World.title: High Court to hold voir dire in David Lambey murder case over disputed police statements
World.content:
High Court to hold voir dire in David Lambey murder case over disputed police statements

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The High Court is expected to conduct a voir dire in the murder case against 20-year-old David Gill Lambey, as his attorney challenges the admissibility of statements he allegedly gave to police following the December 2023 killing of San Pedro bartender Irvin Enderson Martinez.

Lambey appeared before Justice Candace Nanton on Thursday as preparations continue for his murder trial, which is scheduled to begin on February 9, 2027.

The defense is challenging alleged notes of interview and a caution statement attributed to Lambey, contending that they were obtained under duress and were not given voluntarily.

Justice Nanton is expected to hear arguments from the defense and prosecution during a voir dire — a hearing held to determine whether contested evidence can be admitted at trial — before delivering a ruling.

The matter was adjourned until December 1, 2026, when the voir dire is expected to commence. Lambey remains on remand at the Belize Central Prison.

Lambey was 18 when he was charged with the murder of 28-year-old Martinez, who was fatally stabbed on December 15, 2023, at the Mahogany Bay Village Resort compound south of San Pedro Town.

BBN reported at the time that Martinez, a bartender at the resort, was walking home with his common-law wife when an altercation occurred involving Lambey and three other men. Police alleged that Martinez suffered a fatal stab wound during the confrontation.

Lambey was charged with murder, while Zephaniah Mariano, Zechariah Mariano and Keyron Lambey were charged with aggravated assault in connection with the incident.

Martinez was rushed to the Dr. Otto Rodriguez San Pedro Polyclinic II, where he was pronounced dead shortly after the incident.

Lambey has been before the High Court several times as the case proceeds toward trial, including an appearance earlier this year before Justice Nanton.

World.title: Belize hosts regional cybercrime training for police officers
World.content:
Belize hosts regional cybercrime training for police officers

By Zoila Palma: Today, Police representatives from Belize, Curaçao, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Barbados, Aruba, Suriname, and Jamaica gathered for a cybercrime training workshop.

The workshop hosted in Belize was led by the Presidential Agency for International Cooperation of Colombia (ACP Colombia) and the Colombian National Police.

The forum, called “Successful Strategies and Experiences Combating Cybercrime,” gives investigators from these countries a chance to share ideas on how to stop criminals who use the internet and technology to target unsuspecting people.

Participants are also looking forward to networking, as they recognize that tackling these complex digital security issues requires cooperation beyond any single country or agency.

World.title: Prime Minister confident for 2027 Municipal elections; says PUP continues to “Serve the People”
World.content:
Prime Minister confident for 2027 Municipal elections; says PUP continues to “Serve the People”

By Zoila Palma: During the Open Your Eyes Morning show today, Prime Minister John Briceno expressed confidence for the PUP as it nears the 2027 Municipal elections.

“We are excited about our candidates. I believe we have a good team of mayoral and councilor candidates. We have been generally successful in all municipalities with the exception of San Ignacio and Santa Elena that we don’t control.

And we believe, I firmly believe that at the end of the day they will be looking at us once again to continue to lead in municipal elections for municipalities across Belize,” the PM said.

The Prime Minister said that he had planned to retire but is now focused on his legacy and a succession plan for the next PUP leader.

“What is it I want to leave behind, in 2020, they (UDP) had their worse defeat in history and they can’t put it back together yet they are still fighting among themselves.

I don’t want to have that legacy that I leave my party in shambles. So, if I have to stay back some more years to help plan out a good succession plan then I am prepared to do so provided that the people support,” he added.

The PM said that the PUP remains connected to the people and continues the mantra of “Serve the People.”

“I walk the streets, people greeting me, taking pictures, that gives you a sample of what people feel. Yes, we have issues like every family but what binds us is that of serving the people. That is our mantra, to serve and its in our DNA, the issue of social justice. If you do not believe in social justice, you can’t be a PUP,” the PM said.

World.title: PM says Tropic Air’s decision driven by financial losses on route
World.content:
PM says Tropic Air’s decision driven by financial losses on route

By Zoila Palma: Today, on Open Your Eyes, Prime Minister John Briceno said that the decision by Tropic Air to discontinue flights to Punta Gorda Town commencing November 1, 2026 was a decision driven by financial losses.

“The decision done by Tropic is simply a financial one. He is telling me that the cost continues to go up and there is not enough traffic. Truth of the matter is as he pointed out to me, they are losing half a million dollars on that run, to Punta Gorda.

It’s unfortunate that he tied it up with other issues, we have a responsibility to make sure that the runways are safe so we were going to upgrade that runway, he would benefit from it because then the runway would be smoother,” the PM explained.

The PM said that upgrades are necessary and would be done to ensure safety.

“Also, he was mentioning the issue of the $10 security fee. Times change and we are going to put in security so who is going to pay for that. And then we didn’t even start to implement, we were going to $6 in June of next year so we didn’t even start to implement.

I will sit down and talk with him and see if there is anything that can be worked out like with the buses we have to give some kind of fuel subsidy,” the PM added.

World.title: Honduran woman pays $1,000 fine for overstaying 20-day permit; Remanded to prison awaiting deportation
World.content:
Honduran woman pays $1,000 fine for overstaying 20-day permit; Remanded to prison awaiting deportation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 39-year-old Honduran woman who had been living in Crooked Tree was fined $1,005 and ordered removed from Belize after pleading guilty to failing to comply with the conditions of her visitor’s permit.

Jessica Carolina Sarmiento Pineda appeared unrepresented before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Monday, where she was charged with one count of failure to comply with the conditions of a visitor’s permit.

According to the prosecution, Pineda entered Belize on May 6, 2026, and was granted permission to remain in the country for 20 days. She did not leave Belize within that period or obtain an extension of her stay and subsequently continued residing in Crooked Tree Village.

After the charge was explained to her in court, Pineda pleaded guilty.

As a first-time offender, she was fined $1,000 plus $5 in court costs. The fine was ordered paid forthwith, with three months’ imprisonment in default.

Pineda was able to pay the fine, avoiding the default prison sentence; however, the court also issued a removal order requiring her to be sent back to Honduras.

She was remanded to the Belize Central Prison pending her removal from the country, which is expected by the end of the week.

Belizean courts have previously dealt with similar immigration offences involving visitors who remain in the country beyond the period authorized by their permits, with offenders subject to fines and eventual removal from Belize.

World.title: PM: Ministries can access SmartStream accounts, but must remain accountable
World.content:
PM: Ministries can access SmartStream accounts, but must remain accountable

By Zoila Palma: Earlier this year, information was leaked about vendors in the Smart Stream accounts within the Government’s procurement system.

While, the leaks revealed a pattern within the Ministry of Defence, there could also be concern of other vendors that supply the Government with different items across the Ministries.

On Open Your Eyes morning show today, Prime Minister John Briceno explained that in the Smart stream system, now, the Ministries have access to their own Ministries Smart stream accounts.

“When you start to release any and everything just to undermine, I don’t think that’s fair game, more importantly in every organization, we need better mechanisms in place.

The point is we also have a responsibility to manage the monies as best as possible but that doesn’t allow to leak and undermine Government. People from health have access to health and Agriculture have access to agriculture,” the PM explained.

The PM said that now, the Government is putting in place an internal auditor to audit the ministries and more checks and balances within the system to ensure that government is ran open and transparent.

World.title: Radar data confirms Guatemalan military plane entered Belize airspace
World.content:
Radar data confirms Guatemalan military plane entered Belize airspace

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Government of Belize says radar data confirms that a Guatemalan military reconnaissance aircraft entered Belizean airspace without permission on September 24.

Prime Minister John Briceño chaired an extraordinary meeting of the National Security Council on Monday, October 5, to review the incident.

According to Government, primary and secondary radar data showed a Guatemalan Armed Forces aircraft, tail number FAG706, entering Belize’s airspace from the east at 7:29pm, flying at 4,000 feet.

At 8:07pm, the aircraft allegedly switched off its transponder to avoid detection by secondary radar. Three minutes later, at 8:10pm, Belize’s primary radar picked it up again.

The aircraft then flew southwest, passing close to Punta Ycacos in the Toledo District, before leaving Belizean airspace at about 8:40pm.

In total, the plane was in Belizean airspace for roughly 1 hour and 10 minutes.

Government says the flight took place during a regional counternarcotics operation that did not include Belize.

The findings stand in contrast to last week’s comments from Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo, who denied that any incursion took place and said the initial report came from a teenager using an app.

World.title: 11-y-o among two killed in Denham Town house fire
World.content:
File photo

KINGSTON, Jamaica — An 11-year-old boy was among two people killed in a house fire along North Street in Kingston early Tuesday morning.

The deceased have been identified as 11-year-old Jaydon Whyte and 60-year-old Junior Barrett.

According to the Denham Town police, lawmen were alerted to a fire in the area about midnight.

Members of the Jamaica Fire Brigade extinguished the blaze and conducted cooling-down operations. The charred remains of Whyte and Barrett were subsequently discovered inside the home.

Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the fire and the deaths.

World.title: Reggae Boyz book ticket to quarterfinals of Nations League
World.content:
Jamaica's forward #11 Tyreece Campbell celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Concacaf Nations League Cup football match between Honduras and Jamaica at the Nacional Chelato Ucles stadium in Tegucigalpa on October 5, 2026. (Photo: AFP)

Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz have advanced to the quarterfinals of the Concacaf Nations League after a 1-1 draw with Honduras at Estadio Nacional Chelato Ucles in Tegucigalpa on Monday.

The draw saw Jamaica finish second in Group B of League A on seven points, the same as group winners Guatemala and third-placed Suriname, with goal-difference separating the teams.

The point was also good enough for Honduras to avoid relegation to League B.

Tyreece Campbell scored his first goal in Jamaica’s colours when he fired home in the 27th minute, curling a ball from the left side of the Honduran 18-yard box and off the inside of the far right upright.

Luis Palma equalised for the hosts with a goal of supreme quality, beating goalkeeper Andre Blake with a looping, curling shot from at least 30 yards out, the ball nestling in the far right corner.

Jamaica missed a number of other good scoring chances.

Javon East, the two-goal hero against El Salvador on Friday, had arguably the best opportunity to score with just the goalkeeper to beat on a breakaway late in the first half, but shot wide of the goal.

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Doctors pleased
World.content:
TRADE unionist Senator Lambert Brown says doctors have welcomed the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) ruling on emergency duty payments, urging the Government to comply with the award and work out a disbursement plan with the Jamaica Medical Doctors’ Association (JMDA).

“We are pleased, the doctors are pleased, and we know that the panel was unanimous in respect to the overtime rate,” Brown told the Jamaica Observer on Monday.

Brown, who represents the JMDA in the dispute, was responding to the IDT’s October 5 ruling which ordered a new framework for emergency duty payments and rejected the Government’s proposal to place doctors under a standardised Extra Hours Worked (EHW) system.

The tribunal ordered that the new Emergency Duty Allowance (EDA) rates be based on the JMDA’s March 15, 2024 cost-reduction proposal, with some adjustments, and that the payments be applied retroactively from April 1, 2023.

The ruling also ordered the reinstatement of the incentive allowance for eligible medical officers from

April 1, 2023. Tribunal member Berita Locke, JP, dissented on that aspect of the award, while Chairman Dr Noel Cowell and member Beatrice Rhoden formed the majority.

Brown said the focus must now shift to implementing the award.

“I hope the Government will comply with the ruling of the IDT and will sit down with the doctors and work out a payment schedule, a payment plan to effect their award… the doctors have been suffering for too long, it’s time to put an end to this dispute. Forty-two months is too long,” he said.

Minister of Labour and Social Security Pearnel Charles Jr, in his response to the ruling, said the ministry has acknowledged the tribunal’s decision and would continue to focus on maintaining stable industrial relations.

The dispute centred on whether junior doctors should be placed under the Government’s standardised EHW policy or continue under a system that recognises the different types of emergency duties they perform.

The Government’s EHW policy was designed to establish a standard overtime system across the public service. Under the policy, overtime was generally paid at 1.5 times the normal rate for the first day and twice the rate for the second day and public holidays.

The policy also included a 15-hour weekly limit on extra hours worked, with an exception where an employee was unavoidably required to work beyond that limit to achieve a clearly defined objective and permission was obtained from the appropriate senior official.

The JMDA argued that the arrangement was unsuitable for doctors because of the nature of hospital services and the need for continuous medical care.

The tribunal agreed, finding that emergency duty payments were different from generic public sector overtime because they reflected the specific demands placed on medical officers.

It noted that junior doctors may be required to work 16-hour overnight emergency shifts during weekdays, from 4:00 pm to 8:00 am, as well as 24-hour weekend shifts. Doctors may also be required to cover multiple hospitals and deal with emergencies that cannot be treated as ordinary scheduled overtime.

The tribunal described EDA as a specialised form of overtime pay that takes account of the intensity of doctors’ duties, continuous 16-to-24-hour rotas, cross-coverage and location-based differences.

The JMDA had proposed retaining a multi-tiered emergency duty payment system while reducing the number of existing categories.

The association’s March 15, 2024 cost-reduction proposal grouped the payments into four main areas: rostered duty, covering multiple hospitals, Type C hospitals, and premium rates.

The tribunal accepted that proposal as the basis for its award, with minor adjustments.

Under the new arrangement, the EDA hourly rate is to be calculated using the midpoint of the relevant medical officer salary scale.

For rostered emergency duty, doctors are to receive 1.5 times the applicable hourly rate for a normal weekday, 1.75 times the rate for the first day off, and twice the rate for the second day off.

For doctors covering multiple hospitals, the rate is 1.75 times the applicable rate for a normal weekday, twice the rate for the first day off, and 2.25 times the rate for the second day off.

Ward sessional duty is to attract a rate of 25 per cent above the rostered duty rate, while premium duties — including casualty, Type C hospitals, health centres, and cross-coverage — are to attract a rate 50 per cent above the applicable rostered duty rate.

The tribunal ordered that the EDA payments under the new framework be made retroactively from April 1, 2023.

The Government had argued that revised sessional compensation rates should instead take effect from August 1, 2024, when the standardised EHW policy was issued.

The tribunal rejected that date, saying there was “no legal, contractual, or equitable justification” for using August 1, 2024 as the implementation date. It pointed to the March 16, 2023 Memorandum of Understanding between the Government and the JMDA, which required discussions on revised allowance policies by March 31, 2023.

The tribunal also found that the Government had not established that applying the April 1, 2023 date would create the level of financial or administrative disruption claimed.

It noted that other public sector groups, including the University Hospital of the West Indies (UHWI) and the Jamaica Urban Transit Company (JUTC), had received overtime retroactivity dating back to April 2022 without causing a “knockon” effect.

The tribunal also ruled on the incentive allowance, which had been a separate point of disagreement between the parties.

The Government argued that the allowance had been discontinued and absorbed into the restructured basic salaries of medical officers, while the JMDA argued that it had not agreed to the removal of the allowance and that it remained protected by the March 2023 agreement.

The tribunal found that the JMDA’s position was supported by the evidence and concluded that the incentive allowance had survived the signing of the March 16, 2023 agreement. The majority therefore ordered its reinstatement from April 1, 2023.

Eligible non-rostered medical officers, including interns, senior house officers, and medical officers levels 1 to 3 working in emergency and clinical specialties at the Ministry of Health and Wellness’s head office, are to receive an allowance equal to 40 per cent of the midpoint of their respective salary scales.

An allowance of 55 per cent of the midpoint is provided for medical officers levels 2 and 3 serving as medical officers (health), as well as medical officers otherwise eligible under the 2017-2021 heads of agreement.

However, a medical officer who performs rostered emergency duty during a particular calendar month is disqualified from receiving the incentive allowance for that month.

Locke agreed with the EDA decision but issued a minority award arguing that the incentive allowance fell outside the tribunal’s terms of reference and that the tribunal therefore did not have the authority to reinstate it.

The dispute dates back to the March 2023 agreement between the Government and the JMDA, under which the parties settled the restructuring of doctors’ basic salaries, but negotiations on the EDA remained unresolved.

After months of unsuccessful negotiations, the JMDA took industrial action in December 2024. The matter was subsequently referred to the IDT on January 15, 2025.

The tribunal said the parties made written submissions and oral presentations over 53 sittings between April 24, 2025 and April 1, 2026, with evidence from 10 witnesses and 162 exhibits.

The JMDA represents approximately 2,500 public sector medical officers, including locum interns, medical interns, senior house officers and medical officers levels 1 to 3.

World.title: Insurance assurance
World.content:
HENRY… we have heard the concerns raised by the tourism sector and we take them seriously

THE Insurance Association of Jamaica (IAJ) has promised players in the tourism sector that its members are working to resolve some claims and questions surrounding settlement calculations, deductibles, property valuations, and the application of the average clause.

Last week the Jamaica Hotel & Tourist Association (JHTA) reported that a new survey of its members found that six in 10 tourism claims made after Hurricane Melissa last October remain unresolved, and that most operators expect to recover well short of what they lost.

According to JHTA President O’Brian Herron, major players in the insurance sector committed to accelerate the resolution of outstanding Melissa claims, with the objective of settling the vast majority, excluding complex and litigated matters, by the end of September 2026.

“We welcomed that commitment. The evidence from our members shows how far there still is to go,” said Herron.

In a media release over the weekend, the IAJ said it has taken careful note of concerns raised publicly by the JHTA.

“We have heard the concerns raised by the tourism sector and we take them seriously. Questions surrounding the time taken to resolve claims, settlement calculations, deductibles, valuations and the application of policy provisions deserve clear and constructive engagement. Our objective is to work with our members and stakeholders to address these concerns while ensuring that claims are assessed fairly and in accordance with the terms of each policy,” said IAJ President Rosemarie Henry.

She added that the IAJ believes policyholders should understand how their settlements are calculated, how relevant policy provisions are applied and have an appropriate channel through which questions or concerns regarding their individual claims can be addressed.

“The association remains committed to constructive engagement with the tourism sector and other affected policyholder groups as Jamaica continues its recovery from Hurricane Melissa,” said Henry.

The IAJ head pointed out that the Category 5 storm posed an exceptional test for policyholders, insurers, brokers, loss adjusters, reinsurers and the wider Jamaican economy, highlighting important lessons on catastrophe preparedness, claims communication, loss-adjusting capacity, and the timely provision of financial support to affected policyholders.

“Hurricane Melissa tested Jamaica at every level, including our insurance ecosystem. We must carry forward lessons, and the industry has a responsibility to learn from them. Our commitment is to support the completion of outstanding claims, strengthen the experience of policyholders and continue working with our partners to build an insurance sector in which Jamaicans can have confidence, particularly when they need it most,” Henry added.

The IAJ said it will continue working with its member companies, the Financial Services Commission, the Jamaica Insurance Brokers’ Association, the Loss Adjusters’ Association of Jamaica, the JHTA, other policyholder groups and relevant stakeholders to support the completion of outstanding claims and Jamaica’s continuing recovery.

In the meantime, the IAJ reported that its member companies are intensifying efforts to bring remaining claims to resolution, with industry data showing that 90 per cent of motor claims and 77 per cent of Jamaican dollar-denominated claims have been fully settled and paid, while progress has been slower among non-motor and US dollar-denominated claims.

The IAJ said it recognises that outstanding claims continue to place financial and operational pressure on families and businesses working to recover and rebuild. Additionally, greater attention is now being directed towards progressing these matters and strengthening communication with affected policyholders.

“Our responsibility is to ensure that the remaining claims receive the attention they require and that policyholders are kept informed throughout the process. Insurance is fundamentally about being there when people and businesses experience loss, and we understand the importance of delivering on that promise.

“Our members are focused on bringing outstanding matters to resolution and helping policyholders move forward with greater certainty,” said Henry.

The release noted that, as at the end of September 2026, 49 per cent of US dollar-denominated claims and 54 per cent of non-motor claims had been fully settled and paid.

“Transparency is essential as the industry works to complete the remaining Hurricane Melissa claims.

When we report a claim as closed, we mean that all outstanding obligations related to the claim have been paid.

These figures show where progress has been made, but equally important, they identify the areas where greater attention is required.

Our immediate focus is on working with our members to accelerate outstanding claims and move as many as possible through to final settlement and payment,” said IAJ Executive Director Everton McFarlane. The IAJ said it will continue to monitor claims progression with its member companies and will provide further industry updates as claims move towards completion.

“For insurers, the priority now is to work through the remaining claims with the level of attention each case requires and to keep policyholders informed as matters progress. Where additional information is required, an assessment remains outstanding, or there are questions about a settlement, there needs to be clear communication so those issues can be addressed and the claim can move forward.

As an industry, we recognise how important it is for policyholders to have clarity about where they are in the process and what comes next,” said Tammara Glaves-Hucey, chair of the IAJ’s General Insurance Committee.

The IAJ said its member companies have been asked to provide policyholders with up-to-date information on the status of their claims and any information still required; identify a clear point of contact through whom the claim can be progressed; explain the basis of settlement offers, including applicable deductibles, the average clause or other material policy provisions; and provide clear next steps and, where reasonably possible, an expected timeline for completion.

World.title: Fernando Edwards Jamaica’s heroes through fashion
World.content:
Fernando Edwards

WITH National Heroes’ Day approaching on October 19, Jamaican-born film-maker, writer and actor Fernando Edwards is celebrating the country’s seven national heroes through a collection designed to carry their stories beyond the history books.

The founder of Jamroc Dept has unveiled the National Heroes Collection, a three-capsule streetwear release that places Jamaican heritage at the centre of premium fashion.

Paired with his children’s book, The Seven Lights of Jamaica, the project offers two ways of engaging with that history: Adults can wear the stories while children read them.

Born in Clarendon, Edwards traces the inspiration to the stories that surrounded him growing up and a question that emerged when he entered fashion.

“I grew up hearing the stories of our national heroes. When I moved into fashion, I saw luxury brands charging premium prices for heritage that wasn’t mine, and I asked myself why Jamaican heritage wasn’t being honored at that same level,” he told the Jamaica Observer .

His answer is a collection that treats Jamaica’s historical figures with the reverence he believes their contributions deserve.

Each capsule is anchored by a premium heavyweight T-shirt in the brand’s signature washed black, made from 430 GSM fabric.

Released in story order, the pieces are intended to unfold like chapters, moving from Garvey’s vision to the struggles and leadership that helped shape Jamaica.

The first, A Greater Tomorrow, is dedicated entirely to Marcus Garvey. An Africa graphic appears on the front, a full Garvey composition occupies the back, and the sleeves mark his lifespan, 1887 to 1940. Its themes of vision, unity and self-reliance draw on the ideas central to Garvey’s work.

Heroes of Legacy, the second capsule, brings Nanny of the Maroons, Marcus Garvey, Sam Sharpe, and Paul Bogle together in a single archival-style composition. Edwards describes the four figures as pillars of resistance, identity, freedom and legacy. On the back, the brand’s tagline, “Carry the Story Forward”, gives the artwork its continuing purpose.

The third capsule, Foundations of a Nation, honours George William Gordon, Norman Manley and Alexander Bustamante through an exploration of leadership, labour, and nationhood. A restrained insignia introduces the design on the front, while the fuller visual narrative appears on the back.

Hoodies, jerseys, and sweats extend the collection’s washed-black aesthetic, but the three central pieces remain its storytelling foundation.

“The three capsules are the heart of it: Seven heroes, three chapters, one story worn forward,” he said.

With the collection newly launched, Edwards is encouraged by an early response that has been as much about personal connection as clothing.

“I’ve been getting messages and calls from people sharing how the pieces make them feel, which tells me the story is landing the way I intended,” he said.

Pre-orders are being circulated to his e-mail list as he begins building an audience for a project he hopes will reach well beyond Jamaica.

“I want the story of our heroes worn all over the world, not just in Jamaica, but across the entire Diaspora. I want a kid in London or Toronto or Brooklyn to wear one of these pieces and know exactly who Nanny of the Maroons was,” he said.

His longer-term ambition is for Jamroc Dept to become a defining heritage brand for Jamaican culture, with a presence in stores, resorts, and communities wherever Jamaicans are found.

Fashion, however, is one expression of a wider creative practice. Through his company, Irienando Productions, Edwards writes, produces and directs, maintaining the film-making identity that underpins his approach to storytelling.

His psychological thriller Rooted Betrayal is available through his distributor, FilmHub, on platforms including Fawesome, Plex and Stash TV.

The director’s cut is also available on his YouTube channel, @irienandopro.

He is currently in production on the short film HEART BEAT, which he is also developing into a feature. Alongside those screen projects, The Seven Lights of Jamaica provides a younger audience with a companion to the clothing collection’s celebration of national heritage.

For Edwards, the range of formats reflects a vision that has developed over time. He has honoured Jamaica’s heroes in earlier work, but regards this collection as his fullest expression of that commitment so far.

“The idea has always been there. I grew up on these stories in Clarendon, so in a real sense I’ve been conceptualising this my whole life,” he said.

Having reached a point where he feels his platform and craft can support that ambition, his advice is rooted in patience: “Don’t rush the vision. Let it grow with you until you’re ready to carry it properly,” he said.

World.title: Accused push back against prison shoe ban
World.content:
Horizon Adult Remand Centre in St Andrew

TWENTY-THREE of the 25 accused in the ongoing Klansman Gang trial on Monday harnessed the power of the court to press prison officials to relax a recent blanket ban barring visitors from bringing footwear to inmates at Horizon Adult Remand Centre in St Andrew.

The Department of Correctional Services (DCS), in a post on its social media platform on Tuesday, September 15, had advised that bringing footwear for inmates at Horizon had been prohibited with immediate effect. It said this was in order to “safeguard institutional security, maintain safety, and preserve good order within the Horizon Adult Remand Centre (HARC)”.

The DCS said footwear for inmates would be provided through the department’s established procurement process. But the inmates, 23 of whom are housed at the facility, raised concerns last Thursday about the ban which, they said, impacts their ability to properly attire themselves to attend court proceedings for the matter which generally runs from Mondays to Thursdays from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm.

Trial judge, Justice Dale Palmer, on Monday requested the presence of corrections officials after being told that the matter had not been resolved, contrary to indications that the defendants would be exempted. However, attorney John Clarke, who represents defendant Kemar Miller who is housed at the facility, said his client had not benefited from that exemption.

“Those are my instructions, and what is even more concerning too, milord, is that it seems, from what I’ve gathered in terms of that general edict, that that directive which came from the commissioner himself was done essentially to punish persons who are being detained by virtue of some action which may or may not have taken place,” Clarke said in asking the court to use its powers to pull the relevant officers before it to explain.

“It also has engaged the constitution in relation to the dignity of the person whose liberty has been taken, and our Parliament has guaranteed that that dignity will not be taken,” Clarke maintained, adding “this is a problem that should never have taken place”.

“We must be grateful to the court and the Crown for the efforts which have been made in times past, but it’s a bit surprising because the DCS, in the past, has maintained that where attendance was concerned it would not interfere with that,” Clarke said in urging the court to issue a formal order to ensure that the situation would be “sorted out once and for all”.

According to the attorney, similar intervention in other matters by the court has helped resolve issues permanently. Monday afternoon, an acting superintendent of the remand centre, appearing via Zoom, told the trial judge that indications had only come from five of the defendants that they were without footwear when they were asked last Thursday to register.

He said while provisions were made for them get footwear, only one individual reported receiving any. Clarke, however, countered the prison official’s version of the facts, telling the court that the defendants said only five of them had been able to register because at the time the details were being collected, the prison truck which was to take them to the Supreme Court had arrived, preventing others from registering.

The acting superintendent, in the meantime, noting the recent restrictions — which were imposed because of the frequency with which prohibited items were being discovered in shoes — said the measure was not “cast in stone” as far as remandees with ongoing trials are concerned.

“With consultation with the commissioner, he gave permission for the remandees who were not properly attired for court, especially with shoes, to get shoes for court. This was established with the remandees on Thursday. A listing was done and it was sent to the main gate to say that whenever these visitors arrived they were to be considered.

And there is a protocol as it relates to how it is done; it is to be sent straight to the reception area where the remandees are prepared for court in the mornings,” he said.

After hearing the concerns, Justice Palmer said while the need for the security measures was not lost on the court he would be satisfied if a timeframe was established so family members could deliver the necessary items at a convenient time, given that the defendants are away from the prison a minimum four days weekly.

The deputy superintendent said, in consultation with the commissioner, a solution would be arrived at. He, however, noted that on a normal basis court clothing can be delivered, and searched, and processed up to the day before. “This is an issue where I don’t think we should be here discussing clothing for court when time is being wasted,” the prison official stated.

Addressing concerns regarding a dental issue for defendant Jerome Spike and a dietary issue for the accused Kemar Miller, the prison official said “all requests made from the court, we try our best to resolve”.

The matter resumes at 10:00 this morning in the Home Circuit Division of the Supreme Court in downtown Kingston. In June, Justice Palmer ordered medical attention for 11 accused in the trial after a slew of complaints were made about unattended health issues.

The 25 accused, said to comprise the Tesha Millerled faction of the gang, are the second faction of the gang to now be tried by the court.

They are to answer to 16 offences allegedly committed over the span of five years, between August 2017 and November 2022, according to the case being built by the Crown which began in February this year.

World.title: Intense battle between defence, prosecutors  begins in Andre Ruddock murder trial
World.content:
An intense battle between defence attorneys and prosecutors began on Monday over the admissibility of certain documents that could make or break the case against murder accused Andre

Ruddock in relation to bizarre events that unfolded at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, in 2021.

Trial judge Justice Leighton Pusey began hearing the arguments in a voir dire, which is essentially a trial within a trial, to ascertain whether the documents will be accepted or rejected. The voir dire could last up to Wednesday during which time there will be no media coverage as it will be a private session involving the judge, defence lawyers Anthony Williams and Venice Brown, the prosecution, as well as witnesses who had anything to do with the documents. Ruddock is on trial in the Home

Circuit Court in Kingston for murder in relation to the October 17, 2021 killing of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner whose throat was cut, allegedly by Ruddock on instructions from his now-deceased pastor Kevin Smith, during what was said to have been a human sacrifice ritual at the church.

Smith allegedly told Gardener that her blood was unclean and therefore she had to die by having her throat cut. After she told the pastor that she believed he could bring her back to life if she was killed, Ruddock allegedly used a knife to slit her throat.

Two other people were killed at the church that day.

Member Michael Brown was killed after Pastor Smith allegedly ripped a catheter from his body, causing him to bleed out. He, too, allegedly told Smith that he believed the pastor could raise him from the dead. It is alleged that

Brown, who was gravely ill, pleaded to the pastor to save him but the pastor allegedly reminded him that he failed to bring $600,000 to him as was requested on a previous occasion.

Based on the account from witnesses, the pastor contemplated putting his lifeless body inside a chicken coop.

Kevaughn Plummer, the other person who was killed at the church, was shot dead by police after he rushed toward them with a knife. It is alleged that he was acting on the instructions of the pastor who told him to kill the police if they attempted to gain access to the church compound.

In relation to the contentious documents, defence counsel Williams objected to them being admitted into evidence last week, which triggered the voir dire.

Last week, a detective constable testified that he was part of a team that was present when Ruddock allegedly admitted to killing Gardner.

“There was no threat whatsoever. Nothing was promised and no, there was no force,” the detective constable told the court in the presence of the seven-member jury.

“He was willing to say what he had to. He was very cooperative. Yes, it was voluntarily given and yes, I would describe the process as fair,” the detective said, during the examination-in-chief led by prosecutor LaToya Bernard.

According to the detective, two justices of the peace were present during the interview and both of them signed the statement as witnesses.

“The justices of the peace were in the room for all of the process. After he was done, Detective Sergeant Bond invited Ruddock to sign all pages, as well as the justices of the peace. I signed the document as a witness and Detective Sergeant Bond signed that document as well.

“When Andre Ruddock was done telling the story and Detective Sergeant Bond confirmed it, he told him that he would read over what was said to him. I focused the camera on Detective Sergeant

Bond and Andre Ruddock as he spoke and the sergeant wrote it. He was writing on a Jamaica Constabulary Force prescribed form. Detective Sergeant Bond had the form on the table and at the start it was shown to the justices of the peace and Andre Ruddock to show that nothing was previously recorded on it.

“Andre Ruddock looked at the form. He signed the form after giving his name. This was after Detective Sergeant Bond cautioned him and asked him if he wanted to record it or if he wanted to write it himself. He asked Detective Sergeant Bond to write it,” the detective constable testified.

The trial is expected to resume in the presence of jurors on Wednesday.

World.title: For our boys
World.content:
Second-place winner in the Jamaica Constabulary Force category, Constable Jessie Calvin (left) collects the overall winner’s prize on behalf of Constable Jamar McTagart. Making the presentation is Yaniqueka Wallace (right), employee relations officer at Princess Hotels and Resorts in Hanover, while organiser Judith Brown looks on

LUCEA, Hanover — As a guidance counsellor at Rusea’s High School in this parish, Judith Brown has always had an intense passion for encouraging and helping young males become productive members of society.

Therefore, it came as no surprise when she conceived the idea of staging a 5K run/walk to raise funds for high school-leaving boys who need help to pay for tertiary education.

The initiative has been adopted by the Ministry of Education Region 4 leg of the Jamaica Association of Guidance Counsellors in Education (JAGCE), where Brown has served as finance chair for the past three years.

“I always want to do something for the males. Why? I notice you have fewer males going to university and more females,” Brown explained after the second staging of the JAGCE 5K Run/Walk in Hanover on Sunday.

She believes that educational imbalance can create social friction.

“When you’re going into a relationship, you want someone that can meet you halfway… Sometimes even the men get intimidated by the women when they are more advanced than they are,” she said.

Noting that females benefit from numerous social support groups while comparable resources for males are often minimal, Brown has set out to change that dynamic.

“There was a time when men used to stand up and we had to respect them and they were assertive, they were able to manage, they were able to be that father,” Brown said of her efforts to help young men reclaim their footing in society.

She emphasised the need to change the narrative and help men understand and fulfil their role. “Some have lost their purpose and feel there is no hope because of how they are stigmatised and labelled — and that is not good,” stated Brown who said she is happy to see fathers now standing up to their responsibility.

Despite the various hurdles she pointed out, Brown remains fiercely optimistic about the vital role men play.

“They have their faults, just as females have faults… We might bad-talk the males but they are human just like us and they are just as special and unique.

We can’t live without them and sometimes we can’t live with them, but they are special,” added the high school guidance counsellor.

“That is why I want them to understand who they are and to pursue better for themselves and their family, because they have it in them and they can do it — and I’m one woman who is advocating for them,” emphasised Brown.

She described this year’s staging of the 5K run/walk as a major success compared to last year’s inaugural event, which served as a learning curve. Last year’s event raised in the region of $85,000, most of which went toward settling bills and assisting counsellors in attending conferences.

A portion was also set aside to support a needy student at Cornwall College in St James in memory of a guidance counsellor who died suddenly.

This year, however, the focus is squarely on males leaving high school. Brown said her team will determine how many students they can assist from this year’s proceeds, after covering expenses. She is already looking forward to an even more successful event next year.

“I was saying to the Lord, ‘Let us make $1 million,’ but it did not work out because we were looking at some students that we would want to give like $100,000 towards their school fee.

But, as I said, people don’t know us — JAGCE — so well. They were hesitant to come on board,” stated Brown.

She said she has interpreted one expression of interest in sponsoring next year’s event as a sign that they are doing something right. “It’s the teething process and it’s costly but we’re getting there,” assured a confident Brown.

She expressed appreciation for her team members and others who contributed to this year’s successful staging of the event.

Aside from support from a wide range of public and private sector sponsors, Sunday’s event was supported by a delegation from the association’s Region 6 branch in St Catherine.

World.title: Greens promise ‘campaign mode’ and continuity under new leaders
World.content:
But she also made clear that renewal would not mean a fundamental change of political course.

“Obviously it’s a renewed leadership,” Reintke said. “But we are also going to continue the line on engaging and fighting in this house for everything that we can achieve in the next two and a half years.”

Ștefănuță, meanwhile, presented the new leadership as an attempt to broaden the Greens’ appeal beyond their traditional environmental agenda, pointing to younger voters and bread-and-butter economic concerns.

He said the group had chosen to “invest in dynamism” and a leadership that takes seriously concerns such as “the fact that the cost of living is very high” and problems with energy prices and economic stability.

The pitch is a delicate balancing act: present a sense of renewal ahead of the 2029 European election without abandoning a long-held strategy.

Reintke has led the Greens/EFA group since 2022. Ștefănuță has risen rapidly through its ranks since moving from Renew Europe in March 2023. Nine months later, the group elected him as one of its vice-presidents. He went on to become a vice-president of the European Parliament in July 2024.

World.title: Les renforts d’Europol en IA suscitent des inquiétudes sur la protection de la vie privée
World.content:
L’UE a dévoilé cet été un projet visant à opérer une “évolution transformatrice” de l’agence basée à La Haye. Il est question de doubler son budget pour le porter à 3 milliards d’euros, et de lui conférer un rôle actif dans la lutte contre les nouvelles menaces, en lui donnant accès à davantage de données et à des technologies de pointe.

Alors que les développeurs et les responsables politiques débattent de l’opportunité de ralentir le développement des modèles d’IA de pointe, les forces de l’ordre, elles, sont déjà confrontées à des criminels qui utilisent les technologies les plus récentes.

Mais ce projet soulève aussi des questions en matière de gouvernance et protection de la vie privée, suscitant un débat houleux sur l’étendue des pouvoirs dont devraient disposer les forces de l’ordre pour assurer la sécurité des citoyens face à l’IA et grâce à celle-ci.

Wojciech Wiewiórowski, le Contrôleur européen de la protection des données (CEPD), qui veille à ce que l’ensemble des agences et institutions de l’UE respectent les règles en la matière, s’est dit “tout à fait favorable” à l’idée de donner à Europol les moyens d’utiliser des données et de nouveaux outils basés sur l’intelligence artificielle. Mais il “faut qu’il y ait un contrôle”, a-t-il ajouté.

“Quand j’entends parler du renforcement d’Europol, de la modification de son champ d’action et d’investissements vraiment très importants dans l’agence elle-même, je m’en réjouis en tant que citoyen”, a-t-il poursuivi. “Mais je me dois de poser la question : pourquoi il n’y a rien dans la proposition sur la manière de superviser Europol ?”

Plus rapide et à grande échelle

Pour Jürgen Ebner, directeur général adjoint de l’agence, qui a été nommé le mois dernier à sa tête, la lutte contre la criminalité exige aujourd’hui de doter Europol de toutes les capacités offertes par l’intelligence artificielle.

World.title: Britain’s Tories really, really don’t want to team up with Farage. They might still have to.
World.content:
Senior Conservatives at lunches and receptions this week were quick to aim invective and mockery at Reform — privately and sometimes in public, fueled by a row that Braverman triggered last week when she said that, as a British-born woman of British-Asian origin, she was “not an English person.”

“They’re just not our kind of people,” Conservative Leader Kemi Badenoch, the first black leader of a major political party, told the BBC about Reform on Tuesday.

Badenoch’s most senior aides put it even more bluntly. “They’re just nasty people,” said one top Conservative official, granted anonymity to speak frankly. “These people [Reform] have spent two years viciously attacking the exact people they would have to meet about any deal,” said another. “If Kemi and Rob go into a room, what are they going to fucking talk about?”

Badenoch told broadcasters Tuesday that she would rather force a second general election than strike a deal with Reform. That may be the only practical option left to her.

POLITICO spoke to more than a dozen senior Conservative politicians and aides at the party conference. Almost all indicated that a deal with Reform is not only undesirable, but the hostility is now so bad that it would fail if Badenoch ever tried to enact it.

A senior Reform official responded to this story by saying: “Two years of being hammered at the local elections has finally made the Tories crack. Quite clearly they’re obsessed with us whilst their own party crumbles around them. We look forward to consigning them to the dustbin of history.”

World.title: Ireland’s 2027 budget offers tax break to help people invest savings
World.content:
Presenting his 2027 budget, Finance Minister Simon Harris told lawmakers that residents would be able to open Irish Investment Accounts starting in July. He said individuals could use those accounts to invest in stocks, bonds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs), many of which are listed on the Dublin stock exchange, via a list of state-approved banks and brokers.

The first €50,000 in each account would not be taxed, while any balances above that would be charged 1% on the excess amount, he said. This means a fund valued at €100,000, for example, would face an annual tax liability of €500.

Under the plan, most investors would take a few years to grow their accounts to the €50,000 threshold. Annual contributions to each account would be capped at €12,000, Harris said, underscoring the center-right government’s aim to spur investment by middle-class savers, not the wealthy.

This approach, he said, “strikes a balance between encouraging small-scale investment, while ensuring that those with greater means continue to make a fair contribution.”

Investment firms offered a muted welcome, noting that Harris’ regime retained significant disincentives.

“Today was the government’s chance to get Ireland investing, and it has missed it,” said Michael Healy, chief executive of online trading and investment platform IG Consumer.

Healy dismissed Ireland’s plans as “fundamentally flawed,” as they will tax all balances above €50,000, regardless of whether they have recorded any gains that year. “Someone could face a tax bill even when their investments have fallen in value — effectively paying tax on losses,” he said.

World.title: ‘Accidents happen’: French PM defends police after teenagers injured in protests
World.content:
Some 86,000 joined marches outside Paris in the morning, according to the interior ministry. The capital’s demonstration was expected to draw a larger crowd in the afternoon.

The protesters demand more funding and better working conditions in high schools. The movement began in working-class Paris suburbs and has since spread nationwide, becoming a political issue as the campaign for next year’s presidential election heats up.

“I hope we can provide a political response to a very real anxiety among high school students,” Lecornu conceded.

On Monday, a 15-year-old boy in northern France had his hand blown apart by a grenade. The local prosecutor said he could not “say for certain whether the student picked up the grenade or whether it was thrown at him.”

In Tours, a 16-year-old lost an eye after being struck by a projectile that the prosecutor said may have been a sub-lethal riot police weapon.

Boris Vallaud, leader of the center-left Socialist group in parliament, said his lawmakers would introduce legislation addressing the use of sub-lethal weapons, which can cause irreversible harm, during high school protests.

World.title: Greens probe conduct complaint against Deputy Leader Mothin Ali
World.content:
Both were then asked to leave, the Sept. 15 minutes state. The Green Party told the Exchange at the time that it disputed “this incomplete account” of the alleged altercation.

A complaint about Ali was lodged with the Green Party a week later, according to a party official, who was granted anonymity like others in this article to discuss a sensitive matter.

The deputy leader has not been suspended by the party while the allegations are under review. A Green Party spokesperson said: “We do not comment on internal matters.” Ali declined to comment, instead directing POLITICO to the party press office.

The first party official referenced above told POLITICO any decision on whether or not to suspend Ali is expected to take about five weeks, in part due to the Greens’ Brighton conference — which Ali attended — slowing what is normally a shorter process.

The second person familiar with the process, an ally of Ali, said the deputy leader had been “under a lot of pressure” and that the party had failed to support him in the face of attacks.

Ali — one of two Green Party deputy leaders — said in a statement on X last month that he had “been subjected to a sustained series of allegations, complaints, leaks and personal attacks” since standing to become deputy leader, and argued that some of these had been “explicitly racist and Islamophobic.”

World.title: Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI avatar to make deepfake speech
World.content:
Veliaj has been in prison in the coastal city of Durres since early 2025 amid investigations over allegations of corruption and financial crimes. He denies any wrongdoing.

"My hostage situation has been going on for 20 months, and I can only greet you with artificial intelligence,” his avatar says. “I will continue to work even from the cell … I hug you with longing, you and your wonderful children.”

After his arrest and imprisonment, snap elections for Tirana were scheduled last November, but were canceled at the last minute after a Constitutional Court ruling found he could not be dismissed outside of normal democratic processes. Veliaj has delegated duties to several deputy mayors while he is incarcerated, but remains the official mayor of the city until municipal elections take place in the first half of 2027.

This isn't the first time imprisoned politicians have used AI to communicate with the public. In 2023, Pakistan’s jailed former leader Imran Khan used an AI deepfake to urge citizens to vote for his Tehreek-e-Insaf party during elections.

Then in July, an AI-generated avatar of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro appeared at the launch of his son Flavio’s presidential campaign. Bolsonaro is under house arrest and barred from participating in election-related discourse or events.

This is also not the first time Albanian officials have been provocative with AI. In autumn 2025, Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama introduced the country to Diella, the world’s first AI-powered virtual minister, who was officially appointed to the government cabinet and tasked with rooting out corruption in tender and procurement processes.

A few months after the appointment, Diella came under fire when the woman whose likeness was used for her face and voice objected to the use of her image for a ministerial position.

World.title: Police arrest another British man in RAF Fairford investigation
World.content:
Concrete blocks have been installed by the RAF Fairford main gate, in England on Oct. 1, 2026. | David Bown/Getty Images

The arrest is the seventh in connection to the investigation into a security incident at the airbase, which led to the U.S. withdrawing B-1 bombers.

LONDON — A seventh man has been arrested as part of an investigation into the suspected terror plot around the RAF Fairford airbase, Britain’s Counter Terrorism Policing said on Tuesday.

The statement said that a 22-year-old British man was arrested on suspicion of the preparation of terrorist acts under Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006.

This is the seventh arrest in the live investigation into events surrounding a suspected terror plot near the RAF Fairford airbase, which has been used by the United States to conduct defensive strikes against Iran.

World.title: Judo: Japan crowns two new world champions in Baku
World.content:
It’s day three of the 2026 World Championships here in Baku.

 

International Judo Federation President Mr Marius Vizer and CEO of CBH Bank, Mr Simon Benhamou, signed a sponsorship agreement.

And an MOU was signed between the IJF General Treasurer Dr Naser Al Tamimi and the International Police Sports Union Secretary General, Gonzalo Londono

As the National Gymnastics Arena filled, fans were treated to the chance to meet some of their judo heroes, before settling in for another fantastic day of competition.

Current World Champion, Eteri LIPARTELIANI made it to the final once again at -57Kg.

LIPARTELIANI provided some of the highlight throws of the day!

Trying to take the title was Japan’s Akari OMORI. Throughout the prelims, OMORI showed how dangerous she can be in standing and groundwork. Her toughest fight came from teammate Momo TAMAOKI. A huge victory on the road to the final.

In a tense final that entered golden score, OMORI showed her dominance on the ground, successfully turning over and holding down the current world champion to take the title.

When I was fighting, the support for Liparteliani was so loud it was all I could hear. The atmosphere was incredible. I was determined to win, even if it meant disappointing the crowd. OMORI Akari (JPN)

CBH Bank CEO Mr Simon BENHAMOU, Awarded the medals.

At -73KG, TANAKA Ryuga had a tough draw, but after successfully defeating the category’s top seed, a waza-ari score in the semi-final put him in contention for gold.

World number 3, Makhmadbek MAKHMADBEKOV of the UAE already has a World bronze, and today he was hoping to finally take the top spot. A fantastic display of skill and power in the preliminaries made that look possible.

The final was another close battle, with just a single score enough to take the victory.

It was TANAKA who struck the winning blow, an incredible driving ouchi-gari, taking down MAKHMADBEKOV for a yuko score. Two new world champions for Japan, crowned on Day 3!

I think it’s wonderful to see judo spreading not just in Japan, but all around the world. Seeing the crowd cheering for every athlete and being so invested in the matches gives me a lot of energy. Ryuga TANAKA (JPN)

General Treasurer of the International Judo Federation Mr Naser AL TAMIMI awarded the medals.

We’ll see you tomorrow for Day 4.

World.title: UK trial of three Iranians over alleged plot to target Iran dissident journalists
World.content:
Opening the trial the prosecution alleges the three men were Iranian spies, conducting surveillance of journalists at a UK-based Persian news channel critical of the government in Tehran, with the intention of physically harming and intimidating.

 

Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, and Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, went on trial in Woolwich Crown Court on charges of engaging in conduct likely to assist Iran’s foreign intelligence service between August 2024 and March 2025.

Prosecutor Bill Emlyn Jones said people criticize Iran “at their peril” and that Iran International, a London-based satellite channel, had “come under particular attack” for its opposition to Tehran. He reminded jurors that former leader Ayatollah Khomeini ordered the death of Salman Rushdie in 1989 for his novel “The Satanic Verses,” and noted the vicious 2022 stabbing of the author in New York.

The three men have denied the two charges brought against them under Britain's National Security Act.

This new law was passed to give the British authorities additional powers to counter threats posed by foreign states.

'Ultimate aim': expose them to 'serious violence'

The trial of the three men has opened at a time when tensions between Britain and Iran have been rising. Prosecutors say Iran has repeatedly targeted its critics and opponents both inside the country and abroad.

According to reports from the trial the three defendants had investigated at least two journalists working for Iran International, visited addresses linked to them, and taken photographs and video footage in preparation for an attack that Sepehvand was to carry out.

The group is accused of spying on journalists Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, both journalists for Iran International, as well as Jonathan Turner, a founding member of U.K. Lawyers for Israel, crown prosecutor Emlyn Jones said.

He added: "Their ultimate aim was that one of these individuals, and perhaps more than one, should be exposed to serious violence, an act which was undoubtedly in retaliation for their criticism of the Iranian government, and also intended to create fear and to try to silence others."

He told the court that all three defendants have admitted going to the locations and taking images, but they disagree over why they did so.

AP news agency, citing the prosecution case, reports that Javadi-Manesh and Nouri have said they did not know their actions would assist Iranian intelligence, while Sepehvand has admitted he was aware of this but claims he was forced to act "under coercion or threat".

World.title: Swedish Patriot missiles to be sent to Poland to bolster NATO's eastern flank
World.content:
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson announced the decision to take over the tasks currently carried out by the Netherlands. The Swedish regiment will be responsible for protecting the hub from threats coming from the air, including drones and rockets.

 

The Commander of the Swedish air defence regiment, Colonel Sofia Westermark, described the operation as the most complex mission Sweden has undertaken as a NATO member. She stressed that the location is exposed to threats both from the air and from the ground.

The importance of Rzeszów-Jasionka is exceptional. It is one of the key transit hubs for international military and civilian aid to Ukraine. According to the Swedish authorities, around 18,000 tonnes of equipment pass through the airport in Eastern Poland each month. All in all more than 80% of the military donations sent to Ukraine cross Polish territory.

The country's Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz welcomed Sweden’s decision to send Patriot systems to Poland. He also thanked the Netherlands for supporting Poland and NATO’s eastern flank so far.

Sweden steps up its military presence in Poland

The deployment of Patriot systems will be another element in Sweden’s growing commitment to the security of Poland and NATO’s eastern flank. Since the beginning of October, Swedish Gripen fighter jets have been taking part in a NATO mission to protect Polish airspace. Their task also includes helping to safeguard the logistics routes used to transport aid to Ukraine.

Stockholm stresses that increasing its military presence in the region is a response to rising threats to Europe’s security and more frequent violations of NATO countries’ airspace. Sweden, which joined the Alliance in 2024, is gradually stepping up its involvement in NATO operations on the eastern flank.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, left, and Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson shake hands during Thursday’s summit in Harpsund in Flen, Sweden, on 28 November 2024. COPYRIGHT TT NYHETSBYRÅN

One of the most important aspects of these efforts is the protection of infrastructure in Rzeszów-Jasionka. At present, its defence includes, among others, Dutch Patriot systems, the Polish Mała Narew short-range air defence system and iLauncher systems armed with CAMM missiles.

The Swedish mission will thus be another example of NATO countries working together to shield strategic infrastructure on the eastern flank.
