World.title: Iraqi policeman killed in terrorist attack near Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two security sources told Reuters that ISIS terrorists assaulted a federal police post near the northern Iraqi city of Kirkuk on Monday, killing at least one Iraqi federal policeman and injuring four others.

The assailants used semi-automatic machine guns and sniper fire on the federal police unit stationed in Hawija, around 70 kilometers (43 miles) southwest of Kirkuk.

No one immediately claimed responsibility. However, security and army officials indicated ISIS militants, who are still active in the area, were responsible for the attack.

The raid is the first documented assault by ISIS terrorists on Iraqi security forces since US troops withdrew from the country on September 30, terminating the military operation in Iraq.

The United States led the international coalition that aided Iraqi forces in their war against terrorism, including measures to keep the extremist organization from reorganizing.

Washington said that it will continue to offer targeted training and intelligence assistance following the departure, but Iraqi forces would be fully responsible for the country’s security and the suppression of remnants of terrorist groups.

Despite the defeat of the terrorist group over a decade ago, Iraqi security officials told Reuters that the organization still has sleeper cells in the country.

The pullout of the US-led international coalition raised concerns that a security vacuum would allow the terrorist group to recover momentum, with some officials warning that Iraqi security forces would now have to hold the group without the coalition’s military presence.

World.title: Iraq estimates oil price at $58 per barrel in 2027 federal budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government aims to spend 217 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $166 billion) in 2027, assuming an oil price of $58 per barrel, according to parliamentarians familiar with the draft budget.

The measures would result in a fiscal deficit of around 40 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30.6 billion).

Members of the parliamentary finance committee told Reuters that the draft budget anticipates crude oil exports of around four million barrels per day, including shipments from Iraqi Kurdistan.

The Iraqi cabinet is also studying raising the local currency’s exchange rate to between 1,400 and 1,500 Iraqi dinars per US dollar, up from roughly 1,300 now, according to legislators.

Oil exports generate the majority of the Iraqi government’s revenue, accounting for roughly 80 percent of the general budget’s resources.

The US-Israeli military conflict with Iran has disrupted shipping via the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iraq to seek other routes for its crude oil exports.

The Iraqi parliament is about to start official deliberations on the 2027 federal budget.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

World.title: Chinese refiners increase oil imports from Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Chinese independent refiners are swiftly increasing their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives, according to Reuters.

Experts see that the step represents a desperate search for alternatives due to logistical obstacles, rather than a true rebound in Chinese domestic crude demand.

Private refineries in China have historically relied on deeply discounted, sanctioned Iranian oil to optimize their refining margins, previously importing over one million barrels per day. However, the US naval blockade and the higher cost of Russian oil alternatives are two major geopolitical factors that have forced a shift.

A rigorous US blockade linked to the larger crisis involving Iran has trapped at least 50 tankers transporting mostly Iranian petroleum off the Chinese coast, cutting off the refiners’ key supply source.

State-owned Chinese refiners have successfully secured the majority of the available Russian crude oil. As a result of the fierce competition, Russian barrels now command significant premiums of roughly $30 per barrel above Brent, driving smaller independent refiners out.

Refiners have purchased at least 12 million barrels of Iraqi and Qatari oil for October and November delivery, with total estimates ranging from 15 million to 20 million barrels.

Buyers are mostly interested in the sulfur-rich Basrah Medium and Basrah Heavy grades. Independent refiners normally reject these higher grades in favor of lighter Iranian or Russian choices, but they are embracing them since they are readily available.

Major global commodities trading firms such as Vitol Group, Trafigura Group, Mercuria Energy Group, and TotalEnergies SE are facilitating the deals.

This move is being aided by a steady recovery in total exports leaving the Arabian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz, making Middle Eastern options physically available even as regional tensions remain.

World.title: Turkey to turn Iraq’s Development Road into multi-fuel energy corridor
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Turkey intends to develop the planned Development Road from Iraq’s southern ports to Europe into a multi-fuel energy corridor worth $80 billion annually.

According to Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar, this strategic route will go beyond typical freight transit by incorporating crucial infrastructure for oil, natural gas, and power transmission.

In a statement to Anadolu Agency (AA), Bayraktar expressed Turkey’s enthusiasm for building the Development Road not merely as a transport corridor but also as a strategic energy route. This route would be bolstered by the inclusion of oil, natural gas, and electricity transmission lines along its path.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi instructed in July the establishment of a defined structure to finance and implement the strategic project of the Development Road, assuring the start of practical steps within a planned timeline.

In early June, the head of the state-owned General Company for Ports of Iraq (GCPI), Farhan al-Fartousi, said that the planning process for the project and the al-Faw Grand Port has made tremendous progress, with essential operating plans already submitted to the government.

The project will enter the implementation phase following government approval in the coming months, according to al-Fartousi.

The $17 billion project, which will connect the al-Faw Grand Port in southern Iraq to the Turkish border by constructing a railway and road network, is anticipated to transform Iraq into a transit center by cutting the time it takes to travel from Asia to Europe.

In addition to pipelines for energy transportation, the project’s railway will significantly assist in the transportation of commodities, with a first-phase capacity of 3.5 million tons and a second-phase capacity of 7.5 million tons.

By connecting the port city of Basra to Turkey via an overland route, the logistics project will compete with Egypt’s Suez Canal and establish Basra as a gateway to Europe.

In 2024, Turkey formed a council involving Bulgaria, Hungary, and Serbia to arrange the connection of Europe with Iraq’s Development Road.

As a worldwide corridor for commodities and energy transportation, the project is expected to attract international commerce and create considerable employment opportunities and investment possibilities in Iraq and other countries in the region.

World.title: Iraq’s seaborne oil exports jump to 2.57 million bpd in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s crude oil exports rose for the fourth consecutive month in September, growing by over nine percent—equivalent to 218,000 barrels per day—to reach their highest level since the start of the Iran war.

Iraq’s seaborne crude oil exports jumped to 2.57 million barrels per day in September, up from 2.35 million barrels per day in August.

Despite the monthly improvement, Iraqi oil exports in September remained 25 percent lower than the 3.41 million barrels per day recorded during the same month in 2025.

Iraq’s oil exports gradually recovered in September, after hitting a low of 98,000 barrels per day in May.

Iraq’s average crude oil exports plummeted by 52 percent between January and September 2026, to an average of 1.6 million barrels per day, down from 3.34 million barrels per day in the same period in 2025.

The volume of oil exports surpassed three million barrels per day at the beginning of the year before experiencing a major shock due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which caused shipments to collapse to 540,000 barrels per day in March.

Exports continued to fall sharply, reaching historic lows of more than 90 percent in April and May before gradually recovering to 2.57 million barrels per day in September.

World.title: Iraq targets 1M electric vehicles via Green Taxi initiative
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Environment reaffirmed on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, that private sector investment forms the bedrock of its national “Green Taxi” initiative and the phased transition toward deploying one million electric vehicles (EVs).

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Haidar Qasim Al-Darraji, Director General of the General Company for Carbon Economics at the Ministry of Environment, outlined a comprehensive framework to transform Iraq’s transportation grid into an investable, eco-friendly ecosystem.

Al-Darraji emphasized that the green transit transition cannot operate as a conventional state-run enterprise, but rather as an integrated public-private partnership (PPP) bringing together government regulators, commercial banks, private equity investors, energy providers, and automotive innovators.

Under this model, the state will establish statutory and technical codes, streamline the regulatory climate, lay foundational infrastructure, and verify carbon credit baselines. In turn, private industry will handle capital expenditure, vehicle manufacturing, importation, fleet operations, maintenance logistics, and the rollout of solar-powered charging networks.

Inter-agency groundwork is already underway through coordinated channels involving the Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Transport, and the General Company for Private Transport Management. The bodies are evaluating existing municipal transit garages and public transport depots for conversion into EV charging hubs powered by distributed solar photovoltaic systems.

Clarifying the scale of the transition, Al-Darraji noted that the target of one million electric vehicles is a phased, metrics-driven national roadmap rather than an overnight influx. Rollouts will begin via scalable pilot projects across Baghdad before expanding into the provinces.

The strategic objective is to cultivate an integrated domestic industrial value chain around e-mobility—spanning local assembly, maintenance, bank lending, commercial insurance, ride-hailing software, and monetization under sovereign carbon credit mechanisms—thereby curbing state fiscal burdens and generating skilled technical employment.

In tandem with public sustainability policies, regional automotive distributors are expanding their electrified footprints across the domestic market. Ahmed Al-Ani, Branch Director of Toyota Iraq, revealed to INA that Iraq has emerged as a major regional adopter of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), ranking as the second-largest consumer of hybrid cars in the Middle East.

Highlighting consumer demand for green mobility, Al-Ani announced the official domestic market launch of two electrified Toyota flagships: the all-electric bZ4X Touring SUV and the RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV), offering extended electric range and modern efficiency tailored to Iraq’s expanding charging landscape.

World.title: US dollar holds above 160,000 IQD in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar held firm above the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency markets on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, consolidating Monday’s steep gains across trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

The persistent gap between free-market rates and the Central Bank of Iraq’s official peg of 131,000 dinars per $100 continues to hover near 22.5 percent as exchange bureaus navigate heavy cash demand.

Market data showed that exchange bureaus and trading counters in the capital city of Baghdad maintained cash selling rates at 160,500 dinars per $100, while buying bids ticked slightly higher to 160,150 dinars, narrowing the intraday bid-ask spread.

In Erbil, the regional hub of the Kurdistan Region, parallel counters offered greenbacks at 160,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 159,750 dinars. In the southern trade center of Basra, rates rose to match the 160,000 mark, with cash sales quoted at 160,000 dinars per $100 and buying bids settling at 159,500 dinars.

The elevated rates across major cities reflect ongoing liquidity pressures as retail merchants and unbanked importers seek physical foreign currency outside the formal electronic transfer platform. Despite regular market interventions and central bank oversight, speculative buying and regional fiscal uncertainties continue to anchor cash prices above key psychological thresholds.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim attack on Riyadh airport, deny losing territory
World.content:
Sanaa – Yemen’s Houthis claimed an attack on the main airport in the Saudi capital while also denying on Tuesday losing territory to government forces, as fighting intensified.

After declaring a counter-offensive, government forces claimed Monday to have pushed the Houthis out of the Bab al-Mandab area, a key shipping route in the Red Sea, as well as the port city of Mocha, which was captured last month.

Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify with the situation on the ground moving fast and access for journalists difficult.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed on Telegram that the group still held all territory recently seized, including strategic areas along the Red Sea coast.

Their fighters “have full control over all their advances on the ground”, he said.

He said the Houthis had carried out dozens of strikes in the past few hours targeting government forces in Yemen’s Al-Jawf and Marib regions, while also attacking Taiz governorate.

On Monday night, the Houthis said they had struck Riyadh airport and a refinery belonging to Saudi state oil giant Aramco.

Loud explosions rattled the Saudi capital on Monday evening.

On Tuesday Saudi Arabia’s civilian aviation authority said at least three people were also wounded in attacks on Jazan and Najran airports near the Yemen border a day earlier.

Saudi Arabia, the main backer of the Yemeni government, has been providing air support for a counter-offensive launched by government forces.

– ‘Victories on several fronts’ –

Yemen’s government forces claimed late Monday that they had achieved “victories on several fronts”, but military sources with the government nevertheless refrained from officially confirming taking Mocha, only saying they had cut the one supply route to the area.

They also said they expelled the Houthis from several areas in Taiz in the southwest, where fighting has surged in recent days.

Yemen’s government has announced a goal of retaking all Houthi territory — home to most of the country’s population, and much of it held for more than a decade.

Yemen’s civil war flared up again in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the wider Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

The Houthis last month seized control of the entire western coastline of Yemen along the Red Sea in the country’s deadliest fighting in years.

Since then, they have regularly targeted oil and military installations in Saudi Arabia and have declared a maritime blockade on its ships.

Pakistan and Turkey have pledged to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia under a mutual defence pact following weeks of Houthi attacks.

The Yemen conflict has caused a humanitarian crisis. Since the renewed fighting broke out, more than 184,000 people have been displaced from their homes, according to the United Nations.

A spokesman for UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was “deeply concerned by the sharp escalation in fighting”. He condemned “the continued Houthi cross-border attacks” on Saudi Arabia.

World.title: ED unearths bribe racket involving top executives of 40 PSUs, banks & companies
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Enforcement Directorate has unearthed a bribery racket involving top executives of at least 40 public sector undertakings and government banks, besides some corporate houses engaged in siphoning off and laundering hundreds of crores of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds channelled through multiple charities promoted by a class XII dropout, who has been caught impersonating as a medical doctor for close to three decades.

According to ED, the fake doctor, Dharmendra Kumar Chandradev, received CSR donations in his multiple trusts registered for the purpose of laundering money meant for charity and exempted from taxation. These funds were further returned back to the "donor" in cash, after retaining his commission. The racket involved some corporate houses, hospitals, public sector companies and govt banks. Top executives of these PSUs were heavily bribed for releasing CSR funds.

On Oct 1, the central agency carried out searches at eight locations across Maharashtra, Bengal, Gujarat and Delhi-NCR related to these bogus donations cases. The agency seized several pieces of evidence and details of transactions related to PSU executives and corporate hospitals, in addition to Rs 21 lakh in unaccounted cash.

"The CSR mechanism was utilised as a conduit for conversion of accounted funds into unaccounted cash.





Funds amounting to Rs 200 crore have been routed through the above mechanism," ED has estimated through its preliminary investigation.

The agency further said its probe revealed that CSR contributions from corporate houses were "returned substantially in cash" to the contributors after deduction of a small commission.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Searches have also revealed a network of agents and intermediaries who channelled CSR funds to the trusts, which were thereafter routed through shell entities controlled by market operators.

Most of these entities have also been flagged in multiple GST fraud investigations.

"At least 40 PSUs and public sector banks across the country have provided CSR donations to the trusts operated by the accused. Several projects were only partially executed or not executed in proportion to the funds received, while vendor bills were inflated and excess funds routed through bogus or shell entities. Kickbacks and commissions were allegedly paid to intermediaries facilitating the CSR funding," ED said.

World.title: Election Commission: Was ready to meet 240 opposition MPs but not at their chosen venue
World.content:
Till 4 pm, no political party had sought an appointment, EC said

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday, while willing to meet the 240 opposition party MPs at their request conveyed through Delhi Police, declined to do so at their suggested venue of Parliament House annexe, saying the poll panel's protocol required such meetings to be held only on EC premises and based on a request from the parties' authorised representative."EC considered this request as unusual and therefore, it could not be accepted," the panel said in a statement.As an alternative, EC proposed that its most senior officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive a memorandum, "which in itself would have been an unprecedented step", said an EC spokesperson. However, this offer was declined by the MPs.While emphasising that any political party may request for a meeting with EC, which would then schedule a date and time, the commission said it must balance its respect for parliamentary and democratic processes with that for its own protocols and conventions, "which are of utmost importance".EC said during the march by certain political parties towards Nirvachan Sadan, "it was learnt through the media that some MPs wished to meet the commission along with their delegation"."It is clarified that, till 4pm, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with EC," the commission said. EC said around 4pm, information was received from police that a delegation of MPs led by Rahul Gandhi wished to meet and submit a memorandum.Referring to the procedure laid down in 2025 for meetings with political parties, EC said if a delegation wishes to meet, it seeks an appointment through its authorised representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides. "This is a regular practice," EC said.When the panel was considering the proposal, it was informed by the Delhi Police DCP that the meeting was sought to be held with 240 MPs and the proposed venue was the Parliament House annexe, it said. "EC, considering its protocol to meet political parties only on its own premises and its procedure to only schedule such meetings in consultation with the parties' authorised representative, declined the offer," it said.

World.title: Cabinet adopts resolution hailing achievements of PM Modi
World.content:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Picture credit: PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Cabinet on Tuesday adopted a resolution hailing the achievements of Narendra Modi in the last 25 years, first as chief minister of Gujarat and subsequently as PM.I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution marks Modi's uninterrupted public service between Oct 7, 2001 and Oct 7, 2026. The resolution listed decisions taken by Modi which have touched the lives of common man and has given the country confidence. Vaishnaw said Modi's success and long service is a result of people's trust and faith in his style of governance and a vibrant example of the strength of Indian democracy.The resolution highlighted PM's tenure with a list of policy and political mandate he has got in Gujarat and at Centre. It mentioned initiatives from Modi's tenure as Gujarat CM that were adopted and extended at the national level. These included SWAGAT, the grievance-redressal system through which Modi interacted with citizens in Gujarat, and PRAGATI, Centre's platform for reviewing major projects and resolving implementation hurdles.It also cited Gujarat's Jyotigram scheme, which created separate agricultural electricity feeders, as an approach subsequently expanded nationally. The resolution linked Modi's experience of poverty with welfare initiatives, citing 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty.It highlighted women's empowerment, saying nearly 3.5 crore women had become Lakhpati Didis, while Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women's reservation.PM-KISAN transfers exceeding Rs 4 lakh crore and PM-JANMAN for vulnerable tribal groups were also cited.

World.title: CBI raids CM Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, his OSD’s home in graft probe
World.content:
Central forces stand guard as CBI searches Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann's camp office in Chandigarh

After CBI raid in graft probe, Punjab CM claims BJP has started poll preparation

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: CBI registered an FIR against Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mannâs OSD Rajbir Ghuman and five others Tuesday, following it up with raids on eight locations, including the CMâs camp office in Chandigarh.The coordinated search came within hours of the state govt moving Supreme Court against Punjab and Haryana high courtâs order for a CBI probe into EDâs allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through the OSD.The search at Mannâs camp office in House No 50 of Sector 2 started around 6pm, sending shockwaves through the administration. It was at this office that Ghuman used to allegedly meet the co-accused, said CBI sources. A CBI team also visited Ghumanâs home in his village, Gharachon in Sangrur.CBI said the case was registered following a court order that was based on an ED report. The investigation centres on allegations of corruption and abuse of power and political influence. Apart from Ghuman, those named by CBI in the FIR are Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and âunknown public servant(s) and private person(s)â.Nitin is alleged to be a âliaisonâ in the âcash-for-transferâ scandal with access to Ghuman. His brother Jitin was allegedly provided access to CMO through Ghuman and Dr Romi Mahajan, described as an âassociateâ who allegedly worked with Ghuman and helped coordinate appointments. Devinder is an AAP youth activist and Nagra is a âprivate associateâ.CBI searched premises linked to the accused in Chandigarh, Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar and seized laptops, mobile phones and financial documents.The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery, official impropriety, and financial paper trails.Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann responded through a post on X in Punjabi, âBJP has started preparations for Punjab elections. A CBI raid was conducted at my camp office. Now ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab so that Punjab govt and I can be defamed. BJP is in panic as it sees the love received from people.âCBI said the FIR is meant to investigate allegations of corruption against OSD to CM, Rajbir Ghuman, and his associates for âinfluencing and manipulating postings of officers, including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land-related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefitsâ.âIt is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the govt,â said CBI, adding that those named in the FIR include two public servants, middlemen, and associates.ED had conducted searches in Punjab from May 7-10 in a PMLA case and written to the DGP on July 30 to register a case.Advocate Nikhil Saraf filed a PIL in HC, alleging ED had written three letters to the Punjab DGP, seeking registration of an FIR against Ghuman and others, yet Punjab Police didnât do so.On Monday, a division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor heard the PIL and said, âWe are not impressed by the manner in which Punjab Police has acted so far and, therefore, deem it appropriate to entrust investigation to CBI.â

World.title: Jammu and Kashmir: Arms & drugs seized in cross-border smuggling case; 4 held
World.content:
JAMMU: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via drones in the border village of Arnia in Jammu district.

An Italy-made Beretta pistol, two magazines, four live rounds, and over 1kg of narcotics were seized during subsequent searches, police said Tuesday.

On Oct 3, cops manning a checkpoint at Arniaâs Tamala Bridge stopped two men moving on a bike around 10.45pm. One of the men, Rahul Kumar, was found carrying 264g of suspected heroin, a Beretta pistol, two magazines and four live rounds. Another 276g of suspected heroin was seized from the second man, Ajay Kumar Talhar.

Both are residents of Arnia.

During questioning, the accused allegedly confessed their links with Pakistan-based handlers and admitted to having received two air-dropped consignments in the past. Information obtained from the duo led cops to a third suspect, also named Ajay Kumar. He was arrested with 464g of opium resin and 13.3g of heroin, police said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Further probe revealed the involvement of a fourth suspectâJaganpreet Randhawa alias Jaggi, believed to be a forward link in the smuggling nexusâwho was arrested in Punjab.





Arnia PS registered an FIR under relevant sections of the NDPS and Arms Acts. Officials said further investigation was underway.

Many such cases have earlier been reported from forward areas along the Indo-Pak international border and the Line of Control in J&K. The probes were later handed over to NIA due to the magnitude of the smuggled contraband, arms and ammunition.

World.title: Cabinet okays new body to bring roads, rail, ports, aviation under one planning framework
World.content:
The agency will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more (ANI Photo).

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Cabinet on Tuesday approved setting up Indiaâs first integrated transport and logistics authority, giving the new body a mandate to plan, appraise and monitor projects worth over Rs 500 crore across roads, railways, ports, aviation, waterways, urban mobility and logistics.The Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) is aimed at ending fragmented planning across multiple transport ministries and agencies and driving greater coordination and multi-modal integration in infrastructure development. Announcing the decision, I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, âBy fostering greater coordination and multi-modal integration, ITLA is a new institution responsible for prospective planning for infrastructure development in the country. âThe new agency is modelled on similar institutions in the US, UK, Germany, Australia and Japan, and was first reported by TOI in April 2024.Govt said ITLA will also create a unified transport data repository by obtaining relevant transport and logistics datasets from multiple sources, including GSTN e-way bills, FASTag, Vahan, GPS-based systems, urban traffic management systems and other databases. It will undertake data analytics for planning, monitoring and impact assessment.Each transport and logistics-related ministry will have an ITLA division to ensure better coordination and implementation of projects and schemes, officials said.The agency will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more. It will also evaluate five-year sectoral plans and annual plans of transport ministries to ensure consistency with the master plan and promote multi-modal infrastructure development.Vaishnaw said ITLA will coordinate the resolution of inter-ministerial issues and assess the impact of projects after their completion, making post-completion assessment an important part of its mandate.

World.title: Focus must now be on taking digital literacy, financial literacy to every citizen: Uttarakhand CM
World.content:
Dehradun (Uttarakhand) [India], October 6 (ANI):

Pushkar Singh Dhami participated in a programme organised at the Mukhya Sevak Sadan at the Chief Minister's Camp Office on Tuesday to mark Uttarakhand becoming a fully literate state.

On the occasion, the Chief Minister felicitated neo-literates who successfully cleared the examination conducted by the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS).

The Chief Minister said the achievement was the result of the hard work and collective participation of teachers, students, neo-literates, volunteers and everyone associated with the campaign while congratulating the people of Uttarakhand on the state becoming the sixth fully literate state in the country.

He said achieving the goal of full literacy in Uttarakhand, with its challenging geographical terrain and remote areas, reflected the strong determination and collective strength of the people of the state.

The Chief Minister said Uttarakhand had achieved the distinction of becoming a fully literate state under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the ULLAS-Nav Bharat Saaksharta Programme.

"After Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Sikkim, Uttarakhand has become the sixth fully literate state in the country," he said.





He said the achievement would further strengthen the state's resolve to emerge as a leader in education and other sectors.

Congratulating the neo-literates, the Chief Minister said they had demonstrated that there is no age limit for learning and that it is never too late to move forward.

"Education not only instils confidence in individuals but also opens up new opportunities in their lives," he said.

He said literacy is no longer limited to reading, writing or signing one's name.

"In the changing times, awareness of rights and duties, digital and financial literacy, and life skills are also important components of literacy."

The Chief Minister said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, continuous efforts are being made to make education more inclusive and modern across the country. He said that the Prime Minister's vision is to ensure that no person remains deprived of education and an educated person not only transforms their own life but also contributes significantly to the progress of their family, society and nation.

He said the state government was focusing on improving the quality of education as well as the overall development of students.

"Under the Nanda Gaura Yojana, eligible girl students are being provided financial assistance. Virtual classrooms and a central studio are being established in 500 schools across the state to ensure that students in remote areas also have access to quality education. As many as 189 Atal Utkrisht Schools are being operated in the state.

Under the Mukhyamantri Balashray Yojana, free education is being ensured for orphaned children.

Work is also underway to develop modern laboratories in 100 schools each at the high school and intermediate levels," CM Dhami said.

The Chief Minister said the achievement of full literacy should not be viewed as a destination but as a new beginning.

"The focus must now be on taking digital literacy, financial literacy, health awareness and life skills to every citizen.

Continuous efforts will be made to ensure that every citizen of the state keeps pace with changing technology and is able to use it to improve their quality of life," he said.

Education Minister Dhan Singh Rawat said Uttarakhand had achieved the significant milestone of becoming a fully literate state under the leadership of Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami. He said around 25,000 volunteers had made an important contribution to the success of the campaign.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The state has now set a target of achieving 100 per cent literacy over the next six months".

He said the National Education Policy 2020 has set a national target of increasing the Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education to 50 per cent by 2035, and Uttarakhand is moving rapidly towards achieving this target this year itself.

The Education Minister said the state government was committed to ensuring access to education for every child. He added that no school would be closed in a village as long as even a single child in that village is enrolled as a student. (ANI)

World.title: CM Samrat Choudhary reviews Bihar flood situation, seeks damage report
World.content:
Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary ordered authorities to provide a thorough report as soon as possible, after reviewing the state's flood situation and the devastation it caused.

A news release states that BJP national president and MP Nitin Nabin attended the review meeting, which took place in the "Sankalp" auditorium at Lok Sevak Awas.

During the meeting, water resources department secretary Dr Chandrashekhar Singh briefed Choudhary on the causes of the floods and the situation that developed in the state in two phases.

In the first phase, the Ganga, Son, Ghaghra, Kosi and Punpun rivers recorded their highest-ever water levels compared with previous records.

During the second phase, excessive rainfall led to the Gandak River reaching record water levels at four locations. Embankment damage was reported at six locations across West Champaran, Gopalganj and Saran districts.

Santosh Kumar Mall, Principal Secretary of the Disaster Management Department, gave a briefing to the group about the relief and rescue efforts conducted during the floods.

According to Choudhary, this year's extraordinarily high water levels in the Ganga, Gandak, and Son rivers compared to prior years created a major flood situation.





He also identified silt accumulation in riverbeds as one of the major factors contributing to the floods. The Chief Minister noted that Bihar was the first state in the country to formulate a silt policy.

In order to expedite relief, rehabilitation, and necessary development work in affected areas, the chief minister instructed officials to keep a close eye on the current state of rivers and the damage caused by the floods.

He also ordered that a preliminary detailed report on the damage caused by the floods be submitted as soon as possible, according to ANI report.

On October 12, 2026, Choudhary announced that households impacted by the second phase of the floods will get ex-gratia assistance.

Additionally, he instructed the Disaster Management Department to work with all relevant agencies to evaluate the damage caused by the floods and the estimated cost of repair, and to submit the report as soon as possible.

In light of potential issues, officials were also instructed to make the required preparations following the draining of water from flood-affected regions.

Senior officials included Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Agriculture Department Principal Secretary Narmadeshwar Lal, Disaster Management Minister Ratnesh Sada, Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, and Water Resources Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary were present in the meeting.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, October 3, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary gave the Disaster Management Department instructions to guaranty the prompt delivery of relief supplies to flood-affected and inaccessible areas of Saran district, with special air-dropping operations being conducted in cooperation with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Defense.

The Chief Minister's Office reports that 15 Indian Air Force helicopter missions have delivered over 28 tons of food supplies, including more than 5,600 dry ration packages, into flood-affected districts of Saran district.

In accordance with Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's directives, the Disaster Management Department organized the air-dropping operations in collaboration with the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of Defense to guaranty the prompt delivery of vital food supplies to flood-affected and inaccessible areas.

The initiative was aimed at reaching affected areas where road connectivity had been disrupted.

The Disaster Management Department and district administration are continuously monitoring the flood situation, while alternative modes of transportation are being used alongside road routes wherever required.

The administration is working to ensure that essential relief materials and food supplies reach every flood-affected family as quickly as possible.

Pilots and personnel from various Indian Air Force units have been involved in the relief operation.

The air-dropping mission is being conducted under the leadership of Group Captain Anuj Gupta and Wing Commander Vishal Khatri (Gorakhpur), Squadron Leader Rohit Dadarwal, Flight Lieutenant Kunal Kalamkar (Bagdogra) and Flight Lieutenant Rathore Bharat Singh (Bagdogra).
