How well do you know your music trivia? Music streaming service Spotify has unveiled a new mobile feature called Music Quiz that tests fans’ knowledge of over 2,000 artists. It’s rolling out to the US, the UK, Canada, Australia and a handful of other countries from Tuesday.

The shareable quiz, which follows a BTS quiz earlier in the year, features music trivia, album cover art and audio tracks spanning an artist’s music and milestones. Fans can share their scores for each artist’s quiz with friends, like the popular New York Times puzzle Wordle.

There are quizzes for artists including Bad Bunny, Don Toliver, Bruno Mars and Charli xcx.

More from CNET



How to use the Spotify Music Quiz

To find a music quiz, you have to go to the individual artist’s page.

First, make sure your Spotify app is up to date.

Next, play a track from the artist, and a Music Quiz card will pop up in their profile.

The app will then ask a series of questions about the artist and their music, and once you’ve finished, you can share your score on various social media and messaging apps.

Spotify is the world’s largest music streaming service, with over 300 million paid subscribers. It frequently experiments with new ways of engaging its users, including snapshots of your music streaming history, AI-driven personalization options, a Running Mode for your workouts and the popular Wrapped yearly summary.

Tech.title: I’ve Been Testing Kitchen Gear for Years. Here Are 4 Prime Day Deals I’m Texting to Friends
Tech.content:
Amazon’s October Prime sales are a chance to outfit your kitchen with sought-after items without paying full price. With everything more expensive, you’d be wise to take advantage of discounts if you’re hoping to upgrade your coffee maker, air fryer, blender and other helpful cooking equipment.

There’s a lot to parse, with thousands of deals on Amazon and plenty of knock-offs that look tempting but may not be worth it even at a discount. I’ve been testing kitchen gear for years and know how to spot a great kitchen deal through the smoke and mirrors. Of the hundreds I sifted through, these are the four I’d recommend to friends, family or anyone gift shopping for a home cook — established or aspiring.

Vitamix $295 (save $205) Vitamix Propel Series 510 blender Get it now $295 at Amazon Expert Take All Vitamix blenders pack big power, but the Propel Series has a little extra — at least compared to the VX series (formerly called the Explorian). It has 2.2 peak horsepower, so it can handle just about anything you drop inside. Unlike the manual-only VX, the Propel has three built-in automatic programs for smoothies, frozen desserts and hot soups for hands-off blending. It’s also one of the quietest and lightest Vitamix blenders, which makes it feel user-friendly. These blenders aren’t cheap, but as CNET’s Anna Gragert, who uses a 19-year-old Vitamix without issue, can attest, they really last. Bottom Line This is the cheapest we've ever seen the Vitamix Propel 510 drop on Amazon. The powerful blender retails for $500 with an average tag of $433 on Amazon. It's only been down to $300 twice before during flash sales. It comes with a five-year warranty.

Pamela Vachon/CNET $153 (save $27) Ninja Crispi glass-bowl air fryer Get it now $153 at Amazon $153 at Best Buy Expert Take Simply put, this is the best air fryer we’ve tested, and it’s currently at its lowest price ever on Amazon. The Crispi broke the air fryer mold when it launched, with a modular build that’s easier to store and a glass bowl cooking chamber that’s easy to clean and PFAS-free. If you’ve used a nonstick air fryer basket, you know how quickly it accumulates a layer of gunk that’s hard to remove. Not so with the Crispi. As a bonus, the cooking chamber comes with a tight-fitting lid that makes storing leftover food simple and intuitive. The Crispi has as much power as you’ll ever need from an air fryer and features uncomplicated cooking controls. If there is one ding on this model, it’s that the cooking chamber is lower than some we’ve tested, meaning you might struggle to fit a whole chicken or large cut of meat without breaking it down first. For more cooking capacity, try the Ninja Crispi Pro — also on sale for Prime Day. Bottom Line Our favorite air fryer at its lowest price ever on Amazon — what's not to love? The Ninja Crispi has significant advantages over pod-style nonstick air fryers, and thanks to its outsized popularity, it rarely goes on sale.

Technivorm $270 (save $100) Technivorm Moccamaster KBGV coffee maker Get it now $270 at Crate & Barrel Expert Take The Dutch coffee maker company Technivorm has sold exceptional brewers for decades, earning it cult status among coffee snobs. The KBGV drip coffee machine has clean lines and sharp angles that give off both a vintage and laboratory feel. Retro design aside, in our testing, this brewer consistently delivers perfectly balanced coffee, heating water up to a precise temperature as it hits the grounds. Bottom Line Technivorm's brewers often sell for $400, so snatching up one of its most popular models for $270 is a no-brainer if you were already planning to upgrade your home setup. The KBGV is currently listed for $366 on Amazon and seldom drops below $300.

Ninja/CNET $88 (save $42) Ninja Blendboss personal blender Get it now $88 at Amazon Expert Take The BlendBoss is the latest addition to Ninja’s blender lineup, and it quickly became our top pick. When we tested it against several others, we found it pulverized ice into snow in 15 seconds — as fast as any — and made quick work of turning dense frozen fruit into healthy smoothies. The blender comes in a range of colors — great for gifting — and has a quirky design unlike any other personal blender I’ve seen. Bottom Line This is one of few times the BlendBoss has been discounted since it launched earlier this year. The small and powerful blender typically sells for $130 but it's down to $88 for Prime Day.

What’s the single best kitchen deal?

That largely depends on your kitchen needs. For me, the powerful Vitamix Propel 510 for $295 is simply one of the best prices we’ve seen on any of the brand’s iconic blenders in some time. I fully expect that deal to expire or sell out long before Prime Day ends.



More from CNET

Is Prime Day a good time to buy kitchen gadgets?

Absolutely. The kitchen category really pops off during Prime Day sales, and we’re seeing discounts of 40% to 60% on some of our favorite gear, making them easy to recommend right now. The next opportunity to save big will be Black Friday, but price hikes can happen at any time, so there’s no guarantee we’ll see deals as good as today’s again.

Tech.title: Are the Early Holiday Sales Full of Fake Discounts? What to Know Before Shopping This Week
Tech.content:
Early holiday sales are here, even though the holidays are a couple of months away.

Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart are just a few of the stores offering discounts and limited-time deals on popular gifts like tech, kitchen gadgets and toys. Is now the time to buy your holiday must-haves at a steep discount, or are retailers inflating the original price, tacking on a flashing sale badge and fooling you with a fake discount? Here’s what our shopping expert thinks.

Yes, early holiday sales are worth it

You may seem excited about getting a good deal on a laptop or headphones, but some retailers have a way of making the deal look enticing, even though it’s not. And some US adults are getting hip to that. CNET’s latest holiday shopping survey found that US adults are prepared for holiday shopping frustrations like fake or misleading discounts (43%) and inflated baseline costs (35%). Other shopping pains include deals selling out instantly (39%) and higher prices for outdated tech (33%).

More from CNET

James Bricknell, CNET’s managing editor for deals, broke down how some retailers may try to show a deep discount that isn’t quite true — also known as inflating baseline or original prices.

“Often, retailers will not inflate the price per se, but will inflate the recommended retail price to suggest the product sells for more than it does,” said Bricknell. “This makes the discount feel larger, when it may only be 5% or 10% off.”

But that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t ignore holiday sales. It could be one way to save on a new device you’re considering, like a laptop or headphones — even if it’s not a deep discount. While some savings may be only 10 or 20%, they could still help shave off some of the cost and avoid paying full price.

But with some retailers adjusting prices to falsify savings, how do you really know you’re getting a deal?

How to spot a good deal during holiday sales

Typically, early holiday sales yield savings on tech but you’ll need to create a plan and do some research before the sales start.

Over the years, CNET has done the work to determine if sales are worth it and shared the best deals on popular tech items. We use several data sources to see when a product is truly on sale, compare the new price with a 90-day average, and share them during big sales, along with expert insight on some of the most popular gadgets to help you shop confidently.

You can take some of the same steps as our deals team by comparing prices across retailers to find the biggest savings.

“Don’t assume the first place you see has the best sale; shop around to make sure the sale price seems legit,” Bricknell said.

If you’re worried about secretly higher prices, Bricknell recommends checking the brand’s official website for the base price. Once you find a good deal, use a price tracker like CamelCamelCamel or Keepa to see historical pricing and determine whether it’s worth buying now or waiting.

Chrome’s Shopping Insights browser extension lets you bookmark a page and track a price. Google says that trackable products are saved to your Shopping list folder by default, too. And now Safari’s Notify Me tool is a built-in tool that can track webpage changes, including price drops. CNET also has a price comparison extension, though it’s probably faster to find what you want through our big roundups of deals during sales.

Bricknell added that if a deal seems too good to be true, it probably is. “A deep discount of 50% or 75% on something that normally costs hundreds is something to be wary of.”
